title: Coach LaFleur Press Conference 8.20.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: What's it mean just to have him back and what's kind of the timeline now to get him fully going? >> Um the second one is you know we're going to take that one day at a time. Obviously it's just uh again the human element like a lot of work was put in um first and foremost by him and then a lot of people behind the scenes to get to this point. So happy for him. He's had a smile on his face. We've known this day was coming for some time now and uh you know it's time for the next step. >> With the other two guys on PUP, Tip and Josh, do you still expect them to to be ready for week one? >> Uh not no with Tip um but you know it's again he's progressing. Uh there's just conversations and then uh Josh is looking good. >> Where is Where is Tip at and what do you think like he can >> I I it's it's hard to tell. I mean it's it's again it's just day day to day. He's putting in a ton of work as well. Um you know so that's just that's just day to day. He's a He's a large man too right and putting a lot of force in that. So um you know like there's there's the good days and there's the there's the not as good days but uh putting in a lot of work but uh we'll we'll we'll see. >> With >> [snorts] >> With With Tip how do you balance the we don't we want him back but we if we keep him on PUP or put him on the PUP he's there he has to miss the first four weeks compared to taking him off >> Yeah I mean that's those are the tough decisions you know and you lean on the player to to speak truth as well and and and trust these guys. Tip Tip is made of all the right stuff. So Tip's going to keep it real with us and uh you know but those are the decisions that have to be made for the reasons that you're saying. >> It's Saturday and you have your announcement Thursday on the starters and it's Thursday >> Is it Thursday already? >> Uh what what's the plan for starters for this week? >> Yeah I'll I'll kind of say it like this um Jacoby will not be playing. So um and and you know following suit with the the offensive line and stuff like that. So uh I don't want to say that all quote unquote starters cuz we don't have our starters yet per se. I mean obviously I'm not going to sit here and say we don't know who's going to be our left tackle and who's going to be our you know our center and stuff like that, but uh um it's not like 22 guys are going to be sitting out. There's going to be guys that are going to be out there on day one that are going to be starters that will be playing in this game, but Jacoby will not. >> Gardner will be starting, and we'll you know we'll take it from there. Probably probably a half a ball for Gardner if not getting into the third quarter just depending on the flow of the game. >> Will Will Carson be ready to go for this? >> Uh most likely no. Um he is going to throw today after practice. Um you know he's feeling feeling better, but most likely no. >> Is that a fair like it seemed like last week he was he was mostly doing it cuz he was playing in the 11 on 11 drills when you all when you guys were still at temp Glendale it seemed like it kind of got worse like you said talking to Matt, and then now it's back on the upswing. Is that Is that kind of >> I'd say that's that's fair. Yeah. I mean those I've had that happen to me. Now don't let me lose you guys. I was in a Division III game where you know the next day or really three or four days later it it felt way worse, you know, so but he's feeling better. He's putting in a lot of work obviously behind the scenes as well. You know, and we'll kind of take it from there. >> With Garrett last year he was used both inside and outside. The year before that was just solely in that nickel spot. Is the plan for him to return to both inside the slot and playing outside corner? >> Uh we'll do what we see is necessary you know depending on where this thing kind of goes, but right now the the plan is to play him inside. Um you know, in in 24 when when he got here it was I know from our vantage point in LA it was like damn they got another good one. You know, and he does some really good stuff on the inside not that he can't on the outside, but that's where we'll start him. >> How important is secondary do you think Williams is just like you said his ability to play inside outside even some safety too. That takes a lot for a guy to handle that both physically and like mentally. Like he's got to be made up of the >> Yeah, it's it's really no different from a receiver that plays in inside the numbers inside the alleys inside the paint. I mean you got to be able to muck it up. You got to mix it up. You got to be physical. It's it's a it's a different game than it than it used to be in there. So, um he's got the size, he's got the want to, he's got the he's got the smarts. Um he's a good player and we're excited to have him back. >> There were some reports that that Wyatt Allen Williams is one of the guys who who's granted a fifth year in at Ole Miss. Is he going back to college now? >> I figured you were going to ask me this one. And it's a good question. Um I I I'm just being honest. I haven't spent two cents with that as of now. I just know that he's done a good job, you know, for us so far. So, um this is this is going to be wild how all this plays out. Uh and again, I when did this all come out? Like 24 hours ago something like that? And I heard there's other guys on other clubs and stuff like that. So, um you know, not not too sure. And I know that Jacoby's not going to get another year of eligibility. He'll be a he'll be with us along with Trey and all those guys. So, >> Do you think the way college football is going, I wouldn't make any promises. >> There's truth in that. >> Did you expect it 12 years ago when you got into the NFL that you'd have a guys potentially going back to college from your from your preseason rosters? >> No, it's a it's a whole different world in that game right now, so as we know.

title: Cody Simon Press Conference 8.20.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: When you When you get into preseason games at this point, I mean obviously you've been through one preseason already. Is it Is it different for you? Do you approach these preseason games differently now than you used to? >> Yeah, I think every year is its own kind of story, but I think being the second year in the system it's definitely a little bit better and easier to prepare. You kind of know the little things better and you're not worried about every little small little detail about every little thing. You're not overthinking things, so definitely being the second year in the system it it's it's been nice and but I've still hitting all the details as hard as possible and and just trying to make sure I'm on top of everything I can be and then just contributing for the team as as much as possible. >> Last year during the preseason split during the preseason slate you played like 40 to 50% of the snaps in each of the games and then when you when you slid into the role you did last year, how did those preseason snaps kind of benefit you or set you up for success once you were slid in? >> I mean I think they're super important. I mean that was that was the first time you really get action and at the next level and you know it feels like you're kind of drinking through a fire hose, but I think that really allowed me to to get a little bit more comfortable and obviously nothing's perfect, but that definitely gave me the confidence to be able to even go out there and play in the regular season and and really make an impact, but I think that gave my coaches a little bit more confidence in me and just trying to build make sure I can do my job and do it at at the level they needed to be at. >> Nick has talked about how you're reading the game faster now than you were as a rookie. What What What are you seeing out there that maybe you weren't seeing 12 months ago or 9 months ago? >> Yeah, I think there's always there's different levels to to the knowledge of football I think and I think when you're a rookie you're you're trying to master the 101 and you're trying to make sure you can get the the the basics down and understand the game at a at a certain level, but then once you once you start getting more reps and more more opportunities then you need to be able to understand the the 202s and the 303s like to be able to really make an impact and and I think that's the process right now for me is just being able to to see the the game within the game and and try to be able to predict plays or just be ready for plays that maybe you didn't see the year before. So, it's all just about about the the room and how we see things and just be able to react and and anticipate plays. >> With the way this defense has been looked at, like how do you guys feel like you're gelling at this point considering what everybody thinks could or couldn't happen with this this group? >> Yeah, I mean I for me I I think I think the world of our defense. I don't really know what has been said. I think we we do a good job of ignoring the noise, but for us it's just every day just trying to get better. And I think that's our our biggest challenge is is be better than we were before and you know, I think that's what everybody in the league is doing right now. Just try to find the inch to to to play better, to be more cohesive. I think we have a really good unit and you know, I'm just really excited for for when when the the season starts and and how we can all play together well and um you know, it's you just never know until you know, but I'm excited for our team. >> How do you how do you kind of look at when Jack was in [clears throat] here the other day and he basically said, "Yeah, I know everybody thinks that Cody and I are competing and we are, but it's not really like that." Kind of how do you how do you describe what's that like that how you work with Jack and and Cody? >> Jack Jack is a he's incredible. I mean, we call him Gibby, but it he he is one of the smartest players I've ever been been around and he is elevating our entire defense and and I bet you if you ask anybody on our team that they'd say the same thing. He's he's really another coach on the field and you know, for for our room specifically, he's getting us all better and like I said, it's for us we're all trying to get better. Like that's the the main goal of camp, and really the season. Like, every day is its own challenge. So, I I'd agree with him. I don't look at it as as competing. We're just trying to get better as a as a group, as a unit, as a defense. And he is a catalyst for that, really. And and I'm excited for him on the field, too. And um he's going to be a big a big part of our defense. >> You You last year you were talking about learning while getting thrown into the fire, especially in that green dot spot. When you look back on this previous season, was there a point where you could point to and say, like, all right, this was the time I think I kind of found my voice in that role? >> I mean, a a specific moment, I I couldn't I couldn't really tell you, but I think I think where it comes from that is just the reps. It's every day in practice, being able to do it, and and guys seeing you do it, and um just getting more confident in those roles. At nothing At no point was I perfect last year. At no point was it was it the standard of what I really wanted it to be, but you know, that's the that's the the point the point of football is just trying to get back up and keep going harder and and and getting better as you do it. And I think um that's my my goal this year is to how do I keep elevating? How do I keep finding my voice? How do I keep making plays that the team needs? And and if I can keep doing that, I think that's better for our team as a whole.

title: Budda Baker Press Conference 8.20.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: So, have you ever given any thought to the fact that a teammate of yours in the NFL might end up playing college that season? >> Yeah. Yeah. I mean, I I heard about that. So, uh yeah, we were joking about it a little bit in the uh in the DB room. Um that's that's cool. You know, it's hard to comment on it, you know. I've just never heard of that. But, uh that that's definitely something cool that he has a you know, possibility of doing. big news with Garrett Williams being activated off pup. What does that just add back to your secondary and talk about his journey back? >> Yeah, definitely excited to get Garrett back. Um, you know, like you said, uh, he he brings a lot of, um, knowledge and just great, you know, always there in the right spot, always doing his job at a high level. Um, definitely special to get him back practicing with us. Uh, of course they'll they'll take it easy on him, but um, definitely just to see him come back from that, it's uh, definitely something very special and um, just excited to have them in our, you know, doing our DB work and stuff like that. So, yeah, >> there's been some uh, stories over the last couple days about joint practices and how they've gotten, you know, a bunch of fights and, you know, all that stuff. What how do you like joint practices? Do you you know what what are what what are the pros and cons I guess of them? >> Yeah, I love joint practices. Just being able to um you know playing our defense, playing our style of uh you know play verse another team is definitely it's kind of like a preseason game. Um I like it. Uh I don't I don't really see the cons of it. Yeah, the cons are fighting, but um you know at the end of the day we're professionals. Yeah, that might possibly happen, but you know nine times out of 10 it shouldn't happen. um however many times [snorts] we've joined practice, we haven't had any fights. So, um as long as you can play the game at a, you know, high level and respect the other team, um that's you know, fights won't happen. >> I was about to say, what is the etiquette of a [clears throat] practice? You know, do you can you go 100% or like, you know what I mean? Is it exactly like a game or is it a practice? It's the same etiquette as if if we're, you know, practicing against our own teammates, you know, uh, if the ball's in the air and you're in a you see the receiver in a compromising position and I'm coming downhill on the ball, I'm not going to hit him. I'm going to, you know, let him catch it and tap off. I might talk my little and say, you know, you probably wouldn't have caught that. But other than that, you know, it's, you know, you're being a professional. Um, so you wouldn't want to hurt your own teammates. You don't want to hurt uh the opposing team in a practice. >> Is that when the the fights usually happen is when kind of a breach of that etiquette? >> Yeah, exactly. Breach of that etiquette happens or if anyone gets close to the QB. Um that's a big thing as well. You should never get uh close to the QB. You know, we get yelled at from getting close to Jacobe. If you know, we're playing freaking the the Packers next week. If we get close to love, like I'm going to expect the the offensive line to want to want to fight because quarterbacks are huge the most important position in football. So, losing a quarterback in a practice on another team, that is something where fights will definitely happen. >> You like playing, you said you like being in the joint practices. Is it ever hard knowing that you can't ever really host one? You're always going to have to go someplace because of the weather here. Yeah, I mean I I I like going to other people's, you know, practices and uh you know, kind of seeing their facilities and seeing the way that where they go to work. Um like you said, you know, teams would never want to come to Arizona cuz it's too hot out here. Um guys wouldn't be able to practice from other teams out here because it's so hot. Uh so yeah, it's definitely cool to to go whoever, you know, I've had many joint practices, you know, Denver, Minnesota, you know, uh Tennessee, uh you know, just going to those places and, >> you know, seeing a different scenery is is something cool as well. >> You and Drew like to go at it with each other and you were part of his Madden 999 video. What would you say to him being number 13 on the top 100? Yeah, I actually didn't know that until I think um someone told me um he was 13. Uh so I haven't really talked to him about it yet. You know, we just got done playing ping pong, I put uh you know, we call it No, I'm not going to say it, but uh I won the game. So it it was it was uh next time you guys see Trey, ask him who's who's a better ping pong player. >> What do you like about Coach Laflur so far this whole off season, first year in his messaging, how he's instilled [clears throat] the program here? You've been through a lot of different changes here. >> Yeah, just uh the the detailed version of what he wants and how he wants the offense to operate. Um a lot of things don't start with skill. It starts with uh your mind, your mental um just yourself being able to, you know, align in appropriate positions. Um motioning and all that stuff. He spends more time on doing that than the actual play. So, I can respect that a lot as a, you know, as a player and just learning the the the way the offense is. Um, he talks in team meetings on, you know, how offenses certain players are supposed to operate and how they're supposed to be doing these certain intricate detailed things. And, uh, for me as a defensive player to hear him and to understand, oh, that that's why they do this versus that. Uh, it's it's definitely something that is going to make me better as a defensive player. And um I think our offense is going to be operating at a high level, but also just the operation I think is going to be, you know, um shall I say just a lot better. >> How's his his presence in front of the room is pretty strong. >> Yeah. Yeah. Very strong presence. Um the way he talks, um you know, you can hear him. He's he's he's lively self. Um he's, you know, authentic, just who who he really is. It's definitely uh something cool to see as a as a player to know that as your coach. >> So many guys have talked about how ping pong has been another outlet for them to be competitive. >> Yeah. >> Why is sharpening your competitiveness so with that so important when you guys are professional football players for a living? Like you're you're you're automatically competitive. Like why is that important to do? >> Yeah, it's it's always important to compete. You know, it always it brings some best out of guys um no matter what. you know, like you said, you know, we're competing in pingpong. We know we're going to compete on the field, you know, so there's those conversations you have where it's just like, you know, you always want to win no matter what sport we're playing. You know, rock paper scissors. I rock paper scissors guys on the planes and, you know, I'm trying to beat everyone, you know. So, it's all about that competing factor in this NFL, in this league, because no matter who you're going to play, every team is is really good. You know, you can lose or win versus any team in this league. a team can be, you know, 9 and0 and the other team can be 0 and9 and they can, you know, have a game. Um, so that's the special thing about this sport. Um, it's the, you know, ultimate team sport and just that competing factor will will come on when the game when it's fourth quarter. We're going to remember those times of us competing in, you know, in team meetings or competing in on the in training camp and otaas and in practice and um, we're going to want to win. So that's the big message is, you know, you compete to win to win no matter what. >> Is it the same competitiveness you guys have on the fields or is it is it different because it's not exactly? >> Yeah, I mean, of course it's different. It's it's it's different because of you know, this is our job on the field. Um, it's not my job to beat anyone in ping pong, but uh so uh yeah, it's it's it's it's different in that aspect. >> A lot of people have been very complimentary of Bug and just how he's been playing his training camp and going through it. What have you seen from the secondary player? Similar to you, he had to cut his teeth in special teams, but primarily in the secondary, what have you seen? >> Yeah, uh Bug's doing a great job of understanding the defense like like you said, second year in the defense. Um um just a a lightning bolt out there, very fast, very quick twitch, a guy who can get to the football, play all the coverages, um and uh do what you want him to do on on the football field. So, um, continue to work his mental, continue to work his knowledge of the game, and, uh, the sky sky's the limit for Bug, whether that's, you know, defense or special teams. You know, I always talk my little smack with him because my rookie year, I was a I was a special team or all pro. So, uh, you know, I was talking to him last year about, you know, what what he had to do if he could get this much more tackles or make this many plays. And, uh, you know, we have that competing factor as well. So, um, he's definitely a player that's on the up and up and a player who's going to continue to to get better and, um, have lights out plays on game days. >> Coach Austin, TA, you said he's kind of a TA. >> Yeah. Um, kind of in limbo of just kind of like moving around to different position rooms and just given his expertise and and his history as a coach, where have you felt his fingertips either on your game specifically or the defense as a whole so far? Yeah, I mean he he's in there in every single meetings giving little detailed information on every single DB like DBs, corners, linebacker rooms. I mean on the practice field if you see him, he he might with be with the Dlineman one day, then he's with the DBs the next day just taking notes and um just, you know, his knowledge for the game and his ability to help, you know, other coaches and other players, you know, just kind of understand the game of football at a higher level. He's doing a great job. very happy to, you know, to have him here and, um, you know, me and him always talk about our golf games, you know, for the most part. But, uh, he he's a great coach, a great guy who's going to come in there and help help whoever out. Um, he just wants the best for the team and, um, that's that's [clears throat] cool. >> Julian said he can't get into your golf course for what does that take exactly? ah you know we got to we got to play somewhere where we're not going to uh you know be slow you know so I'm not a member anywhere yet but uh right now it's I kind of keep my keep my you know I golf with maybe one or two guys I'm one of those guys I can't I can't wait on the golf course you know so um one day we'll we'll get Dewey out and uh it'll be in the off season for sure so we can you know we can have a little more fun. What do you what have you noticed on the field with Dwey in terms of how you mesh with him? >> Yeah, I mess with Dwey a lot. You know, he's a great great safety. Uh great knowledge of the game. Um you know, guy came in in OTAAS. Uh you know, not really understanding the technique yet, of course, because you know, it's his first year here, but now he's he's playing like a veteran. He's very smart. I love playing with him. He's a real real great guy. um real fiery at times and um that's something that you know I would love you know to have as my other safety um whether that's Dewey Bug or you know Rabbit. So, all those guys are doing a great job. But, uh, Dwey came in, brought some life into the, you know, into the DB room. And, um, you know, he always calls himself the the white safety. You know, the the guy who, uh, you know, is very fiery, covers covers guys, hits guys, has a great time out there, and, uh, it's definitely special when we're on the field together. We're talking, he does great job of communicating, and, um, he's he's doing his job at a high level right now.

title: T.J. Edwards on defense developing chemistry | Press Conference
text: Um, obviously, I think me personally, just working back into things, making sure the whole body is is on track and it's it's feeling really good. So, yeah. >> Do you have a sense of when you can be full go? >> I don't know ex- I don't know exactly, and it's it's more so, um, you know, just the training staff and the coaching staff, just making sure that I'm ramping up the right way. So, um, you know, I personally, I can't have what happened last year's never happened in my career. Um, and [snorts] so, making sure that I'm doing all the right things necessary to kind of ramp up the right way and be smart about this. Um, cuz I'm not [snorts] used to missing anything, so I'm not I'm not letting that happen again. >> Obviously, you guys are facing a pretty tough offense today. Just what are your takeaways from? Seemed like early on they were getting a lot of completions, but then the defense made some adjustments and had some of their moments, too. >> Yeah, I mean, obviously, they're really good offense. Um, saw them last year, too, you know, so we definitely had familiarity of just how they attacked us a little bit last year and kind of, right, what they what they do best. And obviously, they got, um, some guys on the outside, a great quarterback, really good run game, good running back. Um, so we knew it was going to be a really good challenge for us to see kind of where we were at. Um, and I think our main thing we wanted to do today was just compete, like every single rep. We wanted to get takeaways, we wanted to get pressure, energy, um, all those things. And without looking at the tape, you know, there's always going to be stuff we want to clean up, but, um, I thought we did that today. It was It was a lot of fun. Again, you know, going going out with this this team for the first year. There's a lot of good guys, a lot of new guys on it on it too, so, um, it was a lot of fun. Yeah. >> How do you feel like Devin's speed has changed the defense, you know? >> Yeah, I mean, he's he's he's definitely noticeable, right? Just the way he moves and, um, his ability to get to the ball, right? As a as a linebacker, that's that's your job, is to get to the ball, and he's he he does that consistent- consistently. Um, and [snorts] also just a good dude to be around, like a great guy to have in the locker room and, uh, in the linebacker room. Um, when you get to talk to him, he's pretty funny, too, so you'll get a feel for him, but, um, yeah, he he definitely brings that that element to the defense for sure. >> It seems like you guys have been very good at being able to get to the run, diagnosing the run, and and getting, you know, 11 hats to the ball. Is that more of a familiarity with the scheme, or is it more of the speed that was added this off-season? >> Yeah, I mean, I think it's a little bit of both, right? I think uh, year two now in DA's system, you kind of understand how he wants us to play things more, and um, you kind of have a better feeling for what he likes to call, and just what we're trying to get done on each play. Um, so I know for the guys last year that are here this year still, um, it definitely helps having that that familiarity. Um, but yeah, like you said also, we added some some speed and and things like that. And at the end of the day, it's all of us just getting on the same page with what we're trying to do, and I feel like we're we're getting to that a little bit quicker this year. >> DJ, there's two rookies starting in the secondary. Where do you see Malik and and Dylan kind of making the progress, specifically maybe today? >> Yeah. Um, I think Dylan's been a sponge, man. Um, just a guy who's came in and just worked, you know? Uh, he's got all the tools, that all the things that, uh, you know, they were saying about him coming out. And he comes in, and you can see his speed, you can see his physicality. Um, and I'll say the same with Malik, right? You can tell a guy that that likes to be around the football, and can make the plays when they come to him. Um, and now it's kind of what I was just talking about, getting everyone on the same page, and making sure we're all seeing and uh, and saying the right things, man. But they're um, definitely progressing like like we need them to, for sure. >> Do you feel like they're adjusting to NFL speed a little bit quicker? It seems like, you know, Malik playing a position he didn't play in college has really acclimated to being in the nickel spot. >> Yeah, I mean, as a, you know, as a rookie, right? It's one thing to go to camp, and then you go on a preseason game where speed's a little different, and you're going to first regular season game where the speed's a little different. Um, you know, and [snorts] all those things you kind of just got to take as they come, right? So, I think it's on all of us just to make sure that it's not, you know, it's not all on one position group, one guy, to be out there and not really have a feel for it. It's on all of us to be on the same page and and help anyone that needs to be helped, to be honest, cuz we need everybody. And it You saw from from last year, right? Like we need everyone on the defense to be involved and be able to be ready to play at all times. So, um I think that's kind of been our main, you know, effort this year. >> TJ, when you guys get When you get Kyler back, what does Kyler bring to that position that is really difficult to replace? >> Yeah. I I uh I think Kyler's one of the best nickels in the game. I really do. Um I think when he's when he's on the field, he changes the game. And uh you know, he's his ability to blitz, his ability to stop the run, his ability to to cover when needed, play the pass. Um he does it all, right? And I know he's working his butt off and um talk to him every single day, man. He's just itching to get out there. So, um you know, we'll be we'll be ready when he gets back and um we know we know who he is when he's on the field. >> What's the biggest difference in playing next to Devin than it was with Tremaine the last couple of years, outside of size, of course? >> Yeah. Um yeah. Man's larger than life, you know. Um No, I mean, I think I think both guys, really with all of us, I feel like we just understand football, right? And um it's where, you know, I think it's easy to kind of just play next to us with a guy like Bush, where he gets the game, he understands kind of where he's supposed to fit, um what I'm seeing. Um I think it I think it's been seamless, right? And um also big 10 guy, you know, big 10 ball. We just We just get it. So, um but no, it's been it's been great, yeah. >> TJ, with the Jaquan, you've been with him, obviously, since he got in the league. >> Yeah. >> What are you looking forward to seeing how he can maybe take his game to the next level? >> Yeah. Um I think Dex is a is a guy who's come in every single year and just gotten better. And I think he's understood what he can do um when he's playing with technique and doing those things and how how he can take over a game, quite literally. Um so, I think [snorts] his confidence is growing and growing and um we need him to. I think that whole front's been been awesome this year. You can see the work that they've they've putting in and you can see just kind of the steps that they've taken cuz they're they're the engine, you know? They It starts with them up front, and I think, you know, that that group with their leadership with Grady and Taz and and adding guys like Street and Neville, really good for that room, and you can see Dex kind of coming into his own, for sure. >> TJ, to go off that, where do you with Neville, with K'Lavon Chaisson, with Van What do you notice maybe the the difference? Is it speed, quickness, up line? title: Ben Johnson looking forward to joint practice with Bengals | Press Conference
text: All right, man, good start here. It's great for our guys just to get used to our our road routine. So hitting the plane, traveling on out here. We had a good day yesterday getting settled in and and I know they're excited about the opportunity to go against a new opponent. So Zach and I have talked. We're on the same page with what we want this to look like and I think it's going to be really good quality work for both teams here. So I'll open it up from there. >> How do you feel about the Obviously your progress from the beginning of the off-season to where you're at now. I know it's just barely kind of left here lately, but just overall what's that look like for you? >> Yeah, well, I mean I think when we looked at last year with him as a whole, it was this guy's a an asset in the running game. We like how he runs off the ball. He plays with good pad level and body lean and and he's able to to displace defenders. It was the pass pro that was just a little bit behind and so that was really his mission throughout the off-season was to make sure he's in the right body position to where he's not leaning forward in the pass pro. He's still punching with his hands and and uh I think we've seen a guy that's in better positions fundamentally to where he's not lunging and getting beat the way it was a year ago. So we're really encouraged with what that looks like. Um most of those snaps so far have been on the right side and so we want to take a look at at what that's going to be on the left side and and how that translates, but for all these guys that have been here going into the second year now, you can feel them. They're not thinking as much about what we're asking them to do schematically and so they're able to hone in on those fundamentals a little bit more and we've been encouraged with what we've seen from them. >> What have you seen from Beanie Bishop on the practice field? I know he had that gift basket interceptions >> Yeah, yeah, yeah, it's still limited exposure at this point, but you know, you can't you can't overlook ball production which he he had in the game and you know, it's it's good to get them out there and compete. Um we're looking for guys that are sticky on the back end and able to play man coverage for us. And so, that's something that we'll be able to evaluate here today. Uh certainly on on Saturday and and going forward with him. But, he's got as good of an opportunity as anybody. >> What do you appreciate about Joe Burrow? >> Oh, shoot. Um this guy this guy is he's like a surgeon back there. Um from my perspective at least, he's got uh great pocket awareness. Um he can dissect defenses in a hurry. He knows recognizes coverages. He's able to to distribute the ball. Um And then he trusts the guys that he's got on the perimeter as well. We know that the two guys on the outside, they're they're probably the best of duo in the business right now um when you look at it. And so, he gives them a chance to make plays. Um this will be a great test for our defense right now with with where we are and what we're doing coverage wise to face an opponent like that. But, um it's fun to talk to a guy like JT Barrett. He was he was teammates with with Joe at Ohio State. And so, there there's some shared history there. And you know, he speaks very very highly of who Joe is as a person as well. >> And from your perspective, what's the value in these joint practices compared to a preseason game and the way you're able to to structure these to to maximize them? >> Yeah, well I mean they're controlled controlled reps here. Um you know, the emphasis is going to be on our starters. And you know, talking with with Zac, he feels the same way. It's uh they'll get the bulk of the workload here. And and we'll assess where we're at after the practice just in terms of that workload. But, um yeah, it's exciting cuz we know you know, there's ground rules. Stay away from the quarterback. Um you know, we're thudding up and and things of that nature. And so, there's we can just make sure it's safe, it's controlled. Um and yet the competition goes up, the intensity goes up. You can't help, but when you have a new face across from you, you want to go out there and make sure your identity and who you're about what you're everything about shows up on tape. And so, um that's what we're looking for today. We talked about it this morning. We we want to see our style of play transfer and translate even though we're on the road here. >> And on Caleb's throwing accuracy, where is he at relative to your standard for what that needs to be and where do you still need to see a little bit of work? >> Well, it's trending upward and that's that's really what we want to see is uh it continue to get better. Um I thought I just told him this morning, I thought the last 2 days, even though it was abbreviated practice yesterday, they were really good. And so, uh red zone was a big emphasis for us last year. We got a few good reps of that uh yesterday. Um I think he's he's shown significant strides there. He's taken a lot of pride in where he's putting the ball throughout throughout practice. You see it early on in uh our warm-up periods, to routes on air, and it's translating over to the team periods as well. And yet, he still hasn't lost that stinger of being aggressive and trying to push the limits a little bit. And so, I think that's healthy, particularly in practice, just seeing how tight of windows we can fit these things into. Um and there's a there's a good delicate balance and and we're doing uh our normal day off, player day off, meetings and able to assess what we previously put on tape. And you know, that's where I they like yesterday was so good because there's a few things that we talked about uh the last player day off that showed up yesterday that that gets you excited as a coach. And so, he's making significant strides each and every day. >> Coach Taylor said that because you can't hit the quarterback and he really wants to see how like the left tackle does in one-on-one situations. Um Dennis Allen talked about seeing how well the corners could could cover. What is one thing that you're really looking for today in terms of assessing something about the team? >> I I'm looking at special teams today. Um this was a unit that when we went against them a year ago, we we did not perform very well. Um we talked about it in the team meeting earlier this week. It was we we kind of needed it uh with where we were within the season. It was a wake-up call and uh we got hit right in the teeth and I thought we played better the second half of the season on special teams and so um a ton of respect for coach Simmons and and what he's done over the the course of his career. They always have really good units. I know coach Hightower is really excited about this opportunity for us, but uh to me that's that's where my eye is going to be starting here today is watching how how our return units uh operate, um our coverage units. Um they have some explosive returners and and I want to see our long snapper. I want to see Bo put in some some tough situations and how he responds as well. >> What is Tyson's status? >> Tyson's week to week. >> He's week to week. And what Tyreek, is he going to be out there today? >> He's going to yeah, yeah, we'll see the extent of which he practices, but he's going to start. Yeah. >> Did Tyson and Kyle travel with you guys even if they might not play? >> Yeah, no, they did not. >> And then with your corners and safeties going against Burrow and Chase and Higgins, what can you learn about your guys' defense? What can they learn just going against that group today? >> Yeah, well, I mean we it's it's the same thing I talked about. I just want to see our style of play, everything that we've been coaching translate now that we have an opponent. There were times that it happened in the game against Cleveland last week. Um and yet the consistency with which it shows up can can be at a higher clip as well. So, um I think shoot, I think Tez talked about it. Like there's there's some proof in the pudding right now with the guys that were out there on Saturday when they did it the way that we wanted, they had some results from it and so um that's what you want to see up front. You want to see us come off and strike blocks uh the way that we been doing, not not lose our minds now that we got a different opponent out there or uh it looks a little bit different. And then yeah, on the back end like we we need to see stickiness in coverage. We want to see be able to stay attached and uh and try to make plays on the football. You know, our calling card a year ago was the takeaways. It would be great to get a couple takeaways today. >> It seemed like last year the joint practice was really where Caleb and Drew grew together. What are you hoping to see in this joint practice with Garin and Caleb to get them kind of locked in on the same page? >> Yeah, I just I really what I want to see I want to see alignment assignment pre-snap taken care of. A year ago those joint practices they were they were discombobulated so that's not what we're looking for. I just want to see clean concise what we've been doing over the last couple weeks just see that translate everybody keep their composure throughout throughout practice here and and operate at a high level. >> Last two Kevin and Pat. >> Ben Marcus Davenport in his very brief time in Detroit but what just curious your experience with him and then talking to Deion about the decision to bring him in. >> Yeah, no I think he's going to add some competition to us on the on the edge there. He's still very hungry and motivated individual and we got a plan on how we want him to come back and be able to to help us out. So we're looking to execute that. To me it's it's adding adding some depth there to the defensive end spot and giving him a chance to compete with the guys that we already have. >> Will he practice today? We haven't seen him out on the field yet. >> He's not practicing today. >> And then Caleb has has talked about wanting to get off to a faster start. Is that something that you can watch in a joint practice that and then go okay this may apply to games? >> Yeah, I mean I think anytime anytime you hit the grass that's whatever you emphasize you want to see show up and so yeah we we start off I think today with the seven on seven in the red zone you'd like to see him start off hot there and and we talked about it this morning in the team period we'll work some base downs there when we come together as as a unit and like to see us get off to a fast start also. You know last game that's that that was kind of the the the the part that leaves a bad taste in your mouth even though you win, you know, 34 to 10. Well, you're down 10 to nothing at the end of the first quarter and you have a couple three-and-outs on offense and so um each week you try to pick out a couple things of of room to grow and improve and that'll be our theme here this week is is can we start faster not only in practice but also in the game on Saturday.

text: And similarly, with similarly, with Jaylen obviously the tackle in space and then you come back and you make an interception, that one interception. Like, you've had your ups and downs. They needed to make enough explosive plays to allow the run game, some space to breathe and some space to work and then allow the defense to carry some of that burden as well. I think defensively Brandon Staley has a lot of athleticism to work with, a lot of versatility. Again, talking about Kaden Ellis, particularly up front that in that front seven, they want to be disruptive and multiple rather than simply looking in one look. So, stylistically, I actually think the Saints and the Falcons may have more in common than what you may think. And not just because they a lot of kind of what I just said adheres itself to also kind of describing the Atlanta Falcons, but I think that there's a key difference between where the Saints are and where the Falcons are. The Saints kind of are sitting in this spot where they really do think and believe that they have their quarterback. Now, it's just a matter of how good can Tyler Shuck be and what can he ultimately become with another or with at least a full year under his belt based on what they saw in the final half of the season last year. The Falcons is it's a little bit different where it's like we have a new head coach. We're still figuring out exactly what this offense and quarterback situation will look like. Now, Atlanta has more of established stars in Bjan Robinson, Drake London, Kyle Pittz, while New Orleans is really betting heavily on Shuck's development, and defensively they want to be aggressive. The Falcons still have a lot of things to figure out in terms of pass rush, not having Jaylen Walker for the year, not having James Pierce Jr. for the first eight games of the season. But I think the biggest thing I want to emphasize, and this is where I'll wrap up, is I don't think you can go into the 2026 year and approach the Saints, whether at the beginning of the year or at the end of the year, like they're that 6 and 11 team from last year. I think the second half of 2025 changed the perception you have to have of the New Orleans Saints. And now we're finding out whether the late season surge that the Saints had in 2025 was the the beginning of something real or if it was simply a good month of football where they kind of just caught a little bit of fire. That's where we land on the Saints and we'll learn a lot about them as the season goes on. And obviously a big Monday Night Football bout in week four which is huge. Um I know I'm looking forward to that one. So, thank you guys so much for hanging with me, listening to me yap about the saints, which I know many of us don't really want to hear about, but you know, better to know thy enemy, right? Like, so thank you. We are going to be back shortly with even more podcast. Will is up obviously in joint practices like we just talked about. So, thank you guys for joining us and we will talk to you all real soon.

title: Recapping Ravens' Joint Practices | Baltimore Ravens Final Drive
text: A great week of work has wrapped up here in Minnesota after two days of joint practices with the Ravens and Vikings. And for veterans like safety Kyle Hamilton, this will be the closest thing they've had to real game snaps this preseason. >> It's awesome. Um facil first off, facilities are crazy. Really nice up here. Fans are nice, good weather, and uh good team, too. It's it's fun practicing against somebody other than yourself and seeing new releases as DBs and new running backs and new quarterbacks and you know it's all going to be for the better going forward. Hopefully learn from the film and both teams get better. That's the goal. >> Both in these joint practices and on the sidelines, these Ravens stars have had the chance to strengthen their relationships with their new play callers. >> I mean obviously the person calling the plays can only do so much. Um you know clocks 40 seconds and cuts off at 15. So, you're really not trying to flood whoever has the dot with with information. Trying to let them go play. And I think they do a great job of that. Just preparing us before we get out here. Um, so he gives us the plays and we just go play freely. It's not like on game day it's our day from Monday to Saturday, whatever, whenever we play. I think that's when the coaches separate from other coaches. But, I mean, on game day, it's our day. So, we go out there, make the plays, and I think they just give us the tools to go do that. And on the opposite side of the ball, running back Derrick Henry talked about building his rapport with Declan Doyle. >> You're just building that relationship, just talking ball with your coach, building that relationship, having fun. Um, that's that's pretty much it. Pretty much it on the sidelines. Um, we know we we know the expectation and um, you know, the standard that Deck wants us to play and we just try to keep working towards that each and every day. The Ravens rookie class shown in their first outing of the preseason and will look to continue to build the trust of the Ravens coaching staff in the second game of the preseason. Quarterbacks Joe Fagano and Austin Reed will continue to duel it out for the number three quarterback spot and Tyler Loop will look to build on his bounceback second half after a miss early in game one. The key coming out of the two days of joint practices in Saturday's preseason action will be growth. Derrick Henry said that an offense is never where you want it to be in week two of the preseason, but this great week of work will go a long way in making sure it's ready come week one. Kickoff is at 1 p.m. Eastern on WB. Go Ravens.
