We heard from head coach Joe Brady of you know, we want to we want to score we want to do this. I don't want to punt in preseason games but preseason games are a way for you to to ramp up and make sure everything is dialed in and buttoned up and when you have a kicker who hasn't kicked an entire season coming back from injury, you want to make sure everything's buttoned up and yesterday based on how we did you want you probably want to see a little bit more out of Tyler Bass and out of the fact that he's repping with a new holder and in Tommy Sweeney. And he didn't even play with Mitch Wishnowsky last year either. Like these are two new players that he's having to work on chemistry with. >> Yeah, that's a good point. I didn't know I forgot that he didn't work with Wishnowsky. He wasn't the kicker. I Bass is an interesting you know, problem in this camp because he's he doesn't have any competition. He's the only kicker. And by the same token, we were talking about earlier Matty, his misses are all the same miss. It's always just outside the right upright. Just outside it. He doesn't he I haven't seen him hook one all camp. I mean it's always he's been money, but before the injury we would go a week and a half without seeing him miss a kick. So he's still I think finding himself a little bit on the technique and I and one last point about this I've made a a statement and I talked to Jeff Rogers and um Hunter West >> Turner West the operation for the kick and the placement is really fast. I'm thinking they're verging on too fast. Um when you start to go too fast, you hurry, you know, you you starting to hurry to get it fast rather than going at the same pace every time. You don't have to be 1.1 1.1 seconds to get it off. You don't have to be that fast and the faster you you know, I mean just that little extra seriously can 1/10 of a second can be the difference between a make or a miss if you're hurrying. So I I think there's a lot in this that are that's contributing and that are have to be considered when you talking about Bass's performances. >> We and we watched him kick yesterday. He was four of six. Just so our listeners know what we're talking about. Um and then punt return Matty has been somewhat interrupted by injury cuz Dante Perez squarely part of that competition and he's missed practice. And now we're wondering, is he going to be able to be up for this game? Let's not forget, too, he had a fumble in the preseason opener. He recovered it, but, you know, ball security is job number one for those guys. And, you know, that's That's an X mark on the resume for him from last week. You know, he'd probably want to redeem himself, but is he going to even be healthy? And then who did we see on the first rep of punt return last week? It was Ray Davis, who's usually just a kick returner. Are they trying to see if he can do a dual role? There's a lot to be decided there. >> It'll be interesting to see what the plan is at punt returner for this preseason game. Ironically enough, I had a longer conversation with Ray Davis coming out of the Wednesday, Tuesday open practice. What day of the week is it? I don't know. And talked about kick returning and just how his mindset has shifted this season. And Davis said, "You know, this offseason I took a long look in the mirror and I looked at the opportunities I was given by this coaching staff, which were the biggest ones on kick return. I was an All-Pro. I want to do that again this year. >> [snorts] >> It was tough to get there and be like, this is what I want to do. I want to be the best kick returner in the NFL because I would also love to have opportunities on offense, but I know this is where I can help out the team the most and this is what I'm dialed in on. So, if he gets another opportunity with punt return, too, I think Davis at this point, year three, is in a good headspace to be a kick returner and or a punt returner and really really dial into that and and commit to that type of craft. >> Him saying that may be the single reason he did get a chance to return punts. He probably went to Jeff Rodgers and said, "Listen, I'm ready to do this for I'm I'm going to throw it in." And Jeff said, "So, you want to do punts, too? Well, let's give you a shot and and Ray's probably more open to it." I That conversation >> Save yourself a roster spot, more importantly. >> That's true if you have a guy that you trust can do that, also. >> And it's they're two different jobs. It's not going to be just like, "Yeah, okay, just stick him in there." It's It's a hard job to do, and punt returning is all about decision-making as much as it is athleticism. But, the the conversation you described that Ray Davis having with himself, that's enormous. Because a lot of young players never have the self-awareness to have that conversation with themselves. >> What am I You go to any kid in high school or college or whatever, what would you You want to play in the NFL? And they go, "I'd do anything to play in the NFL." Well, most of them will mean it, except they won't cover kicks. >> Or they won't return kicks. Or they won't do something other than the position that they've grown up playing. Ray Davis sitting down with himself saying, "Listen, I'm taking the chance I get. I'm going to make this team by any means necessary." >> What more can I do? He's not >> What more can I do? >> And he'll And he's thrown himself into it. A lot of young players, as crazy as it sounds, never do that. And they never open their mind to the opportunities that would be there if they were only open to them. >> And then, when you're playing behind James Cook, it's it's tough to find a way to get on the field when you're behind the leading rusher in the NFL from 2022. >> plays third down for the most part. So, Ray is looking for other avenues to help the football team and make himself useful and valuable uh to the roster. So, it would make sense. Maddie, thanks for the time. We're up against the break, but you can catch Maddie and Steve on the TV broadcast with Andrew Catalon WIVB-TV Channel 4 Saturday at 1:00 p.m. We'll obviously have stuff on the radio side, as well. But, if you're in front of the TV, check them out.

title: Bills at Browns practice and covering Cleveland sports: Sal's House with Daryl Ruiter
text: Hi everybody, welcome to another edition of Sal's house. We are here in Berea, Ohio, about 20-25 minutes outside downtown Cleveland, much like when you go to Orchard Park from Buffalo, where the Bills have their stadium and their practice facility. The practice facility is here in Berea, but the Browns actually play in downtown Cleveland. And today was a joint practice between the Bills and the Browns. They're going to have a preseason game on Saturday. Joining me, my colleague from 92.3 The Fan in Cleveland, Daryl Rider. Thanks for coming on, man. >> You betcha. Thanks for having me in your house. >> Yeah, you I I appreciate that. My house is here in Cleveland this weekend. I'll be in Cleveland all weekend, actually. Um, I love coming to Cleveland. I think it's a great city. You know, for many years people would make fun of Buffalo or Cleveland, Rust Belt cities, it's cold all the time, whatever. People still do. But man, I I've been to Cleveland just to kind of come over to Cleveland with my wife and son, down by the river, down by the stadium, the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. There's a lot to do here. >> Yeah, I've I've lived here for uh 29 years now. I've been working here uh for 29 years. It's a great town, passionate fans that love sports, uh but also very protective of their city. We're allowed to make fun of Cleveland. You, sir, are not allowed to make fun of Cleveland. Those are the rules. We made them up and we follow them. >> And of course, not only do they have, and Daryl follows and covers the Browns, obviously, but you have the Guardians here. I've seen the Yankees play inside a beautiful stadium a few times. I mean, that is a that is a gorgeous stadium. I know it's a little older now. They They That stadium, I'll tell you, my son is 12 now. When we would come here years ago, maybe the best stadium I've ever been in for kids. Um, the the upper deck right field, the kids club for the Guardians. What I don't know what the stadium is called now, you can tell me, but it is they do a great job there. >> Yeah, it's uh Progressive Field. It's been that way uh for a while. Yeah. But no, the kids clubhouse, Slider, one of the more popular mascots in Major League Baseball, right up there with the Philly Phanatic. Uh but yeah, it's um it it's a it is a great ballpark. They've done a good job trying to maintain it and keep it uh alive. A lot of these teams are replacing ballparks after 25 years or so. Uh the Guardians are trying to keep that one alive because I mean a lot of special memories there. I mean that was basically the revitalization of baseball here in Cleveland going all the way back uh to the 1990s. It's hard to believe that it's been 30 plus years since that ballpark not only opened but the then Indians now Guardians really had a renaissance with that 1994 and 19 95 team. They and and just all throughout the 90s were were dominant. They just bludgeoned opponents. They kept running into the Yankees and Red Sox unfortunately but they got to the World Series twice. Um and and they they've they've had some looks over the years and and and look I mean for all the criticism that that organization gets because they don't spend a lot of money. Their owners don't have deep pockets. They they do find ways to compete. It isn't always pretty. They don't always hit. They don't always pitch. But they just seem to find a way come September to be in the race and I think the smartest thing they did back when Major League Baseball had that big realignment there in the 90s was they got out of the American League East. They went to the American League Central. It's a lot easier going against the likes of the Tigers, the White Sox, the Royals, the Twins than having to go up against the Yankees and the Red Sox and the Orioles and even Tampa Bay. The Rays do a great job in the American League East. But yeah, it's it's it's real nice to see that the the Guardians they find a way. It isn't always pretty. It's not always fun. Um they they're it's a scrappy team this year. It's been a scrappy team the last couple of years but they do a really good job when it comes to you know fans and and environment and things like that and I do think it's one of the better ballparks in in in this country to watch a game. >> Still got a month and a half left of baseball before the playoffs but we are turning the corner for the football season. Daryl talked about a new ballpark downtown for the Indians / Guardians and how old that is. Now a new stadium's coming. We're going to talk about that in a little while, but out here in Berea at Cross Cross Country Mortgage Campus. I'm looking at it right there where the Browns hold their practice facility. That's where the Bills and Browns went at it today. So, let's talk about some observations from there. You've been telling me and telling us about this quarterback competition that we are all too familiar with in Buffalo, or at least we were until Josh Allen got to Buffalo. You're still living it here. What is it like on a daily basis watching Shedeur Sanders, watching Deshaun Watson, and tell me a little bit about the reaction from fans and how you go about your daily coverage of the team. >> It it's real tough because neither one, and you saw it today, neither one is a franchise quarterback right now as we have this conversation. Deshaun Watson, obviously we know we know what he went through off the field. A lot of that his own doing. We also know what he's gone through on the field as far as the injuries he has suffered in recent years. Shoulder injury, the double torn Achilles that he suffered that kept him out last year. He's only played 19 games in six years. So, it's kind of unrealistic to expect that he's going to have a whole lot to offer or that he's going to go out there and he's going to light it up. And as we saw today, he didn't light it up. He made some good plays. There there were some some things there, but then there was a lot of oof. I can't believe I just saw that. That's definitely not an NFL caliber throw. Then you have Shedeur Sanders who's in his second year. Last year really didn't have an opportunity to do much. He was throwing to the ball boys because they ran out of wide receivers. He was the fourth quarterback in a four-man quarterback competition that really wasn't a four-man quarterback competition. He didn't get any meaningful reps with the starters until well, he found out he was going to start a game late in the season. And then he started the last seven games. His fan base is is is one of a kind. Very passionate. If you say anything negative, they really come after you, and they get real personal with it, too. And especially with some of the accusations that they they will make. But, you know, my job is to be honest about it. I I'm not I am not blown away by this quarterback competition at all. I wouldn't start either one of them if I had another option, but there isn't another option. This is what they have. So, my philosophy as far as this team goes, I think it's going to be on these young skill players that they have and it's a very good young core starting with Quintin Judkins, the running back Demetric Felton, another running back in their sophomore seasons. They drafted two receivers, Casey Concepcion, Denzel Boston this year, who I think both of those players are going to be electric if you know, everything goes according to plan there. So, they've got a very good nice young nucleus. I didn't even mention Harold Landry Jr. who they got in the draft last year as well. So, they've got a great young offensive nucleus to work with and hopefully those young players can lift the quarterbacks because I for the Browns to be successful this year, I think that's what it's going to be, but you know, I've lost count of the number of quarterback competitions that I have covered. I enjoyed the Baker Mayfield years. If for anything, he started like 54 straight games for the Browns and that was the longest streak since Brian Sipe going back to the 70s and early 80s. >> The first quarterback I ever remember with the Browns was Brian Sipe with Sam Rutigliano as the coach. >> Yeah, so it's been a long time. Here in Cleveland, the frustrating part of it is not only can they not find a franchise quarterback, they can't even find a guy that can play every Sunday before we can even have the conversation about whether or not they're any good or whether they're elite or can be elite. At least with Baker Mayfield we had that conversation and at the time the team did deem no, he can't be elite. He's not going to take us to a Super Bowl or help us contend for a Super Bowl, so we're going to move on and that's why they brought in Deshaun Watson. So, and we all know the trials and tribulations that Baker went through after he left the Browns. Clearly they were not wrong in their thinking. He's he got cut by Carolina, ended up in the Rams, had that little brilliant moment of brilliance. I think it was Thursday night football or whatever where he was there for 24 hours and won a football game. Like that was one of the highlights of his career. He's found a home in Tampa and good for him. Uh I think he's in a perfect division. That's not exactly the AFC North or the AFC East or the NFC North, one of the more tougher conferences, right? It's competitive, don't get me wrong. The Falcons are nothing to sneeze at. The Saints are, you know, not a pushover. >> Now he's going through his own contract situation again. >> Yeah. So, um but yeah, it's it it is, you know, it is challenging every year, it feels like, when you're going into camp, not really knowing who the quarterback is all the time. And um I I just feel now that like and I made this comment to you before we started recording this and I have no problem sharing it with with your audience, but I kind of feel like if the Browns had their version of Josh Allen, I'm not saying they would be Super Bowl contenders, but they they would be contenders. You would absolutely have to take them seriously. So, yeah, it it does make the job interesting. It certainly drives engagement amongst the fans, there's no question about that. But yeah, I if I had a professional dream doing what I'm doing right now, covering the Cleveland Browns, and and I and you know, I have to be objective and I'm not supposed to have a rooting interest, but I have to confess, Sal, I just wish they had a franchise quarterback. I I really do. >> I get it. I mean, it's makes like makes life so much easier. It is the game changer. The Bills might not have the best roster in the AFC. I think the Denver Broncos might have a better roster. I think the Houston Texans might have a better roster, but the Bills have Josh Allen and he's the equalizer and he changes everything there. Look at, you know, what's happening right now in New England, Drake Maye and, you know, him and going into his third year now and where they could be on that timeline with the quarterback. The quarterback just changes everything, we know that. Daryl asked me, doing some work with him a little while ago, what's it like covering Josh Allen? I said, "Well, it's two things. He's amazing, number one, but you just know every week you have a chance to win." I mean, that's what it comes down to. It doesn't mean you're guaranteed every week to win and you're going to be in the contention to win a Super Bowl, at least go to a Super Bowl and that's where the Bills are. Hey, whether it's the Browns or the Bills or anybody, make sure you head to Sports City Pizza Pub, 1407 Niagara Street. Now, we love our pizza and wings in Buffalo. What is the go-to food here in Cleveland? >> Well, there's a lot of everything here in Cleveland. Uh the food scene is top-notch. I am a personal fan of Mabel's BBQ on East 4th. I I love that. My pizza place, and it it's hotly debated here in Cleveland, but I love Angelo's Pizza in Lakewood. Uh they got a good deep dish uh and their sauce, I I'm a sugarholic. Their sauce has just just that sweet tomato sauce is just phenomenal. There's so many great Italian restaurants here in Cleveland. Uh we don't have that kind of time to name them all. Uh but yeah, it's a great uh food scene uh here in Cleveland, Tremont, Ohio City, downtown. You can't go wrong. >> Sports City Pizza Pub, 1407 Niagara Street. Also, thanks to Herbal IQ, a New York State licensed dispensary, 6300 Transit Road. They got a great back room with yoga going on, a lot of different events going on. Check them out. More than just a dispensary. Fans of Buffalo, how about this? You're going to go on a road trip this year. Look at all these trips the Bills uh road trips have. You know what? Uh there it is. Fans of Buffalo, fansofbuffalo.com. Go there. They're going to take care of everything. A charter flight for the fans, hotel accommodations, bus to the game, tailgate, ticket to the game, and get you back home safe. And you can drink and you can party and have a great time. >> That is an amazing amazing road schedule. Miami, Vegas, Houston, the not-so-frozen yet tundra of Green Bay, up to Minnesota, which is a beautiful stadium. >> Denver on Christmas night. >> Oh my goodness. The Rockies on Christmas, and then you get to go to LA. I mean, I don't know how many games you guys are going to win there on that list, but that's that's a tough sled. But boy, that is an elite road schedule this year. >> Yeah, no doubt about it. So, make sure you check them out. That's uh fansofbuffalo.com. Check them out. And want to just make sure I'm getting the right banner there. There we go. Safet Electric, Johnny Safet, my my guy down in the Hudson Valley area. Now, it sounds funny, folks, but if you're a Bills fan, a Buffalo sports fan, down in the Hudson Valley area, you need any problem any problems with your electricity, John's like, "I got you covered down here. I watch Sal. I listen to WGR. I'm all over the Bills games, the Sabres games." 845-744-50 72. Okay, let's get into kind of some more stuff that happened today out at practice because I felt that the Bills were very good on the offensive side and on the defensive side, you do have a guy here that was brought in in the Miles Garrett trade, Jared Verse, who I said to you a little while ago, you knew he was on the field wherever he went. What is the plan for Jared Verse? How do the Browns transition from Miles Garrett to Jared Verse? What's been the fallout of that trade? >> Well, I I I think that the the the transition is very minimal at this point. Look, he's not Miles Garrett. Nobody's Miles Garrett, right? Miles is one of one. And you And it's anytime it's It's pretty difficult trading a first-ballot Hall of Famer. But the timelines just never aligned, you know, Miles is going to be in his 30s here, and this team is not yet ready to contend. He goes to a team that is the proverbial favorite to win the Super Bowl, that's the Los Angeles Rams. But they get back a young player in Jared Verse, who's made a couple of Pro Bowls already. He's a He was the Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2024. You pair him with the 2025 Defensive Rookie of the Year in Carson Swaimer, who we did not get to see today. He's a little nicked up, but they expect him to be back next week. So, good news there for uh where the Browns are concerned. But yeah, uh you get a player like that back um and number three behind uh Micah Parsons and Miles Garrett in uh pressures. He you know, his thing is his finishing, and he's talked a lot about this off-season that that's one of his goals is, "Okay, I can apply pressure. Now, I want to finish. I do want to come away with more sacks." But he he wants to do it within the team concept as well. The thing that I've been most impressed about with Jared Owusu-Koramoah is his leadership. Uh Harold I'm sorry um their their new left tackle their rookie left tackle Spencer Fano that they drafted in the first round. Um you know Dawand Jones early in camp was getting a lot of those one reps and you're sitting there saying well hey you know because you know when you have a young team typically your first round picks they play they win the starting jobs and that was not happening early in camp and then he got into a fight with Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah in the middle of a practice and it was a pretty good fight there were punches thrown. I don't know if it was the most intelligent thing to do when you're wearing a helmet but okay but it was and it woke something up in Fano because then he just started taking it to Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah. And and I think that might have been intentional on Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah to light that fire in him to really get under his skin and force him to react because Fano is a completely different player since that incident if you want to call it an incident. And and and so like that's what Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah is >> I don't know that Myles Garrett would have done that. I don't know that Myles Garrett would have ever picked a fight with a teammate just to kind of you know ignite him or whatever. And and that's not a criticism of Myles but they >> Just different personality. >> Yeah they're just different personalities. Myles is I'm just going to go out and beat your butt. That that's his thing. I just want to win football games you know. Whereas Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah he's going to talk the trash then he's going to sack your quarterback and then he's going to talk more trash cuz he sacked your quarterback or he hit your quarterback or he messed up your play and tackle for loss or you know whatever. Like so his presence as you said it is undeniable and unmissable when he's out there. So I don't think that there's going to be much of a transition other than okay I don't expect Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah to set the NFL record for sacks in a single season. I don't expect him to be a Myles Garrett 2.0 but what I do expect is he's going to be just as disruptive as Myles Garrett. This is his third season so he's still on a rookie contract and I thought that That a brilliant job by Browns executive vice president football operations and GM Andrew Berry. Um he could have easily stockpiled draft picks and gotten three first-round picks and this is some twos and some three whatever, right? He made sure that he got a player that they could build around uh who's in his lower 20s there. They could build this defense around him and he's going to be here for years and years to come. Uh and and whereas Myles Garrett, by the time the Browns get to where fans want most likely Myles Garrett's going to be at the end of his contract and who knows if Myles Garrett wants to keep playing football after that, right? And so I I I really feel like yes, it was tough for Browns fans to swallow the the Browns trading him, but I also think the Browns fans understand they got a very good player in return and where the team was in their team-building process, it ultimately was the right thing to do. >> Speaking of great players, don't forget TSE Buffalo Total Sports Enterprises. They have all your public and private signings. Go to tscbuffalo.com. They're going to be part of Rally on the River at Buffalo Riverworks. I'm going to be there. Bills players are coming in. They're going to be signing for everybody, but you got to go to tscbuffalo.com. Check in check the uh drop-down menu for um Rally on the River or upcoming signings. Find out what's going on. What are the early returns on Todd Monken? You've had so many different coaches here as we had for many years in Buffalo and they each bring something different. It seems like you go to the opposite guy. You go from Rex Ryan to Sean McDermott. Sean McDermott to Joe Brady. What does Todd Monken What does he represent for this organization? >> Uh he's the antithesis of of Kevin Stefanski. Uh you know, very reserved, close to the vest, not going to tell you anything in the press conference. You ask Todd Monken a question, anything except for an injury question, he'll give you the answer. And and he's you know, and I I appreciate that cuz it also helps me do my job better when you ask him about something and he he'll go into detail. Uh you know, we've had a lot of conversation about cadence and pre-snap operation and all all the intricacies of playing the quarterback here >> [snorts] >> Uh uh in camp. So, I was not crazy about the hire. I was very skeptical. I thought maybe he would be a one-and-done type of a situation, but having now been around him through the offseason program, 17 days into training camp, I think he's a really good coach. I see how his players respond to him. I love the fact he'll cuss guys out in the middle of a play. I mean, he you saw that happen once in today's practice, as well. He He does that pretty much on a daily basis. He He is not afraid to if the offense or is not doing something correctly, he's not afraid to blow the thing dead and say, "Hey, you screwed it up. We're going to re-rack this thing. You're going to do it the way I told you to do it, and the way I want it done, or we're just, you know, we're just not going to continue this thing." He has stopped two practices, once because of things got a little too physical earlier this week, and once a week or so ago because the offense couldn't get their act together. And he's like, "I've had it. We're done for the day. I'm not watching this." And so, and he's authentic. And and I think that that is also, you know, been refreshing. He's himself. Whether you like him, don't like him, whatever, he's he just is who he is. He made an interesting comment earlier this week that I I really respected hearing from him. I I forget what it was what he the the question was, but it evolved into him, you know, talking about, "I'm not worried about the next job. I'm 60 years old. It took me this long to get this job. I'm not worried about the next job. I'm going to do this thing my way, the way I think it should be done, and that's and the chips are going to fall where they fall." You know, because a lot of young coaches, and Stefanski's one of them, where you're worried about not, you know, it's not just about having this job. It's like, "Well, if I do eventually lose this job as a head coach, I do want to be a head coach again, and so I need to do things that I can explain in job interviews going forward to get me another head coaching job. And Todd Monken's not worried about any of that kind of stuff. And I think Sal, that there's some there's a little liberation that comes with that. I I look at I don't look at that as a negative. I look at that as a positive. That Monken is just like, you know what? I'm going to do this my way. We're either going to pass or fail on our merits and I'm going to be held accountable for whatever the results are going to be. And whether they fire me this year, the next year, the year after that, at some point they're going to fire me. I don't know when. And so I'm not going to worry about it. I'm just going to do it my way so that when it's all said and done, I look myself in the mirror, I know I did it my way, how I wanted to be done, and I can live with those results. And I just think that there's something refreshing in a league where it's ultra-conservative, it's ultra tight-lipped, and I mean we film practice out here. Like it's been a while since we've been allowed to film 11 on 11 in in in >> Can't get enough of that. >> Right. And so you know, Todd doesn't seem to be worried about like the little stuff. I I I call it majoring in the minor. And he doesn't major in the minor. And I I you know, we'll see how good this football team ultimately ends up being this year, but the one thing you're not going to say about Todd Monken is that you did not get his authentic self. >> Two more things before I let you go. Appreciate Daryl Ruiter's time. He's out here busy covering the Cleveland Browns. We were here at the joint practice today in Berea. Saturday will be a preseason game at 1:00 p.m. We're covering that, of course, at Sal Sports. And you can go to 92.3 the fan. Caught and right or wrong, by the way, on right is right or wrong on Twitter. >> Right or right or wrong fan. >> Right or wrong fan. There you go. Right or wrong >> I'm a company >> Spelled like that. See it on the screen, folks. >> I I'm a company guy. They made me put fan in the handle. >> Oh, yeah. There you go. >> Funny story when I did that. This was back This is our 15th year of 92.3 the fan, our 15th anniversary. Out when they hired me, they said, "Yeah, we need you to could fan in your handle." Within 30 cuz so I did, no problem, and then I went to reserve the right or wrong so no one could steal it. It was like within 30 seconds someone had grabbed it. >> Wow. >> And they tried to turn it into a Swift account. So, I may or may not be in the process of trying to reacquire that handle just so that I can have it back because all my other social media is just at right or wrong. >> Well, you can see the way he spells his name right there and you do it. Okay, two things. Number one, we do we we have a brand new stadium in Buffalo. It's beautiful. It's great. I hope you get a chance to see it coming up sometime soon. >> obstructed seats up. That's all I'm seeing on the social media about all these obstructed seats. >> And you know, there are a few of those and people who maybe feel like it wasn't what they thought they were buying should have them resolved, no doubt. But, I will tell you the great majority people going to that stadium I think you saw the other day are telling you how great it is and I've been in there every step along the way. It's amazing. You're going through it the same thing here. Now, the difference is old Highmark Stadium was 53, 54 years old. This stadium here is 27 years old since the Browns came back in. So, it hasn't It's lived half but you were already building a new stadium. What is the update? Where is it going? I mean, you know, you hear about these Achilles injuries and, you know, how long it takes some of these guys to get back, but you know, it goes back to the work you put in um into it and he's put in tireless work uh to get back and be with his teammates. What have you seen from uh from him over the past season and and over camp? >> Yeah. No, he's done a nice job. Um he's a young player who's continued to develop and grow. I I don't know what level of that you're okay with. What what did you see and and notice from some of the >> It's a little friendly banter. That's how I look at it. Do you think that backup battle is going to take the last two preseason games for you to decide? >> Yeah, I really don't have a timet on that. I'm gonna let that thing play out. Thanks, guys. >> It's crazy, right? >> Grand Park. So long, man. Did you um you feel like this was good progress the last two days? How do you kind of come away from >> Um I think it was definitely great progress um going against a different opponent. So, I think yesterday we kind of struggled with it, but I think today um we made improvements and um got some good yards in the run game and we protected better today also. >> What was your reaction to the addition? I know he's a receiver, you're a tight end, but he's a guy who has quite the resume. >> Um ecstatic. I mean, you just hear rumors all offseason. We don't know what's going to happen and things like that, but um I think he fits into our offense perfect. Um what Frank and Shane and all of them were with him in San Diego and LA and a bunch of the teach tape clips we watch are Keenan Allen. Um running different routes and different things like that. So adding him to the room, it's like all right, we don't got to watch it in a Chargers uniform anymore. We can watch in a coach uniform. >> I heard you and Drew a lot over the last several days just really hyping each other up big blocks and everything. How much do you guys embrace just the physical aspect? >> Um uh we we embrace it a lot. Um Tom, one thing we've really worked on this offseason is just like running full speed off the ball. Like if you guys haven't noticed, we made a big emphasis on outside zone and at the point of attack is us. Like we're the first block on the outside. So we've been trying to set that edge um either pinning a D in or kicking him out. So we got to be very physical doing those job doing that job. And I think this these two practices we did a great job of that. So, we were just getting fired up doing doing those things. >> Big picture, how did this camp differ from maybe camps in the past? >> Um, shoot, I don't think it was that much different. I mean, Shane's done a great job pushing us, especially these last two camps have been harder than our camps in the past and different things like that. And he tries to keep the tempo very up. And, um, I I would say the biggest difference this year was probably our pass game was way more efficient. And I think that just came from just working with one quarterback all camp. Um, being with Daniel Camp, having your set starter and different things like that, I think that just helps the offense flow a lot better whether than whether as a flip-flopping quarterbacks, you get different cadence and different each quarterback does different things better and things like that. So, I think just having that continuity and that consistency every day here at Grand Park, too, how much will you miss? >> Oh, shoot. I just definitely miss it a lot cuz everything's here. It's super convenient. The hotel's 2 minutes away. Um, it's great having the fans come out here. So, I don't know how we're going to make it work at the facility. Last time I was there was my rookie year, but everything was a blur back then, so I don't remember much. >> You know, when Daniel got hurt last year after the season, Shane and Chris Brower were both telling us, you know, we think he's going to be back. He's going to, you know, he's better than ever and so forth. But it's hard to envision it back then, right? I mean, >> how for you, did you did you envision? >> It's definitely super hard to envision it because it's Achilles. I mean, you don't really Only couple people I've heard coming back that quick was Cam Makers that one year, came back for the playoffs, and then Jason Tatum recently. So, there were there weren't many great examples of somebody coming back that fast. And then we came back for OTAAS. He's already throwing, running out there in his rehab, and then he starts taking parts in seven on seven, like, hold on, this this might this might be real. And then, um, we went down two weeks before camp, we got together as offense. We went we were down in Florida throwing and he's running, moving around, doing different things. I was like, "Oh yeah, he's back." And then we get into camp, he looks like he hasn't missed a beat and he's scrambling, actually running looks a little faster and different things like that. So, I mean, I think that's just kudos to his work ethic and um the type of person he is. I said like he's always first one in, last one out, always in the weight room getting work done, film room in that quarterback room. If he's not on the field, he's getting different looks. Just just goes to the type of person and player he is. >> And it sounds like you you alluded to this earlier. It seems like you think he's better this camp than last year. >> Oh, yeah. He's definitely playing a lot better. I mean, but he said last year's first year in the system, second year in the system, he gets to put his imprint on it, more his input and different things like that, which is what you want from your starting quarterback. You want him in the coast to see it in similar ways and things like that to put us in a best position to make plays and win. And I think you guys have seen some of that. >> Well, you've seen the highs and lows being here with the Colts and Carly mentioned like the find a way mantra. What did that mean to you when it comes to just winning and getting to the playoff? Um yeah, I had um told the team um I told them find a way. Um to me doesn't happen without trust, belief, and faith. We got to trust each other, believe in each other, and have faith that we're going to get the job done and working towards a common goal. And um I was telling them how in 2018 we were one and five. Um shoot, we even went into a Thursday night game. I don't even think we dressed a full full 48 and things like that, but um we met as a team and we found a way to dig ourselves out of that hole when nine won like eight of the last nine or something like that. and I told him we like came back and won a playoff game. So I said going through that experience um I never believe we start slowing I never believe that we're out of it cuz I've experienced it before. So when guys get down I always tell them like you got to have a short memory in this league because it things move fast and there only you care no one cares about your last game. It's only you got to put your be where your feet are and focus on the next step. So that's what find means to me [laughter] >> last practice training camp. How do you think you guys got better during this period, >> man? We just found a way to win these team periods. So, uh, everybody just went out there and made a play. >> Yes, sir. >> At the end of each camp, what are emotions for you? Like, you guys obviously keep practicing next week when camp's over. >> Oh, man. I'll be kind of sad, but then again, I'll be happy because I don't have to be in all day. [laughter] >> How would you um assess the way Kobe Wooden has kind of helped you all that? Oh man, I love Kobe man. Um, he come to work every day, work hard, man, try to get better, ask me questions and stuff like that. Even though we different players, but um, I still help him out with his power stuff and u, he's just a great guy. >> What have you seen from these young players specifically on defense, the linebackers and what have you seen this camp from them? >> I see all the young guys stepping up making plays like they coming out here each and every day helping out the team and uh, they showing up. I know you played defense, but but when Daniel got hurt last year, I mean, I remember like the gut punches that that was for everybody. Could you ever imagine doing this already? >> Hey, man. Like I tell him every day, man, you're a bad boy. I said, I appreciate you. Whatever you need from me, you want me to beat anybody up, I got you. >> Kind of the same thing with Buck. Like, he had a very serious injury. What's it mean to you for your running to be back? >> Yeah, man. That really hurt my heart, man. knowing that uh the forest he was dealing with that and uh he was going to be missing and stuff like that because you know me and Buck like two peas in a pod. So like knowing that he was going through that but like the way that he came back and like still good still the forest Buckner I call him Buck Nasty. It's a great thing having back out there man. >> This is the last time you guys want to be at Grand Park. What's it been like being here the last time you >> It's been great man. Uh I've been to Grand Park at least nine times. So, it's been a great experience, man. >> What impressed you most about how Buck approached his recovery and how he's kind of back up? >> First off, I'm going to say Buck is a bag man dealing with a injury like that. I mean, only thing you can do is respect the guy. Like, coming back knowing how serious it is and I'm just proud of my guy. >> Just how much have you guys just grown over the course of this camp as a group? >> I say we grown a lot, man. And from day one to now, like each day we got better and like each day you got players stepping up, young guys getting better and either olden guys doing better with their technique. So I say we've been growing every day. >> You got a lot of rookies, especially on defense. I mean, they're all in contention to make the team, the whole rookie class. And have these rookies made an impression on you? >> Oh yeah, man. I love the rookie, man. linebacker. I I give him I talk to I talk trash to him every day, man, because I was like, I want you to be the best, man. I know you could be the best. And uh just like Housey, I was like, hey, man, come on. Let's get it. So, every day, like dealing with the young guys, it's a great feeling for me cuz I know they coming to work and they going to do their thing. Yes, sir.

title: LIVE: The Houston Texans address the media
text: Hey, coach. Can you just talk about what you like tonight and what you uh stood out in terms of areas of need? >> What I really liked tonight was we we improved as a team. All right. Starting off with our offense, the way they came out, open the game, starting drive, driving the ball down the field like we did. Thought the O line blocked it really well. Woody of course has some nice runs, but credit to CJ too. He made some really good decisions. Didn't throw it around a ton, but when he did throw it, good decisions with the football. He moved us up and down the field. So, I'm proud of what those guys went out there and did defensively. The first group did a really good job as well going out getting some stops. Wade came through with the big play, getting the interception for a touchdown. Uh, that's our mantra. That's what we were built on is attacking the football. So, when we do that, puts us in a really good position. So, I saw a lot of improvements from our team from week one to where we are now. Definitely played our style of football, our brand of football. I felt a more physical team. I felt like guys played fast. Felt like we played with some confidence on offense. So, I'm I'm pleased with the outing, right? What our guys did early on in the game. Does don't like the outcome of how it ended most certainly. So, our backup guys there got a lot to improve upon, but that first half was a really good uh half of football for us as a team. Demo with the, you know, first offensive line group that was out there. Is that indicative of how those guys have performed all through um training camp and preseason? >> The first offensive line group, as you guys know, I talk about it constantly. We move guys around to make sure we got our best five guys out there. So, to see that, you got to see guys working together, see guys getting those reps. So, that's indicative of the group you saw out there today. Those are the five we went with today. Those guys have done a really good job. title: Breaking news: Texans sign pair of receivers, what this means for depth chart, trade market & more
text: Hey guys, Aaron Wilson. The Texans took decisive action today, reacting to the season ending injury suffered by wide receiver Jaden Higgins. They signed not one but two wide receivers to try to bolster this receiving core, reeling from the loss of one of their top playmakers. So, they had a workout today that included Sterling Shepard, formerly of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and New York Giants. They also worked out former Jacksonville Jaguars, Arizona Cardinals, and Las Vegas Raiders and Buffalo Bills wide receiver Z Jones, former second round draft pick from my alma mater, East Carolina, where I was a walk-on football player with Zay Jones's dad, Robert Jones, former Dallas Cowboys first round draft pick. And he comes from a great football family. So Zay joins the team along with Sterling Shepard. They also worked out former Texas A&M wide receiver Josh Reynolds and they were looking for a bigger wide receiver and they got that in Jones who's 6'2 200 lb. Shepard is more of a classic slot receiver and he last played for the Buccaneers. He's caught 443 career passes 4800 yards and 25 touchdowns. Caught 34 passes for 349 yards and one score last season but was limited to 10 games and one start. He's 5'10 193. He's a shifty player. He's always been able to stop and start pretty well and he's effective out of the slot. So Jones, he's got 307 career catches, 3,295 yards, 18 touchdowns, but he tore his Achilles last year in November after catching just 12 passes for 183 yards. So he was actually injured against Seattle Seahawks. He was on injured reserve and he worked out for his old team, the Jacksonville Jaguars, earlier this month and now he's a Texan. So, they'll join the team. The plan is to get them in here and have them practice on Saturday. Today is a day off for players. Obviously, not a day off for the personnel department. And as I said, they made exploratory trade calls and didn't, you know, wind up working out. It still obviously something they could revisit if they want to, seeing how these things work out in the short term. But in the interim, yes, they made exploratory calls. Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Rashad Baitman, New England Patriots was wide receiver Kahan Boute. No momentum toward a deal with either. And as Texans said, losing Higgins is not easy to do to replace him. In talking with, you know, Texans coached Demo Ryan and also CJ Strad and wide receiver Xavier Hutchinson. The takeaway I had last night was they're certainly not done because I knew about the calls that reported on the calls and that they were organizing a workout and now today it all came to fruition with the two deals. So it's a situation where the Texans are certainly in a fluid fluid depth chart. How would these guys fit in? So Jaylen Null has missed the entire training camp. He's just practiced a little bit. He hasn't done much. He's now healthy, I'm told, after the hamstring strain that was preceded by a broken right pinky finger. So, this definitely changes things a bit at the slot. Shepard has extensive experience at that position. And Null has to get healthy, practice on a sustained basis, and then get himself ready. He's a vertical slot threat, but he's got to be healthy for the Texans to put him out there with Xavier Hutchinson definitely going to be part of this, but is he going to be the primary number two receiver or is it going to be more of a committee approach? Looks like more of a committee approach. So, they're going to have several players involved in this, you know, quest to replace Higgins production. And really, some of it was projected production. So he caught 41 passes, 525 yards, but six touchdowns. How did they get that kind of numbers from these other guys? Answer is they can, but we were thinking bigger. We were thinking that Higgins was going to ascend, you know, I was doing some projections and I don't think I was being out of line when I thought maybe catches 20 to 30 more passes with his increased targets we feel like he was in line for. So that would have been like 60 to 70 catches and I think his yardage would have went way up 800 900 yards maybe eight nine touchdowns and if that happens then it would have freed up Nico Collins. Of course they're still going to lean heavily on Nico Collins and Dalton Schultz. That's what they did last year. That's what they'll do again. And for anyone asking me about Tank Dale to anticipate the question until Tank Dell practices and is out there where they're comfortable exposing him to contact situations, then you can't count on Tank as part of the receiving solution. Obviously, you know, he has big playability. We've seen him run routes. He looks quick. He looks explosive. I think he cuts very well still. It's been a miraculous comeback from this terrible injury, but it's something of a two-year injury generally when you have those kind of issues. And there's no one else like Higgins, 6'4, 215 pounds, very unique wide receivers now out of the equation. And as CJ Stra said, this is tough. Jaden Higgins was doing great. The best he'd seen from him, making plays, doing things he hadn't seen him do before, playing physical. And you know, he called him a heck of a talent. Somebody came in this league, made plays, and he said, "It sucks. There's nothing good to say. Sadly, we have to try to do our best to rise up with the other guys around us. He said he thinks the guys in that room are special, so we'll be able to do it, but he's definitely going to be missed. He will be, you know, that was something Deco Ryan's acknowledged, too, that this creates a void and it's a significant loss. He called it and it will not be easy to fill that void. I agree with him. This was a unique player and is and of course he'll come back strong. He's going to have surgery. He has been placed on injur reserve formally. They did that officially today, which was anticipated obviously with him being out for the season and being unable to play. Surgery pending. Dr. Dan Cooper, the Dallas Cowboys team doctor, and many have asked me, I've reported this already, why the Cowboys? Can you trust the Cowboys? He's a medical professional and he is the go-to guy for ACL repairs. Dr. Walter Low, formerly a Texans team doctor, currently Astros and Rockets. He did the Tank Dell surgery and he's very good, very respected. Cooper is regarded so highly and he also had done Patrick Mahomes ACL repair which has gone very well and Kitt Kitt is the agent for Jaden Higgins and for Patrick Mahomes. So some connections there and sometimes that's why deals happen or surgeries it's connections. So, I don't know how important that is, but I have been asked a couple of questions for people that want more details explaining what does that mean. It means nothing other than it's the players right and preference on which doctor they choose, which medical professional to conduct their surgery. So, speaking of injuries, and I have more injury information for you all, and we are tracking a couple of situations here, newer injuries. They will continue to evaluate whether they have to do something with the thumb or if it'll be a situation of a soft cast and this could sideline him for a few days. They are returning to practice on Saturday. Today was the day off for the players. Sunday is another day off. Monday they will practice at the Methodist Training Center. Uh actually not going to be at Bank of America Stadium. It'll be at the Panthers team training facility which is also in the city limits of Charlotte. Running back Noah Whittington is regarded as dayto-day. He has an ankle injury. It's a mild ankle injury. He got hurt against the Raiders as well. Defensive end Dominique Robinson. This could take a bit of time, perhaps a week or two. He has a calf injury, some calf tightness he's dealing with. So, those are among the new injuries that the Texans are dealing with. And you know, when you think about, you know, where they're at, they've been relatively healthy with the exception of this one major injury, but it is absolutely major.
