We move guys around to make sure we got our best five guys out there. So, to see that, you got to see guys working together, see guys getting those reps. So, that's indicative of the group you saw out there today. Those are the five we went with today. Those guys have done a really good job. So, we'll see how they keep building and moving forward. >> When you look back at that interception by Wade, was that something that you noticed on the tape when he was coming out of Clemson and the role that you expect him to play with this defense? >> Yeah, for Wade, he just has to be disciplined with what we're asking him to do. Like that pick came from him just being where he was supposed to be and finding a way to catch the football and go score. So, he just has to continue to improve rookie. We're trying to get him a ton of reps and he's done a good job with where what we've given him. >> Irrespectful of the score, were you were you pleased with the continuation what y'all saw in practice against them and then moving into the game regardless of the score. >> We had really great practice this week. I really proud of the practice that we had uh both sides of the ball offensively and defensively. I thought our guys practiced really well. We had a lot of good reps, a lot of good positive plays that happened for us throughout the uh practice and also in the game this week. Guys picked up right where they left off in the first half. you you briefly mentioned uh CJ Shroud um you know not being not throwing the ball as much but did you get what you wanted to see um out of him and and the rest of >> By playing CJ I wanted to see him come out get some live reps with the first offensive line just see him get in rhythm have some efficient plays and he did exactly you know what we expecting him to do and that's the reason you just go get those live reps for him so it's not the first time that they're rolling out versus Buffalo Jimmy though, um, talk about guys like, uh, um, Marlon Klein who continues to, I guess, show you guys what you can do. Are you pleased with some of the young guys, especially because now you got to need some more help in the receiving area. >> Marlin's done a really fantastic job all camp. I see a guy who's steadily been climbing, right? We throw a lot at him. He's handled it really well. He made some plays tonight. He continues to show up and make plays. He makes them in practice. it shows up in the game and he'll continue to get better. I just I love his his effort. I love his willingness to grow and take coaching. Like he's a fun guy to coach. He's a he absorbs a lot of information. He goes out there, takes the coaching, puts it to work, and you see the improvement. And that's what I love about coaching is seeing guys improve, take coaching, and Marlin is one of those guys that gets me excited. another guy tonight, uh, Kaden McDonald, right? To see him, uh, take a huge jump from week one to week two and see him come through with the big sack, I was very proud for Kaden, right? He needed that play. He showed up in practice making plays like that and to see him get that sack, I was very happy for him tonight. >> Coach, we haven't spoken to you since the injury to Jaden. Uh, can you just give a more of an update on that and then what do you think about the wide receiver moving forward? Very unfortunate news with Jaden going down with the torn ACL. You know, he'll be out for the year here is uh and it hurt as Jaden is a guy I've highlighted. I feel like every time I've gotten up and talked, I've highlighted Jaden Higgins because of the work that he's done in OTAAS throughout training camp. He was like one of our best players, right? If not arguably the best player on the field when he's been out there. So, it's a significant loss for us. Uh, we got a void to fill there. And, uh, it won't be easy to fill the void that, you know, Jaden is leaving behind. >> Well, you talked about already the early part of the game, the way the offense and defense both worked. Did it fire the defense up more going against Mendoza and knowing what he had done just winning a national championship last year? >> No. We had talked about earlier this week not being pleased with his first performance against the Chargers. Uh to see him get that pick. What was that like? And what do you think about what he was able to do? >> I'll go back and assess the performance when I watch the tape and watch it in detail. But um I like that way he said that he's hungry to get better. Last week it wasn't good enough. We showed him what he needs to improve upon. And you know, he did some of those some good things in practice and, you know, getting a pick is is one play. It was a big play in the game, but there are more plays we have to watch to see if he's really taking all the improvements that we've asked him to do. >> Thank you, coach. >> All right. Thank you guys. >> Kaden about and some other guys about the loss of Jaden Higgins. Um, how tough is that on you guys? >> Obviously, it's huge, man. Uh, we all love Hig and Higgins having a great year. Oh, I mean, great training camp, so you obviously knew that he was gonna have a great year, uh, coming into it. Uh, but of course, you know, that's how just kind of football goes, man. You never know when it could be your time. Uh, and it was cut short for him, sadly. Uh, but he knows that everybody here got love for him. Uh, this organization stands behind him. The players, uh, in this organization stand behind him and we're going to be here for him. You know, the ups and downs of, you know, whatever he needs. >> Your role, do you expect that to expand and how ready do you feel for that? How much do you believe in yourself to be able to take on Mark? >> Yeah, I believe in myself 100%. Uh, I prepared for this in the offseason. Obviously, not for it to happen this way. Of course. Uh, but you know, I prepared myself to be able to take on whatever role this team needed to succeed. Uh, and you know, if that means being more on my plate, then I'm ready for it. I'm just, you know, I'm ready to ball. That's it. >> Have you been in touch with him? >> With who? >> Have you talked to Jaden or texted him? >> Yeah, of course I've talked to him. Uh, I texted him the same day, even when I didn't even know, uh, what exactly had happened and then I saw him the next day and it was just, you know, just giving them love, man. Like, that's a tough thing. So just trying to be there for him. Uh make sure that he knows that it's all level over here. You know, if he needs anything, I'm always here for him. >> That first drive you guys had, was it pretty efficient? You guys scored a touchdown in the opening drive. Just what's the biggest takeaway from it? Were you guys maybe if coach already ended up saying anything to you guys as far as what what really worked for you guys there? >> Uh man, it was really just coming out there and playing our style of football and I feel like we did that exactly. Obviously, you know, we wanted to get the last game started when the passing game had opportunities to, you know, make the plays. Uh so overall give us a A+. Obviously there's some things that we probably got to work on. Uh of course, but you know that's football though. You're never going to always be perfect. So but to capitalize on a touchdown though, that's what you want to do. So it couldn't have been that bad of a drive. We uh we we made up for some of the mistakes. >> Woody said he couldn't recall the touchdown run. He was just like he kind of went blank, you know, during that run. Yeah. >> Whenever you caught Yeah. You caught a touchdown. Have you had that moment before? Can you can you where you just don't recall how it happened? Uh, no. I I recall all of mine. Uh, his though. His he he was kind of like getting uh like pinalled a little bit. So, I could probably see why he can't recall his. He probably thought he was going to be down somewhere at like the two and then he ended up scoring. But that's Woody though, man. He's a playmaker. And it was good to see him get out there, man, get some touches and eventually end up in the box. >> Before you're busy, do you have a sense of of how good the offensive line was working that first first drive? Because there were holes running in particular. >> Yeah. Uh I think you know overall to have positive plays in the NFL everybody has to do their job and I felt like that's exactly what we did. Uh obviously with scoring but then even you know before like the O line held up in pass protection uh the receivers were blocking, tight ends were blocking uh and then obviously the running back was hitting the holes right and uh he you know he was doing his thing. So overall you know it was great to see us out there and uh really just doing what we know we can do. X within the team when somebody goes down, what do you guys say to each other as far as like picking people up and like kind of saying, "Okay, that happened, but we're not going to let that slow us down. We're going to deal with the adversity." >> Yeah. Um I mean, that's football. I mean, like you never know what's going to happen. Like any given play can be, you know, kind of, you know, your last play. So really, you know, it's really just being more grateful uh for the opportunity to get out there and play football. And as far as like just the next man stepping up, like it's the next man up. Uh we've always had that mentality uh and you know I'm I'm excited to see everybody get you know some new opportunities in there uh to really showcase what they can do and uh you know I know everyone's going to step into the role perfectly. >> You said the other day that after the Patriots game you kind of took stock look in the mirror type moment. Um what did that mean to you to basically say hey you know what that was a play I want back and I'm going to learn from it. >> Yeah I mean you got to be a man about it right? like obviously uh it happened on national television in the postseason so there's nothing I can do about it. I can't take that play away. Um so it's really just you know owning up to it and then really making sure that it doesn't happen again. So the way you can do that obviously with the season ending as you go into the offseason you prepare harder uh than you did last year and you put yourself in a position where if you're in that same position again it won't happen again. And I feel like that's what's going to happen for me. >> I like what you said about I deserve good things. You kind of told yourself that like an affirmation basically. >> Yeah. Of course. I mean, you know, it's all about positive talk. You got you got to give good selft talk. Uh, you know, 80% of the game is mental and 20% of it is physical. So, if you go out there and you don't think that you, you know, can make plays, then you're not going to make plays. Uh, but that's not how I operate. Uh, I know I can go out there and I can make plays and I'm excited to see myself make plays out there for the team. And, you know, like I said, whatever whatever opportunities I get, you know, I know I'm going to see them uh 10fold.

title: Domination early: Texans' Woody Marks, Wade Woodaz excel, new OL wrinkle
text: Hey guys, Aaron Wilson at Reliance Stadium where the Texans dominated at times versus the Las Vegas Raiders. Didn't get the victory, but that's when the backups were in the game. When the Texans starters were out there, they were on a roll. They had some great moments, especially running back Woody Marks, showing power, explosiveness, body lane, and that touchdown. That was impressive. You saw the burst. You saw what we've been talking about throughout training camp and some of the moments that we saw from him as a rookie and they gave the night off to David McGomery. Understandable. He's still RB1, but Woody Marx is carving out a nice role for himself. That's what we expected. That's what they told us throughout the off season. I don't think it's going to be any 50/50 split, but Woody Marks still deserves to get a large amount of work, whether it's catching the football or running the football. He ran for 37 yards or just four carries with one touchdown and of course the touchdown run was 20 yards. Impressive blocking big holes. After the game, Woody told me that the offensive line deserves a lot of credit that these guys got it done for him and he was so happy to run behind these guys and to run behind his pads. So, it's a lot of fun playing with Keelin Rutled. More on him in a moment, but let's start with Woody. It's really to me, he was the story early in the game, what he did. And as I reported, you know, CJ Strad got the start. And what did it mean? So CJ was pretty crisp with the football. He only played just the one series. He completed four of his six throws for 27 yards. I thought he made some good throws by the sideline, showed touch, and he was in command. Keep in mind it was the Las Vegas Raiders backups. It wasn't Max Crosby. Nonetheless, he was making some good throws and really, I would say, doing his job of orchestrating the offense, manufacturing plays, and showing everyone what he can do. This was his first game, even though it's not a game that counts, but his first game since the debacle in New England, the four interception careerhigh, a meltdown at Gillette Stadium in the snow. He's worked so diligently since that game to come back from that. And so what I see from CJ right now is a quarterback that's more comfortable and has really a good knowledge of this playbook in his second year in the system. And so some of the things we're seeing is he's getting to a better level of play, better performances. It comes from that experience. So CJ Strad arrow up. And that's probably the last we'll see of him in the preseason. Normally no starters play in the third and final preseason game. And of course when Davis Mills went in there, he was solid, too. 11 for 15, 93 yards. Uh he was only sacked once. And I thought overall a pretty good day for the Texans top two quarterbacks. Third quarterback, Brad Ripin, intercepted once, throws for 44 yards, sacked a couple of times. It was rough out there with the reserve offensive lineman. So beyond those two performances, got to talk about Texans rookie linebacker Wade Woodazz. He kicks some ass. And I think when you look at WoodZ, he solidified himself as that third linebacker. And we've saw all along he had that potential. Prototypical size, 6'3", 236 lbs, 452 speed in the 40 yard dash. very rangy, intense, instinctive, and a sideline to sideline type of guy. So, what that means for the Texans, do I think there's still going to be a nickel a lot at a 425 alignment? Yes. I don't know if he'll play as much as EJ speed, but he showed potential. He showed real speed on that 80 yard interception return. A pick six picking off Fernando Mendoza. And after the game, nothing serious with him. They were examining his thumb. So, he wasn't uh cleared to do interviews. Same thing with Noah Whittington. Had tough sledding tonight after the 40-yard game he had against Los Angeles Chargers tonight. Only 11 yards on nine runs, 1.2 per carry. Not very good. Not a lot of holes for him to run through. Owen Wright pretty similar later in the game. Eight runs, 21 yards. Not much better. But Woody Marks the highlight for the running game. And if they can run the football, they can establish play action and they can hopefully mitigate some the loss of not having Jaden Higgins, who's of course out for the season. We've been talking about that for days with a torn anterior cruciate ligament. Update I can give you on that. So before we get into Xavier Hutchinson, you'll hear from Xavier Hutchinson, Keelen Rutled, Woody Marx, Kayen McDonald, who had a big sack, didn't get the sack against, you know, Fernando Mendoza in the Big 10 Championship when he was for playing for the Indiana Hooers and leading him to the national championship, but he got him tonight. He slung him to the ground. Very impressed by what I saw from Kane McDonald. We've been talking about Kate McDonald. He was coming along. I know there was a little bit of impatience with how he played maybe in the first preseason game. It was his first game and the big rookie has gotten in good shape. He was training here all summer long in the heat and he's worked very hard. He's improved his diet, he told me. And I really feel like he's done a good job. Let's back up a minute cuz I don't want to digress. Jaden Higgins, here's what I've heard. I've heard it's a no on DeAndre Hopkins, not going to be a fit. That they're looking for a bigger receiver and so that kind of eliminates Sterling Shepard who's a no for him. nothing, you know, advancing with Brandon Cooks. Some trade exploratory things I'm hearing about uh that Texans have some interest in Rashad Baitman from the Baltimore Ravens reported that as well as some interest in Kan Boute, New England Patriots. Whether either guy will be made available, hard to say. I tend to doubt that Jerry Judy will be made available and you're not making a trade necessarily on good terms. So, what this means is Xavier Hutchinson and he's got to step up and he said he believes in himself 100% and he's ready for it, ready to ball and of course feels terrible for Jaden Higgins. A lot of sympathy in the locker room for Higgins and our conversations with Woody Marks and also with Xavier Hutchinson. So, some really good perspectives that I'm going to bring to you in a moment, but I just want to give you my overview. So, I know you guys want to hear my thought. So, Marlon Klein, three catches, 31 yards on just four targets. He's their leading receiver in the preseason. This second round draft pick from Michigan. This imposing young tight end is doing a good job and I'm impressed with what I've seen from him. other guys that were catching passes tonight. Daniel Sopquitz, two catches for 30 yards on three targets, continues to make plays. You guys aren't wrong about Sopquitz. He can play. There's just not a spot for him. So, it's probably practice squad. Jared Wayne, who had that nice 12- yard catch from CJ Strad, I feel like he's going to make it. He's going to stick now. Foster Maro been pretty solid as the backup. A night off for David McGomery, Nico Collins, Dalton Schultz. Let's talk now about the offensive line. That's one of the biggest things. I don't want to miss the headline and bury the lead. Here's the wrinkle. We knew the left tackle was on Touristra and I reported before the game uh in video and uh wrote about it. So the significance of Keen Rutick playing left guard and Wyatt Teller playing with the backups cannot be really understated or overstated rather. You can't, you know, really make that a small thing. It's a big thing. And Ke lives, they're going to have him play whatever position they think he's most comfortable at. And he's a natural guard. And what it means is Wyatt Teller gave up a bad sack today. The former Texans draft pick Thomas Booker Jr. looked pretty slow on that play. And I'm not disrespecting Teller, who's a former Pro Bowl selection, but that was a rough moment. And you know, when you think about the Browns and them moving on from him, maybe they knew something. You know, we haven't seen really great movement. This was a rough moment and he had some moments against the Las Vegas Raiders in the joint practice that weren't great. So, is it getting too late for Teller to lock down the starting job? To me, the only thing that's going to give him the starting job is if Rutled plays center. If they choose not to do that, here's what I anticipate. Evan Brown, who got the start as I reported he would, is going to be the center. He's ahead of Jake Andrews and right guard at Ingram. They haven't done anything to take anything away from Ingram. Has it been a banner training camp at all times? No. There have been some rough moments, but they have quite an investment in him. Three years, 37.5 million. Trent Brown started at right tackle this time, and so Braden Smith came in off the bench. Yes, they have max values combined on two-year contracts for Wyatt Seller and Braden Smith of two years and 55 million total. So two years up to 23 million for Beller and two for 25 million for Braden Smith. Some of Smith's, you know, lack of progress on the depth chart, I can attribute to the recovery from neck surgery. Neck surgery is a legitimate thing. With Teller, you starting to wonder like, is it age? Are there some issues? With Smith, he can also play guard and there's value there. What do I think they're going to do? I don't think there's a trade. No one's going to acquire these contracts. So, what you do, I don't think you cut these guys. I think you have the veteran insurance in case someone gets hurt. If the, you know, floor opens up beneath you and you've got a big hole there, you got to have someone to fill the hole. So that's why I believe Teller sticks, but he doesn't start. Evan Brown has had some impressive moments. They like his versatility. I'll bring you the interview with Evan Brown as well. That was a good interview I had with Evan. Nice uh one-on-one talk. My first time getting a chance to interview Evan, who has significant experience playing for the Arizona Cardinals, Detroit Lions. So interested to hear from him. You're going to get a lot of conversations. So, you know, in terms of what they did against these guys, yeah, there was a long run by Mike Washington Jr. who was a very popular player for Texans draft Twitter, I call it, uh, wanting this guy. They did they draft they did ex, you know, they scouted him extensively. They met with him at the scouting combine. They met with him otherwise. and he had nine runs, 56 yards, and 33 yard run. So, some good things from him. As far as the rookie, Fernando Mendoza, tough night for the first overall pick of the draft. There'll be better days ahead for Mendoza. 8 for 15, 86 yards, the one interception, of course, Wade Wood taking it to the house, and he was also sacked one time. He was slung to the ground by Katie McDonald. I thought Katie McDonald moved very well. We heard from Katie McDonald. And as I said, uh, we have some good interviews to bring to you. So, we'll get to all those. And just, uh, you looking about, you know, let's talk a little defense here. So, Brandon Codington, seven tackles, four solos. The corner. Steven Hall, six tackles. Bryce Hall, six tackles. Jaylen Reed played pretty well, moves very well. Aiden Fischer, another good night, six tackles. And Elijah Huzzy made some plays, four tackles. Jake Hmel, four tackles, another four tackles from offer. But the big story on defense was what they saw from the linebacker, Wayne Wood. To have that kind of big play, that's excellent. That's what you want. That's an athlete. And then Solomon Bird, he continues to have a very solid Overall though, not a ton of quarterback hits. There was one from Javian Clowny. I was joking with JD in the locker. I said, "I was surprised to see you out there playing a preseason football." He said he was. I don't think it was up to him. It was uh it was coach's orders, but he did have that pressure. He got in the face of Fernando Mendoza. So, he's a good football player and he still got it. Mario Edwards Jr. was out there. You had Son Bird, a lot of Dylan Horton, Wade Wood started. You had Jake Hmel out there. You had Jaylen Reed. Reed Blankenship was the only defensive starter that started and I think they just felt like because he's new to the system. That's probably why they did that to have him out there and just kind of get a look at him. And sometimes you do stuff like that, but you're just trying to kind of make sure that he's fully acclimated and you know he's someone that is a leader out there. So completely understand that why they would do that. And of course, you're also going to hear from Demo Ryan and CJ Strad. So, we're going to have an extensive amount of conversations. Let's break for a second and you'll hear from some of the locker room interviews that I've been promoting. And of course, uh, thank you to my sponsors, PM Law Firm at PMTxlaw.com. If you've been accident, you give them a call. And FinsGeeks at finsgeeks.com. And on boarding our new sponsor, and that's US Coins and Jewelry. So proud to be associated with US coins of jewelry. Shot part of a commercial with them today. So US coins of jewelry. You need a nice watch or you want some sports collectibles talking Rolexes, protect Philippes, any type of really beautiful watch or coins, gold bullion, you name it, they've got it. Some really unique pieces in terms of like Babe Ruth cards, a signed check from Babe Ruth, all that kind of stuff. But anyway, we'll go through a little bit after this break when you hear some from some players and we'll be hearing from Dico Ryan, CJ Stra as the postgame show here continues. All right, guys. Right back after this down and just kind of what you saw out there and what you did. >> I just seen the hole and I hit it. Um guys did a great job up front just getting me up to the second level and I had to make plays after that. seemed like a continuation of what you did in the joint practice, but also your entire camp. How proud are you of the performance? >> I'm proud of them guys up front. They made me look better, you know, so guys doing their job up there. Shout out to Co for getting guys ready and I think they take pride of getting up to the linebackers and wanting to score them. >> What's it like running behind Keen Rage and guys like that? >> It's amazing. Um, just know when you score a touchdown, he the first person right there. So, um, told him we ain't got no celebration for him, but he said he can throw me up in there. So, just looking at that. >> Does it feel like the offense checked the box, you know, to they didn't feel like any need to have you play the second series. I think originally that was the plan, but they like what they saw. Obviously, the coaches with the one series. >> No. Yeah, for sure. Um, them guys came out there, they was hunting, um, doing doing the right thing. Um, I think they did a great job. So, that was the reason. How important was it to get just to score on that first drive with CJ, you know, at the helm? >> Uh, very important. Just going down there and showing our mentality, what we want to do and what we're about and um just coming out the gates fire. >> The physicality looks like it's at a whole another level. The way you was breaking through those tackles, you know, has your mentality, how has your mentality elevated from last season? I still got that same mentality without, you know, that's why I believe myself about to just do my dirty work. >> Woody losing Jaden Higgins, how tough is that for this team with the kind of the expectation that he was going to have this uh leap this second year? >> Yeah, real tough. That's my guy. I text him soon as I knew what happened. That's a big loss to us and I know he'll be back even better. just praying that he just stay in the work, stay the work. Um, keep tone to the guys. That's the main thing he got to do and never feel alone. Um, somebody got to step up no matter what. >> How about the guy across from us, Xavier Hutchinson, his opportunity now, >> man, he a baller. Hutch is a baller. He going to do what he got to do. Never get tired. So, he's a baller. >> Started with a mic point. Um, everybody was on the same page. Uh, obviously got some good combos going, got some movement, and then Woody did his thing, so good. >> What' you think about the way Woody ran it? >> Oh, yeah. Doing what we knew we could do. He's a dog, so doing what we knew we could do. >> Playing guard. Did that feel like kind like old times? >> Yeah, I mean, obviously that's what I did all of college. Um, right side now left, but I mean, it's all I mean, the way kind of Pop goes about teaching stuff, it's all very similar. Um, so it's just any position. Is there any difficulty in in making that switch and what are the biggest things to focus on in that switch? >> Yeah, I mean it's different. It's a different position. I mean, one starts with a stagger one obviously got your hand on the ball. Um, but we rep it all the time. I kind of go wherever he wants me to. I'm doing anything he wants me to. So, I've had tons of reps at both. >> How How was it to get the reps in a loud game with >> Yeah, it was good. It was good. I mean, obviously that's who's going to be back there. I mean, Davis can get the job done. Obviously, he's a baller, too, but it's good to get out there and, you know, hear his cadence in a real game. Obviously, see how it flows, so it's great. >> What's it like playing with Evan? Uh, what have you seen from him so far? >> Oh, yeah. He's a he's a vet. True vet. Um, on top of stuff, really smart football player. Um, gets us all on the same page. So, he's a baller. >> How do you kind of build on this? I know you talked to you last time, you're clear satisfied when you're done. >> How do you kind of build on it moving forward? >> I mean, you just there's going to be stuff to clean up in this game. There always is, no matter how good it is. So, you just watch it. Um, you try to attack it every day on the grass. Um, you know, try to fix the stuff that you kind of did bad and then grow on the stuff you did good. Any preference or do you, you know, care guard, center, don't matter. Whatever they need me to do, I do it. >> How valuable was it for you to have the experience in a rookie year to have played center in a training camp and get back to your natural position? >> Yeah, I mean, I think it's huge. Um, obviously, just cuz when you're a center, you got to the playbook is I mean, it's you got to tell everybody what to do. You got to make sure the mic points right. you set the tables for everybody. Um, so that was so valuable for me to get in there and actually do that and then have done that. So I know I'm very comfortable with that and then it slows everything down when you go in the guard. >> Is the confidence plan tonight? I mean limited reps I'm sure you've had more in practice between Evan and Arante. How do you feel like you work together on >> Yeah. No, I mean it feels good. Um, obviously we've we've repped it a lot. Um, there's going to be moving pieces. Obviously that's what training camp's for. Um, but it's been great. >> Is the confidence growing each week? Are you feeling more and more comfortable? How's that going? Yeah, I mean you feel more comfortable every rep. I mean you're you know this first time I ever played in the NFL, right? So haven't played a regular season game, but you just every day you get more comfortable. Every day you you get sometimes you get your tail whooped and that's that's a good thing, right? So that's part of being in the NFL. So you just attack it every day the same way. So >> going back to the joint practice on Tuesday, were you mixing it up at all with Crosby and what was the competition like in general out there? >> Uh competition is great. I mean just, you know, good to go out there and you know, punch somebody else with a different color jersey on, you know, have, you know, mix it up a little bit, have fun out there. So it was good. Was that was that you got into it a little bit? >> I mean, yeah. Just, you know, just kind of going out there having some fun, playing through the back of the whistle, kind of doing what I usually do. So, it's fun. >> Thank you. Thank you, man. >> All right, guys. And there was Woody Marks and Keelin Rutled chopping it up, talking about this game and, you know, just going through some of the things that happened, you know, out there. And yeah, very interesting conversations with these guys. You think about, you know, where this thing stands. And we're getting closer and closer to real football. You can kind of feel that, right? That it's starting to get important. Things are heating up a little bit. So before we hear from the head coach of the Texans, a three-time playoff game winner and guy that's had a winning record every season here with the Texans since he became their head coach. So recap a bit from Demo next. So what he really liked is the improvement as a team, the offense, the way they blocked, Woody Mark's runs, CJ Stra's decision-m and just making good decisions with the football, Wayne Woods's big play, and he felt like they played their style, their brand of football. Yeah, I mean, the outcome of the game, that's not that important. Uh, no coach likes that. text: a really great opportunity as we've been looking forward to the joint practice versus the Raiders is being out here today. It was a really good day both sides really competitive football, physical football, both sides making plays. So, a lot of positives from us uh on both sides also a lot to learn, a lot to clean up as well. I think we got out of joint practice right now exactly what we wanted. Really good competitive work, different schemes to go against different players and >> yeah, I thought it went great. I thought we made a lot of plays. Um, of course all the things you can clean up. Um, but I thought, you know, we moved the ball very well, ran the ball great, threw the ball great. Um, took care of it for the most part. Of course, at the end, got to do better there. But, um, I think, uh, overall we had a really good day. >> Hi guys. Previewing tonight's Texans versus Las Vegas Raiders. Preseason game number two at Reliance Stadium. And here's what you need to know. CJ Strad is slated to play a couple of series, 20 to 25 plays ideally for the Texans, former Pro Bowl quarterback and NFL offensive rook of the year. So, the idea would be to get CJ into a rhythm, get him a little bit of preseason action. They don't play the starters in the third preseason game, and he didn't play, of course, last week against the Los Angeles Chargers. And CJ has had a good training camp, showing good command and overall comfortability in this offense. second year in the Nick Kayley system, which is mostly New England Patriots concepts and a little bit of Shawn McVey, Los Angeles Rams deal going on there. So with CJ, you get him out there, you get some timing and some chemistry. They had considered, are we going to play any starters after what happened with Jaden Higgins torn ACL against the Raiders in that joint practice session seasoning injury? And we've been talking about that in separate videos and we'll get into that a little bit. But the biggest thing tonight is that the starters are going to play and not every single starter, but Woody Marks is going to be out there with the one. So, looks like a night off probably for David Montgomery. The offensive line, they're still trying to figure out the top five guys. And before I get into that though, I'll backtrack a moment. We'll talk a little more about Stra. just going to this is his first chance to play in a game against a real team in a game situation since the meltdown against New England Patriots when he threw a career-high four interceptions. One of those, by the way, was off of a drop pass by Xavier Hutchinson. A play that X still feels awful about and has uh kind of had a look in the mirror moment about that play and it's been a real dedication of his offseason to not let things like that happen again. But, uh, every player makes mistakes. That said, for CJ, I feel like the arrow is going up. He's in good shape. We're getting a lot of praise from Nick Kaye, the new quarterback's coach, Jerry Shaplinsky, and also Dika Ryan and teammates. And I think universally, everyone feels like CJ has made the progress, put in the time, and is doing what he needs to do to have a successful season. It's a pivotal year for CJ. There's a lot on the line. Professionally, financially, there is no deal at this time for an extension. The Texans would like to do one. So would CJ, but there's not an agreeant agreement on terms at this point between the Texans and agent David Muligetta. So there's some thought that, you know, the quarterback market is going to go up, that it's going to be more expensive. And obviously, you know, one of the things that the Texans do and another successful team, the Philadelphia Eagles, Howie Roseman, their general manager, sign guys as fast as you can. You're saving millions and millions of dollars once the market value changes. Eventually, yes. Do you have to account for inflation if you still love the player? Of course. title: Which Detroit Lions Stars Have a Hall of Fame Case?
text: Love it. Hey, before we dive into that stuff, I want to take everyone sort of inside a conversation that I was having with Colton today on the sidelines watching practice and we were in the back end zone watching the first team offense versus the first team defense. A lot of good best on best reps today. And he just turned to me and he goes, "Do you ever pause and think about how many Hall of Famers we get to watch out here every day? Like future Hall of Famers on a daily basis?" And um honestly I I hadn't and and I should do that more often. And I said to him like we should bring this up on the podcast. This is a great way to step back for a moment and appreciate the roster that has been assembled and that all of us are getting a chance to cover that all the fans are getting a chance to watch. And I'll let you guys jump in there, but I thought it was a really refreshing reminder of the talent that we are sort of feasting our eyes on on a daily basis. Yeah, Bertie, I don't know if it was like a Gibbs long run or a St. Brown catch or uh one of Hutch's like 12 sacks today. Um that kind of struck that for me. But I I don't want to become numb to that. I guess that was my point of bringing it up because we get to see these guys every day and you know sometimes I we talked about in the past just watching Hutch and Saint do their their their jobs out here. Um you know, you kind of overlook it sometimes just because of how good they are. That's the expectation for some of these guys. But when you really take a second to take a step back and think about the careers unfolding in front of you in real time, it it's it's really cool. Like I think 20 years, 30 years down the road, I'm going to look back at this time and be like, man, I covered Aiden Hudson his prime. I covered Saint and Pane and Gibbs and Jared Goff, like all these guys that are going to have like great careers, lengthy careers, and probably do great things in this league, continue to do great things in this league. It's just a reminder, as you said, Bertie, you don't want to forget what you're watching out here. We can argue about, you know, who's starting at safety, what the secondary looks like, you know, who's going to be the right tackle, all that stuff. We can argue about that, talk about it all the time, but >> the collection of talent that that this team has out there, it's it's pretty special. And when you get to see it on days like this, you know, one of the last days that fans are out here, you you I guess you kind of appreciate it a little bit more. >> I I think it's a really good point. I I there was a quote Dan had last year that I I think about a lot because I think it applies to more than just the singular situation and it was about St. Brown. He said, you know, I just have to remind myself every single day not to take that guy for granted. And you know, I had the opportunity um Will, I don't I don't know if you were in the mix during Kelvin Johnson's career. Feel like you were >> No, my first year was post Celvin. >> Okay. Okay. So, I I had the opportunity to watch Calvin Johnson in practice every day, and it's kind of the same thing and and different in some way because Calvin was a physical marvel, and he would do those jaw-dropping things like practice after practice, and you start to just get used to it. And watching St. Brown this practice, like the the greatness is just so absurd. And for him, it's just this extreme technical proficiency. Like, I've said this before. or I don't know if I've said it directly to any of you guys, but like I don't know how many players in the NFL squeeze more out of their physical ability than St. Brown. Like everything is just so precise, so crisp. Um, Hall of Fame element of the discussion is super interesting because, you know, I know there are people that'll say too many people get led into Hall of Fame. I think it's really tough, really tough to get into the NFL Hall of Fame at five a year given the fact that we know that there are 50 guys in a roster. So, you know, 1,500,600 plus athletes every year and and far more than that when you start factoring in injuries and only five of those guys are are going to get into the Hall of Fame. And um you know, I'll go back to Andomkin Sue who was in five years in Detroit, a three-time first team allpro uh defensive rookie of the year, absolutely dominant, and looked every bit like he was going to roll into a Hall of Fame career. And um you know, Sue might make the Hall of Fame. I I don't know, but it's it's certainly not going to be a a first time through. It it might take him 10, 15 years. I don't know. Uh and so I I I think at some point I'm still recognizing that we're only seeing small stretches of these guys' career so far. Uh the Hall of Fame largely is about sustaining it over a long period of time. But I will say if this group is the group that gets the Lions over the hump as a Super Bowl winner, like that cherry on top will will be very favorable when they're when their candidacy comes up. But right now, I mean, >> if we're talking about future Hall of Famers, like >> S, St. Brown, Hudson, Gibbs are are all kind of like on a very very early trajectory. But again, I think St. Brown's going to have to do it for five, six, seven more years just given the the receiving numbers that we see here. Hutchinson's going to have to have five more double digit sack seasons plus and he's going to have to finish with like 150 sacks for his career. Like there just so much more that needs to happen for them to to get over that hump. But you guys are absolutely right. Like it it goes back to that ESPN survey we were talking about earlier this year where the top I mean there's nine guys at their position viewed by league decision makers not fans not us that are in the forest and maybe not see or you know not seeing the forest through the trees like the league sees this as a star-studded roster. Uh and so yeah it's it's easy to lose sight of that but uh you know certainly worth stepping back sometimes and appreciating what we we get a chance to cover. Justin, I think you make a great point, too. Like, we should also remember exactly how challenging it is to make the Hall of Fame. It's not just about being great, it's about being great for a decade plus. And, you know, I I think Colton's point is like there's a difference obviously between Hall of Fame career and Hall of Fame talent. But, I just made a quick list of nine guys. And I would argue that all of these guys have Hall of Fame talent, have the ability, if they can continue their current trajectories, to one day end up there. You guys can dispute any of these, but it's the first four you mentioned. Those were the first four that I wrote down. Hutch, Paneet, Gibbs, and Saint, Jack Campbell, Jared Goff, Sam Leaporta, Brian Branch, and J Mo. Now, the flip side of that conversation is like I probably, not probably, I definitely would have had Kirby's name written down just a year ago as a Hall of Fame talent. And that's a reminder of how quickly careers and arcs can change in the NFL. But right now as reporters and and as fans, I think this collective community of of Lions observers has it has it pretty darn good. >> Yeah. >> Yeah. The golf debate is going to be super interesting. Go ahead, Colin. You first. >> I was just going to say I think the whole thing that we were talking about earlier is Yeah. We we use the word Hall of Fame. I think Hall of Fame trajectory is probably more accurate here. Just, you know, looking at the scope of talent they have all at once. And the fact that all these guys are under contract for a long time and they're part of the core here. Like you don't really see too many ple places that have this collection of talent that stays in place as long as these guys are going to be here and the fact that we get to witness that every year. I mean this is year five for me on the line speed. My first year was 2022. Back then Saint wasn't Saint Hutch was a rookie. Jamo was walking around practicing the football because he tore his ACL and couldn't practice. Um you know you look at the guys that are that were there then and the guys that are here now like Jack Campbell, Jamir Gibbs, Brian Branson Porter, all those guys were still in college when I first joined this beat. So, I guess the point was just watching all these guys at once. You don't want to get numb to what you're seeing. And it's easy for us to fall into the trap of >> is this six round pick gonna make the roster is, you know, whatever discussion of the day it is. >> Um, and everyone trying to tear this team down before the the season even starts. >> Like, let's just take a second to appreciate what you have. I guess that's my point. Like, as a mutual observer, you know, a guy that didn't grow up in this state, just watching this team and these guys out here every day go to work, it's an impressive thing. And I I guess today I just didn't want to lose sight of that. >> Yeah. And let me just cut off the Jared Goff haters at the pass if they do in fact exist. If he ends up winning a Super Bowl here, to Justin's point, and plays for as long as he intends to play, that dude's a Hall of Famer.

He's a little handsy, and that's that's been his problem. Uh, I think throughout camp is uh, very aggressive with with the way he's playing the receiver physically beyond that 5-yard line of scrimmage. Uh, so if he can clean that up and and learn to be a little bit more reliant on his feet and not his hands, which is the transition all rookie cornerbacks have to make, but particularly shifting from outside to in, where it's naturally more physical. Like, that's going to be his path. I I've said all along I I think he's starting games this year. I was not convinced it's week one, but right now it just feels like that nickel situation is wide wide open. I do not know. I could not tell you who will be the starter week one if you ask me today. No idea. >> Yeah. One thing I love that the coaching staff does is if you're impressing them, they will give you those opportunities, those [clears throat] breadcrumbs, whether it's, you know, you know, putting putting you in on a package here or giving you a couple snaps against Saint, seeing how you hold up. Like I love that in training camp. That's probably one of my favorite things to track. Um I remember when Brian Branch first got here and I think we all assumed back then, okay, C.J. Gardner-Johnson is going to be your starting safety or nickel, I guess, back then. Um and then you have Tracy Walker, this guy that's coming back. It's like, oh, this is a former team captain, of course he's going to start. Brian Branch [clears throat] very quickly like worked his way into that starting lineup and, you know, didn't let go. Um Abney's a little bit different, but every guy's trajectory is different. But seeing him get more opportunities in these practices with the first team defense has been a lot of fun to watch personally for me cuz he's he was a really fun player to study, um his draft tape and how physical he is, how quick he is, how instinctive he is, um and seeing that translate to the field now and getting those reps. All right, all right, young man, go in, line up against Saint in the slot, see how you hold up. Those are tests that the coaching staff like track and take note of. And if he's winning those matchups, obviously he's not going to win more more of them than you you lose against Saint, but if he's showing some fight in those situations, which I think I think he has, especially in one-on-ones, uh in those wide receiver DB drills, those are fun to watch, too. >> Those are the little things that the coaching staff is looking for and how quick you are to react, if you're retaining the information that's being taught to you. Those are the signs that they need to see in order to give you, um you know, a little bit more run with the defense. And so look, he's in the mix, Jeff. That's your guy. He's he's been out there pretty frequently. Um they're they're rotating guys in and out, but uh I think I would say right now he's got probably as good a shot as anyone to win that starting job. And it might come later, as Justin mentioned, but I wouldn't write him off. If he keeps playing like he has, if he's performing like he has, and he uh finishes strong in these two preseason games, there's a chance that he can force his way into the mix.

title: Inside Vikings Training Camp: Keys to Offense's Success, Defensive Depth, Tight End Position Battle
text: Coming up on this episode of Inside Vikings Training Camp. We have Vikings Radio analyst Pete Bercich in [music] studio to discuss this ever-evolving offense as well as diving in to the tight end three battle. But first, let's hear from Vikings left [music] tackle Christian Darrisaw about hosting the Baltimore Ravens in joint practices. >> Uh it felt really good. Um finally get to compete against somebody else in a practice setting. Um and we were able to just uh come out and and just work on the things that we were working on this whole camp against uh a good defense. And um in a practice setting like I said, so like um it's just great to kind of get it done in practice and then um just go watch the tape, see our corrections. >> That's right. We're talking practice. We're talking joint practices, that is. Welcome inside TCO Studios. I'm Tatum Everett alongside Pete Bercich, our Vikings Radio analyst. And Pete, you've been out here all week observing. You heard Christian Darrisaw talk about how this changes things up a little bit at practice. What were some of your observations out there? >> Kind of I think exactly that, right? You get in Not that you get into a rut, but you see the same offense, you see the same things day after day. So you get some just different blood, different colors, different, you know, just everything. The way that the defenses line up, how they're in and out of the huddle. Um so just mixing it up, it just you get that competitive It just builds, right? You got that whole other team here. You got 180 guys on the field. A lot of whooping and hollering. So um it get helps you get through get through these days cuz this is about when camp starts to get long after that first after that first game. Yeah, it starts to wear a little bit. So I think it's the perfect week to kind of freshen everything up. >> Yeah, having the Baltimore Ravens really does present a unique challenge. They're a playoff team from last season. The Vikings were able to face. And if you were here at practice, you were able to see on the sidelines, there was a new face with a camera. Pete Bercich, care to explain how you uh what you were doing out at practice this week? >> Um yeah, my fiance like is very very good with the camera and composure and all those things. and so because her birthday's in June and then there's Christmas every 6 months I'm getting into the gear, right? So I'm I'm cuz I'm it's the gift so I'm I'm learning about all this stuff and I'm an old telescope guy and I love the technology side of it and you know when they asked if I could do that cuz I've always I'm always back in the VEN with with the guys you know just you know wigging out about F stops and exposure times and all you know all that stuff and [laughter] and so they're like why don't you come out and I said I'll be more than happy to so it's yeah it's a lot of fun it if it can make practice fun again it's it's a minor miracle. >> we can't wait to see your work that'll be coming soon on VEN some of our channels hopefully we're able to see how well you did. But let's get back to the X's and O's of things it's not just the offense and Pete Burks had been getting in good work it's the Ravens getting work against the Ravens. The defense has also been putting in the work. >> Yeah man I think it's a little more realistic to say the least cuz you know you don't know what they're going to run they don't know what you're going to run so you kind of got to just play by your rules and play football which I mean I just like it that way you know just move the ball and you know things aren't really set up to to scheme one another you kind of just out there playing so it's it's it's nice man. >> The defense a spirited bunch against the Baltimore Ravens and their two-time NFL MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson. Pete from what you saw out there it's a group that has some new faces in the mix we've got some of the draft picks that are in all the action from what you observed what did you see from that duo defensive line duo of Caleb Banks and Daron Payne specifically? >> Well for the for the guys up front you know you you you Jonathan Allen last year played a lot of snaps so you're going to have to replace that and when you look at the bodies you're getting you know Jaylen Redmond Levi Drake Rodriguez Ingram Dawkins those guys were all backups a year ago. Well well, Redmond played more and more, but those guys are your start You're going to need some people to take snaps off of those guys. And so, for Caleb Banks and Dominique Orange, they're going to be playing a lot regardless. All right? Regardless if you're a first or third round pick. And when it comes to that with the D-line, there's such a transition between what you do in college and what you do in the NFL. Now, for Caleb, he hasn't played a lot of football. So, what he did on Saturday was probably the most he's played in a long time. Now, quick turnaround, you're going against a whole 'nother team. So, this will be a great chance for him to work the technique, and that's really the big thing with with these defensive linemen. It's so technique-oriented, playing with your knees bent. Uh those things take some time. And we're going to need them. So, the faster that they can get ready, uh the better this defensive front is going to be. >> How different is NFL technique from college technique? >> Just Just ask Dominique Orange. I mean, he you know, they played the like a 3-3-5, or they had three defensive linemen, and he'd line up over the center. And if it was a pass play, they would just kind of take up space. I mean, there was no real transition from a run to a pass rush, right? And uh it was very basic what they did up front. Now, he's getting into where they're stunting and where we're we're playing blocks differently, playing cross trying to cross faces of different guys. So, just the whole thing is is a whole it's it's a whole different [music] animal. Um and that transition, I think, from run to pass is something that is new to him, and it's not easy to do, and it's going to take some time. >> Another draft pick worth highlighting is linebacker Jake Golday, who a lot of the veterans are saying he's picking up this defense quickly. What are your observations? >> I've heard I've heard and seen kind of the same thing. Here's a guy that that walked on or got an opportunity, excuse me, to play at Central Arkansas as a D-lineman, and then he moves to linebacker. And you don't normally see guys go from three-point stances and on defense to two and it's not an easy transition but he does all the off-the-ball linebacker stuff while reading guards. Now you're asking him to cover. He has really good feeling coverage. He's a big guy, 6'5", great athlete. The question was kind of physicality. How physical was he going to be? Well, today he had I know one real big hit. So, looks like uh looks like he can bite, too. >> Nice. >> And it all looks good. They used him a lot on Saturday in a lot of different positions and for a young player, I think that that's commendable. >> A lot of different positions as in in the linebacker room or did he move or did they >> Well, yeah. He I mean, he's he's he's kind of doing the Van Ginkel thing where sometimes he's on the line of scrimmage but then he's off the ball. He's behind, you know, they he has a little bit more position flexibility, I think, than Van Ginkel cuz he's kind of a Cashman-Van Ginkel hybrid type, you know, type of more or or more like Eric Wilson who you see off the ball and then on the line of scrimmage and it may not seem like much cuz you're just moving a little, you know, a couple feet but it's a completely different world. The reads are different. The technique is different. Your responsibilities completely different. Um and for him being so young and to be able to pick all that up um is is is pretty remarkable. So, he's a depth person, too. So, if any anyone in those starters go down, he's probably going to be the next guy in. So, could be a Cashman, it could be a Eric Wilson, it could be a Van Ginkel, it could be Dallas Turn- I mean, he's he's the next best guy in. So, he's going to have to learn it all. >> All right. Well, that's par for the course in a Brian Flores defensive scheme, I feel like. Let's dive [laughter] into the Vikings offense and boy, did we see a beautiful completion between Kyler Murray and Justin Jefferson at joint practices day one. That just comes with time, the reps that we we have here in practice, but that's why these joint practices are so important just because we're not getting those game reps until, you know, the season actually starts. So, getting those game reps with Humphries and Wiggins on other side, it was it was definitely work to be done and it was great work. >> Pete, it's been about a week and some change since KO named Kyler Murray as the starting quarterback. We got to see him in the preseason game as well. What are some of your observations about the connection as far as Kevin O'Connell, the play caller, and Kyler Murray have been going? >> Yeah, I um it's always interesting because you're going to wonder how far is KO going to you know, adjust the system to fit Kyler Murray's skill set. So, there's going to be a little bit of a meeting in the middle in that regard and and that's all going to obviously be a work in progress. That's why it's so important for Justin Jefferson and Kyler Murray to be on the same page because things are going to change. It's going to be a little bit different. And it can be great. We'll, you know, we'll see. Uh but the more that those two can be on the same page, the better. You know, Justin Jefferson's a $40 million asset that you have sitting out there that caught two touchdown passes last year. He, you know, he's ready to go. You know he's ready to go. And you know Kyler's just just excited to be able to step on a field and have those weapons on the outside between he and Addison. And you know, you have Hockenson. Uh you know, cuz Kyler Murray loves tight end. You know, tight ends that have played with him have have all had success. Because uh I don't think Green Bay's going to have an idea what to expect when you play them on opening day, which is going to be a big advantage. >> [laughter] >> Yeah. >> That's what I love to hear. I also love that you brought up the tight ends because that is a position battle that we are going to discuss because we do know when you look at the depth chart on the current Vikings roster at vikings.com, you can find that the league's two one of the league's two top two tandems is Josh Oliver and T.J. title: C Aaron Brewer meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Rookie, it kind of looked like the pass protection had its tough moments, but the run blocking was really good. Would you agree with that or how did you think the offensive line did today? >> Um I felt like it was a good battle. You know, we had like they had some wins, we had some wins. So, I felt like it was just some good competition out there. Once I watch the tape, I'll see how we did as a overall, but it felt like a solid day. >> Coach Hafley said before practice he wasn't into the idea of fighting, but that ensued. So, are guys going to see the wrath from that or what? >> Uh I'm not sure. I ain't going to tell you. I don't know which way Jeff going to go about it, but you know, we try to hold our composure as much as we can, but when you out here playing football, it get chippy. Like as I said before, like it's the people out there competing. They taking all the way to the edge and you know, we ain't try to initiate anything, but somebody come at you, like you got to hold your ground. So, yeah. Mhm. Uh yeah, he definitely kept his composure, but as I said, like if somebody like come up to you, hit you in your mouth, like what you going to do? You going to stand there and look at them or you going to respond? And definitely like here at practice, like in the game, I definitely expect him to hold his composure, but the way the things was occurring out there, like I'm not surprised at what his response was. >> Even though there was a break in practice after it appeared that the Giants defense had gotten some pressures, where it looked to me from the stands like you were talking to your teammates. >> Mhm. >> What if anything can you share about what you were stressing? >> Uh just the details, you know what I'm saying? Like details and just a sense of urgency, you know what I'm saying? Like we be out there and we be going and everyone get to at a moment where they trying to just go to the next play cuz you trying to have that short-term memory, but at some time you really got to lock it and see why it be same problems keep occurring. And so, that's what I was digging into them, like we have to lock in right now on these details and fix them, so we don't have them again this next play. And that's all it was, to be honest. >> You got a you got a lot of snaps out there, so did the first team offense. Can you take a guess on what you guys might do Saturday in in how many plays or anything like that? >> I couldn't tell you. Couldn't tell you at all. >> Okay. Uh I feel like that's like literally there's much we have to have in a game, like no disrespect to them, like they are some great pass rushers, they guys that they have over there. And so, I expect them to win some, and us to win some as well. But, you know, that like in an NFL game, you're not going to win every single rep. And so, with Malik, like some of the pressure he got, he was able to move maneuver and get around move rep a little bit. And like that's what we know Malik is as an athlete, as a quarterback. He move, he can move. And so, him being able to do that and keep his composure, that just shows what we need when the season come around with in the live bullets. All right, it just gets you to work your craft, you know, like in the game, yes, we're going to scheme you and give chips to good elite guys. And when you're out here right now, you want to like iron sharpens iron. And so, you want to just continue and just stack those reps and getting in one-on-one reps and working on your craft and seeing like what feels good to you against certain type of players in different looks. So, I feel like that's a great way to just be able to work your craft in this environment. Absolutely. In football, just offensive line play and football is a whole defense, offense, violence and physicality can fix a lot of things. When things go wrong, you playing physical and you run through somebody's face, that can fix everything. And so, we got that part down, the physical and violence part of it, you throw in the details, then you're unstoppable.

title: Coach Jeff Hafley meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Full house, too. How's everybody doing? >> Good. Good practice. >> All right. >> Oh, thank you. >> Do I even have a choice? >> [clears throat] >> So, there there's obviously good young talent at safety and quarterback, but I think you guys are the only team in the league without an established starter from the last couple years in either position. How much have you and Sully talked about that over the last few months? Have you been tempted to add someone and why haven't you ultimately? >> Um well, you've asked me like three questions there. Uh no, we we we've talked about it, but at this point we're we're coaching the guys that we have. Um and I appreciate all the hard work and everything that the guys who are here have done. Um I trust the guys we put out there. I think there's still a healthy competition at that position and actually in both positions. Some we've been hurt at. Traitor is going to work back more in today. So, hopefully we'll get a better evaluation of him, but No, for us it's about who's here, how can we get them better, and then how can we maximize their abilities within the scheme, and then go play ball. but I've enjoyed those guys and I have a lot of respect for how hard they've worked and what they've done. >> What what's the message to your team today so that it doesn't turn into a melee? >> With fighting? >> Yeah. >> Yeah, it's the same thing that I say every day to the team. I mean, that's not tough. Like anybody who's been around me and then watched us play, I I want to tow the line and I want to play physical and I want to be tough, but fighting's not tough. And I and I told him, "If you're frustrated with a guy and you get pushed or shoved, tell him I'll see you next play." And then go play the next play and do it again. That's tough. That's mentally tough, right? Cuz in a game, what's going to happen when you get frustrated? You're going to get thrown out of a game. If you throw a punch, you're gone. Especially now with the new rules, they're going to be able to see it. I mean, it it's not part of the game. So, I'll be really disappointed. If a guy throws a punch, he's out. We haven't had that happen in our practice much. And the other thing is I told him, I think there's a brotherhood in the NFL that you got to respect that all these guys right now, these 180 players, they're all trying to earn a job. And there should be a mutual respect about the guys in this league on how hard they're working to get a job. You're being evaluated by both staffs today, right? And you you want to try to fight and hurt guy on the other team? I mean, that's just I I've seen it. I get it. I get it gets chippy. It's going to be hot out there. But if you want to find out who's really tough, find the guy who walks back to the huddle, lines up, and goes at it next play. I will be really, really disappointed. Could it happen? Sure. I will be very, very disappointed and it will be addressed immediately if it happens. >> Jason Marshall Jr., um I want to know what you've seen from him and has he kind of been on an island considering JuJu Brent's hasn't been there at times, Chris Johnson hasn't been there for a couple of days, and Dante Trader hasn't been there for a couple of days? >> One, he's been available every day and he's been very, very consistent. Um every single day he just his technique, his coverage, the way he's coming up and thudding on tackles. I just think he's a guy who when we talk about consistency over time, he is a a very, very good example of that, which is why he's improving. Um so, I'm excited to see him today against some good wide receivers. >> Coach, if the NFL said that they were going to get rid of the preseason and all you can have would be joint practices, >> do you think that would be enough to get your team ready for a season? >> Um that's a good question. We'd have to. So, I mean, whatever whatever they say we need to do, we need to do. I still think there's something about getting off the bus, going into the stadium, being in the locker room for whether it's an hour or 2 hours depending on when you get there, walking out, going through your pregame routine. I think especially for the young guys. Like, for example, we have we have a lot of young guys and I think right now it's really important for them to go through their routine in these three preseason games. What is their routine? What bus do they want to get on? In college, you just all get on one bus, you go together, you kick off and you play. It's different, right? So they got to feel comfortable and I think a lot of them get the anxiety out that way because no matter if you call it a preseason game or a real game, there's a certain level of anxiety. Just like today, that will start to creep up. Just like when we go in the stadium on Saturday and I think they need to go through that. Um so I I I think they are important still. I think you get a lot out of the joint practices, but I think you still can get a lot out of the preseason games as well. >> The um the Giants, excuse me, have a lot of talent at the edges. What do you want to see out of the tackles and tight ends? >> Well, they have great talent. They have multiple edge players that can rush. Um I think that is an awesome opportunity. I'm excited to watch those one-on-one. I think it's you know, iron sharpens iron. It's going to be fun to see and then I want to see how we get in the team settings. We're not going to do seven-on-seven. Um I know you all will be disappointed in that. We want to play real football and I want to see if we can block them. Um if we can pick up the pressures in our protections, if the quarterback can get rid of the ball on time, if the receivers can run the right routes so the ball can get out on time. So it's going to have to be a team thing, but they've got great edge rushers. I'm excited to see the o-line against them today. >> On the housekeeping standpoint, Juju has been practicing. Is he going to be participating in the 11-on-11s and how much has his setback prevented you guys from evaluating him? >> Well, just like any other player, it's hard to evaluate anybody that's not out there. Um he will not be out there today in 11-on-11. He's getting closer. He's been doing individual. Hopefully this is more day-to-day now as we get closer than it will be long-term. Certainly we'd like to get a good evaluation on him and we still have time to do so. >> Hey, Jordan Brooks, so where does he stand right now? >> Jordan will be out today. >> How do you see your competition between Dodson and Rodriguez at linebacker? >> I think it's a great competition. You got a guy who's had success in the league and has played in a lot of games, has a lot of experience, and is a really smart football player. And you have a good up-and-coming young guy who's extremely instinctive, uh violent. Um and I think it's a a very healthy competition right now. >> Jeff, have you or Bush or Bobby Slowik talked to Kameron Miller about the opportunity in front of him? Do you need to do that with uh with Quinn you were sidelined? >> I'm sure he sees it. Um he got more reps in practice yesterday, so there's opportunity every single day. And I'm sure him and Bobby have had those conversations. >> Jeff, we get Malik today. Just actually what you've seen here in camp uh to validate what you liked about him in Green Bay and and why you brought him here. >> Yeah, um kind of what you saw during the game. Um he's become very confident, uh more consistent. He's taking care of the football. He's getting rid of the ball on time. He's playing in the pocket. But now what he's starting to do is as it gets closer, he's starting to use his legs not just to run the ball, but to kind of step up, escape, make some throws down the field, or take off, or extend plays. We sent a pressure at him yesterday, and I thought we had him or the day before cuz yesterday was a walk-through. We sent a pressure at him yesterday in a situation, and I was like, "All right, we got him. They're not going to block him." And it was really cool. For the first time I saw him, he kind of baited it cuz it was to his blind side. He kind of baited him, saw him, and then spun out and ran and threw a touchdown. And I was angry cuz I'm the one who made the call, but I was really happy because I looked at him and kind of smirked. I was like, "I got no answer for that." So, he's starting to play the game a little bit more rather than just practice. Um and hopefully we'll see some of that today like we said against a good group, and you know, determining whether or not what we do with them in the stadium on Saturday and going forward. >> Jeff, are you cool with him doing that and using his legs more when pressure's on him? Or would you rather him take advantage of throwing it short to H and which H and was really good at doing that? >> Well, it depends. Is H and involved in the protection? Where does his read start? Where does his check down? If he's getting pressured real fast and he's about to get sacked, I sure want him to get the hell out of there. So, I'm really cool with him doing that. I want him to be a free feel free to be himself and that's what I keep telling him. don't want to coach him like a robot. I want him to go through his progression, but at the same time he's got a talent and he has the ability to see things move and keep his eyes down the field and he's very very accurate when he does so. And I want him to start doing that as we play football cuz that's real. >> Jeff, what have you seen from Jackson Dart? >> What have I seen? Well, we played him really it's more from my study last year cuz I all I had was a few preseason clips from him from this season. So, just getting ready for him last year in Green Bay not knowing if he was going to play or not. Um you know, I see a talented young player who who's extremely athletic. He can run. He can make plays kind of like Malik with his feet, but he's got a strong arm. you know, there was a bunch of times I watched his tape last year thinking back where it's like you know, one I respect the way he plays cuz he seems like a tough guy that you'd love to have in your locker room and he's very talented. >> What do you know you're getting when you have when you go up against a John Harbaugh team? >> Discipline. Uh they're going to play really hard. Pre-snap, post-snap, very detailed. I think he's one of the best coaches in the NFL over a long period of time. He's proven that. I have a ton of respect for him. I always have. One of the reasons cuz we kind of set up these joint practices as coaches. It's kind of like I said about Dan Quinn yesterday last week. Dan's a guy I have a ton of respect for in the way he does things. I want to practice against teams like that with leaders like that. I have so much respect for coach Harbaugh that this is a team that I felt like we could get a lot of really good work with because of him. So, that's I can't say enough about him and what he's done and I think he'll be great for the Giants. >> Jeff, when you're when you're building a new team like this, [clears throat] how do you create how do you get buy-in from players on the new culture like you're saying? No seven-on-seven, I'm sure there's guys who want to run that. How do you get buy-in from the guys early on and how you guys want to practice and approach them? >> Yeah, I think one it's who you bring in. You know, I think the draft was really important. You bring in guys that you you see on tape that love ball, that are physically tough, that when you talk to them they kind of you figure out they love football and how to the way you watch their tape, you get guys that really love ball and I think it's easy. And then you look at the the key guys that we re-signed here, right? Brewer [clears throat] is one of the toughest, hardest working guys I've been around. Brooks, the same thing. I mean, those guys want to tackle and they want to go live. Each hand's been the same way, it's been awesome. And then a vet like Zach Seiler. So, the buy-in has not been hard. It's been very honest with them. I've been very transparent with them. I've told them what I want to do, but why I want to do it, right? And then you know, I just we have a really good group of guys in the locker room. We have a lot of guys here who are fighting for their lives cuz they're on one-year deals. When I think when you get in a situation, I think we have over 40 of those guys. I think it's you know, they're fighting for their jobs. I think they're going to do anything that you ask him to do. I just believe in this way as we build this thing over time, if we're going to have a foundation, it needs to be built the right way and these are the things that I believe in and those are the guys that we're going to play. >> Jeff, as you go through preseason games, are there certain situations that you think you absolutely need to see to get ready for regular season like two-minute offense, four-minute offense, red flag challenge, things like that? >> Yeah, unfortunately, I can't control all those in a preseason game, but I can control them in practice. So, you know, one of the reasons I didn't want to have a a third joint practice is cuz I want to use next week as we've kind of built the scheme, we kind of get closer to see who we have, what we have, where they're going to play. Next week will be huge situationally, and we do have to get into all those. I think there's times in a preseason game where I might have to call a timeout or do something I normally wouldn't do to try to generate that situation where people might say, "What is he doing?" And it's no, I want to get this quarterback extra reps or I want to get this ball carrier a certain amount of touches. I mean, there might be an instance where, you know, you're down in the game, but you're going to see us run the ball 15 times just to say we got these two backs and we're trying to figure out who the guy is. So, certainly you got to try to figure that out. Throwing the red flag? I don't know. I mean, I'll throw it if you want, but >> So, it's just a chain of command thing to make sure that the operation is smooth. >> Yeah, we'll see. I got it in my pocket. >> We know point is dealing with a couple injuries, an injury or two. Does that ultimately affect how you evaluate him or do you take it at face value? >> I mean, just get him back, get him healthy, and we'll continue to evaluate him. I mean, that's what we need to see. So, you know, I got to He threw yesterday. I think he felt better. And we'll see how he is tomorrow and the next day, and we still have time, but you know, we have a bunch of film already on him to evaluate him, and I want him healthy so we can continue to do so, and he can put his best foot forward. >> Two of the two of the best offensive linemen in this past draft will be on the field today, both top 11 picks. Did you think back, would you and Sully have been happy with either guy, the one you got or Maui Noah? And how is Proctor doing? >> Proctor's been outstanding. I mean, I just I can't say enough about him. It's just the guy loves ball. The guy is tough. He's physical. The buy-in has been outstanding. He's fun to be around. He loves coming to work every single day. He's a rookie, right? So, he's going to see some stuff he's never seen before. He's going to see stuff at practice he's never seen before cuz it's not our defense and there we didn't game plan against him. So, there's going to be moments where maybe he's late coming back on a game or maybe they stem any combos to the wrong guy and you got to take a deep breath and really watch him grow and that's what I'm say excited most about him. >> I wanted to ask two questions about the last practice that we saw.
