What what qualities does he have that you feel kind of bring the best out of you? >> I think what's really good about Drake is he's super positive and uh he never uh gets down on himself or on the team and he's super encouraging and uh kind of just like a next play mentality, good or bad, we're going to move on and um you know, it it's uh it's great having him as our quarterback. >> How does this How does this physically compare to what you went through at Notre Dame to get ready for the season in terms of the practices, meetings, etc.? >> Yeah, I mean, the schedule is very similar, but the people I'm blocking and going up against is different and uh in in a good way and it's getting me better and uh yeah. >> How was it beneficial going up against more skilled guys, bigger guys, faster guys? >> Yeah, when you when you go against the best, it it raises your your game to another level and uh it's caused me to um turn turn my game up a notch and really really dive in and uh focus on improving, so. >> What specific ways have you improved your chemistry uh with Drake in the last few weeks? >> Yeah, I just think uh just the timing of the routes and um just creating separation uh creates trust and that's what I try to do whenever I'm out there, so. >> Eli, how's the uh Nissan Altima hanging in? >> It's going It's going It's going well. it's in good condition and we're going to keep driving it, so yeah. >> on that car? >> What's up? Uh it's almost at 100. So. Yeah, exactly. >> How do you feel like you kind of progressed as this camp has gone on and you know, what's your comfort level in this offense as things stand? >> Yeah, I think uh like I've been saying before, every day is just uh a great opportunity for me to um you know, improve on the offense and uh every day it's starting to you know, get easier and everything's starting to slow down and um because of that I'm able to play faster and you know, not think as much out there, so it's been good. >> Eli, in terms of this next practice, I mean, what do you feel like the opportunity is for you? same mentality as before, as last game uh just play as hard and fast as I can, try to make some plays and um whenever I'm making mistakes, make them make them at full speed, so. >> Eli, do you feel like there's any extra value to being in that stadium atmosphere? >> Yeah, I think I think it's good for us to be in there and uh yeah, I think visualization is is is an important thing and for us to be out on the field and and uh making plays uh in front of a you know, this crowd. Yeah, it's There's a lot of people here, but in the stadium it's different and I think that prepares us uh uh in a better way for our game, so. >> Personally, have the joint practices been a good gauge for you and where you're at and where your comfort level might be? >> Yeah, I think it's uh I think it's a great thing. I think it um they're they're super competitive and uh kind of simulates a game uh game for us and um you know, when you're going against someone else, um, it's a little different. Like you you feel you know, like you have to perform a certain way and when you know, when we're going against our team, we we kind of feel like um you know, like we're teammates, but when uh, the bar's raised a little bit. >> Eli, you mentioned making mistakes at full speed. The coaches have given you a lot of praise for not repeating mistakes. How would you describe yourself as a learner and what's allowed you to avoid making those repeated errors? >> Yeah, I think for me, I I uh after every practice I write down my my mistakes and uh before practice I kind of write down pre-practice emphasis on what I want to emphasize uh going into practice the next day. And I feel like writing those things down and kind of looking over them has helped me to, you know, be more aware of that on the field uh and and making corrections to my mistakes. >> What did you write down today? >> What did you write down today and how did it work? >> Uh honestly, uh just better better run block footwork for me. Um and that was I mean, that was the main emphasis. Coming off the ball hard and making sure my steps are are going at the right angle. >> Rise up when you when you're out here, but also if you've been able to like think less when it comes to the playbook and and everything and just going out and play. >> What Can you repeat that again? >> Have you felt the level of competition go up in these two days here, but also if you've been able to like not think and just follow the playbook and go? >> Yeah, yeah, I feel like it's gone well. Um, feel like the game's starting to slow down for me and I think the atmosphere's like this are really fun. I love to compete against different teams um I feel like um you know, everything's slowing down, so >> Thank you guys very much. >> Thank you guys.

title: Drake Maye: "When You Get the Ball Out on Time, It's Always Better." | Patriots Press Conference
text: Yeah, there we go. What's your biggest takeaway from the two practices? >> I think we got a lot of great work. I think, you know, the biggest thing is, you know, that's a good football team over there. And I think just not riding the roller coaster. I feel like we had some good periods that we were, you know, attacking them and you had some good plays and we had some periods where we got to, you know, continue the competitive stamina. And that's the thing about this game, you know, you can't just be, you know, one play here, one play there. You got to string some, you know, plays together in a row and I felt like you we did that more yesterday than we did today. So, just getting back. I know it's tough down there in the red zone. You know, a lot of bodies in a short amount of space, but you know, I feel like we could have, you know, done more in the red zone. And I think that's something for us to, you know, learn. It's one of our focuses this year to be better in the red zone. So, we got some work to do. >> Great help. What's your I guess level of play going up with AJ as you guys spend more and more time together on and off the field? >> Yeah, just I think just, you know, growing that relationship. You know, it's it's huge for, you know, a quarterback and receiver like himself, you know, just to, you know, keep growing and keep, you know, not, you know, just feeling like you're leveling off and trying to keep getting better. So, you know, he does a great job of talking to me, seeing what he sees, seeing what he's seeing in the in the DB and and just seeing what I see from my point of view. So, he's eager to learn and eager to, you know, share his opinion. I think that's really important for a guy like him and he he'll continue to make plays and we got to find, you know, more ways to get him the football. >> So, you were saying yesterday that he you make his life easier. How does How does AJ make your life easier on the field? >> Yeah, I think any time receiver like that, you know, who carries that much weight, you know, and just find a ways to get him the football. And like I say, every I was all the time I try to get the ball into their hands cuz they make me look good. And that's, you know, the number one thing with AJ. He's he's made, you know, a lot of you know, plays in his career, you know, taking it the distance on, you know, crossing routes and and making, you know, great catches on deep balls. And he's just, you know, he's another leader in the in the huddle, too. I think that's one of the biggest things with AJ. You know, he's got this, you know, demeanor and respect from the team that he just walked in with cuz of the the player he's been. And I think he's taken that taken that head on and I really respect the way he goes about his work. >> Can you walk us through the interception down here in the end zone? Was there any kind of miscommunication? >> Yeah, no, I just late late to the football late in the red zone. You know, you can't be late in the red zone down there. It's tight and it's um um you know, concept that we you know, probably have need to get some more work on and just find some timing. So, uh you just can't be late down there. >> Drew, you mentioned wanting to be better in the red zone from last season. What are the areas that you felt held you back and how do you feel like you're progressing this season as you work through those? >> Yeah, I think we just got to find a way to make positive plays. I think that's the biggest thing. You know, try to keep moving forward and it starts with me with you know, communication and uh you know, avoiding penalties and avoiding sacks and avoiding you know, negative plays. So, I think that's the biggest thing with us just to find positive plays and you know, keep getting guys the football and and running the football. I think that's a a big area as well. >> What do you think's been What do you think's been your biggest area of growth as a leader in the last year? From last year at this time in training camp to to now. >> You know, I think I still got ways to go. You know, I think I still need to say more. You know, I think I'm you know, comfortable with a lot of guys in the huddle, a lot of guys on our team and I think there's areas for me to you know, take the guys, you know, on on offense especially and bring them to a different level and elevate their game, elevate my game and you know, kind of bleed that into the defense and the whole team. So, I got some ways you know, to work and I think that's the best thing about um you know, working out here and finding some adversity. You got to you know, find something and and keep straining. >> Drew, you mentioned that Dobbs has made a handful of nice catches over the last handful of practices. How do you feel like your connection with him has started to grow? >> Yeah, he's done some great things. You know, the way he moves and and and uh kind of cuts off on some routes and and can kind of move his body side to side and and kind of get by people is really impressive and it's really fun to watch and he's only going to get continue to get better and better as he you know, gets more comfortable in this offense. So, I'm looking forward to him and he's made some great you know, climb the ladder catches. You know, just keep giving him chances to climb the ladder and he'll come down with it. >> You guys had a pretty good front. Just how do you feel like the offensive line you guys did blocking those guys this week? >> Yeah, I think they you know, stood in there and tried to take them take it on the chin. I think that you know, the best thing about you know, those guys up front is you know, they never really get the love that they deserve and I think they really deserve it yesterday and I think there's some things today including myself of getting the ball out and you know, them kind of standing more firm up front today that we can we can you know, continue to challenge them and those guys have a tough job and it was two consecutive days in a row of you know, getting a good front that's got some good players up there that's made a lot of plays in this league. So, you know, they had a tough task and I think they they stood up to it well. >> Speaking of Romeo Doubs, I'm curious, what's it like, you know, when you see him jump up and again over the defender and kind of bring the ball down? Is that a point of emphasis then that you know you can kind of hit him in those situations and target >> It's very comforting seeing that from a a receiver going up and make a play up top. It's a it's a his ball or nobody's what I'm trying to do and um it's been his ball more times than not. >> Great, when it comes to A.J., are you still kind of learning when he's covered, when that means he's open, and when he's covered when he's not open? You know, kind of working through >> Yeah, I think you have to with the details. You know, the details of this offense and what I like to see when I'm, you know, coming back side to him or he's front side in the in the uh you know, in the concept. So, just different versions and moving him around and he's done a great job of learning, you know, kind of what what to do, where to line up, and um there's still ways to go, but I'm looking forward to seeing uh him in this offense. >> How has your process changed the way you approach, sorry, in terms of recognizing the by pressure? >> Yeah. >> So, when they collapse in the pocket? >> Yeah, I think you always have a that idea against you know, teams that have a good front. They may not bring pressure as much, but when they do, they're going to bring it. So, just having, you know, a concept of, you know, what the defenses like to do, you know, coming into the week and then uh from there knowing where my problem is and trying to find answers. >> I two years ago when you guys had joint practices against Philadelphia, it was lopsided. A lot of people came away from it like, "Eagles are elite and the Patriots have a long way to go." How do you think about that now, two years later, where you're competing against them and the competition is really tight, and you're winning sometimes, they're winning sometimes, which wasn't the case two years ago. >> Yeah, that's what joint practice is about. And, you know, last, you know, two years ago, I was a rookie coming in here. I was watching some of those plays earlier in the week. Um I was just laughing. I was I motioned somebody who was coming forward and snapped it and there was a penalty and and little things like that that we were laughing about. Um just, you know, how far you've come, but I think they won a Super Bowl that year. I I think that was what, 2024? Yeah, they won it. So, um you can see that they got a great football team, a lot of the same players over there. So um you know, got to continue to show our identity I think we definitely you improve in regards to 2024 that's for sure. So we got some ways to go but I'm proud of the guys effort. >> How was it talking to Jalen Hurts while he was here and kind of if so what were those conversations like? >> Yeah just I just literally called him on the way out as he was leaving the field you know big fan of his game you know rooting for him I told him back when I was committed to Alabama back in the day he was you know some of the quarterbacks that I was watching them play there and then he ended up going to Oklahoma but yeah he's you know a Super Bowl champ you know that speaks for itself so I had one of my best friends Sam Howell was in the room with him last year so I got to know you know some stories about Jalen and how he works and you know I respect him a lot for that and you know I'm pulling for him. >> Drake you have Sauce Gardner and Christian Gonzalez and Quinyon Mitchell on your team how much confidence does that give you heading into the season that you can go up against any level of cornerback? >> Yeah I mean I like our guys I mean that's it's pretty simple [snorts] I like our guys and I'm always going to like our guys better than theirs so I think we got a chance to you know do a lot of a lot of things in the passing game and we got to you know find ways to get you know different guys the ball and we've done that throughout camp so we got to keep on building on that but you know I think there's a lot of great defensive players in this league and you know we got some good ones on our side. >> Drake do you have any say in how much you get to play in these preseason games and how much do you feel like you take away from your appearances in preseason games? >> Um no I I think you you take it back to looking at my Eagles preseason game my rookie year there was some great you know things that you learn and you know learn about you know being in the huddle and kind of the operation and you know being in a stadium with the play clock and little things like that and obviously coming in my third year I got you know a lot of that kind of understand what it's like and you know really I'm just you know here with the here with the guys and and trying to get better and whatever they think you know with the preseason I'm here to play and and ready to go out and whatever they think I'm kind of you know here for them and here for this team. >> How would you describe your mindset this year when it comes to scrambling? Is it different than than last year? Is it just in when needed? How would you describe how you're going to approach that this year? >> Biggest thing is trying to remain a passer as long as I can You know, trying to remain a passer and and kind of move them to throw instead of kind of always tucking it early and and doing some things, but there's a lot of great quarterbacks in this league that are really effective outside of the pocket and are doing some great things on pump faking and little things like that. So, um I think I need to, you know, focus on you know, trying to you know, execute the plat passing game plays first and when the pocket breaks down or when I feel like I can go make a play, you know, just kind of do what I have been doing and it's just kind of play ball and and be natural. But, I think that's the biggest thing. Um you know, really other than that, you know, these these guys, I think practicing scrambles is really a different deal and you got to have some reps at that. So, I'll continue to work on it and uh just know that, you know, when you get the ball out on time, that's always better. So, thank you.

He called himself a Buck for life, and he said uh people say home is where your heart is, and my heart is in Tampa. >> I love that. And yes, everybody in Tampa is very happy to hear that. And yeah, I just loved all the social media reaction. It's just been amazing. And you know, I I think that I'm really excited about this defense this year, and he is where it starts. That he is the force to be reckoned with, and I'm sure what I loved to see in the reaction from his teammates, too, that Calijah put up something showed the kid dancing with excitement. Alex Anzalone did the same thing, and it's because they know him coming back makes them better. >> Oh, yeah. Especially those two guys in particular. >> Yes, I would agree with that. And so, yeah, I think that this is just it's the outcome we all wanted. We're thrilled. He was not practicing still today. They're going to ramp him back up coming off of that back injury. And Coach Bowles said he's not going to play in this preseason game, but >> Or the next one. >> or the next one, but that they're they're fully preparing to get him ramped up before week one. >> And he's in good shape. Everybody him and Coach Bowles will say he's in great shape. So, >> Which is great. >> Yeah, and and he played last It's kind of sneaky. Last year he played his career high in snaps and snap percentage on defense. And and he now he's in some of the best shape of his career. So, there's every reason to expect him to be the linchpin of that front. And think about how deep that defensive interior defensive line now is after the you know hopefully Calijah meets his goal of playing 17 games. You added Akiem Robinson and Rakeem Nunez-Roches and Demar Ikepare. I mean, we can bring bring them at you in waves. >> Yeah. Yeah, which is especially nice to keep everybody fresh, keep everybody in that fourth quarter ready to go that when you have that kind of depth, like how how great to feel like you can just >> weeks two, three, four in a row at Raymond James Stadium in September. >> And it's going to be a little toasty, a little toasty outside. All right, so that of course was the big news we wanted to start off the show with, but we did also want to look back at the preseason game from last week. We have not had a show since, and so wanted to talk about that, and especially just some of the standouts from that and and every year I love when maybe I don't know if unexpected is the right word, but guys that are not your your first or second round draft pick have just these huge games of you know, undrafted rookies, guys that you know are just fighting for those spots, fighting for their lives and they have these standout moments and this game felt like it was the the textbook example of that. >> And it's it's great also when it's guys that have been standing out in training camp and you've been noticing them and you're like and as coach Bowles often says, what's it going to look like in a game? And when the lights went on, some of these guys really performed as well as they've been or better than they've been performing on in training camp practices and I think coach Bowles said it well in his postgame press conference when asked about how important this process is not only of just the draft, but those key hours right after the draft when you're on the phone trying to nail down your priority undrafted free agents and we've seen it here year after year that some of those guys make the team and and make an actual impact as rookies. So let's hear what coach had to say about that. >> I mean that's huge, you know, that's the part that goes unseen and you never hear about these guys. I think Jason and his staff does a great job doing the little things and after the draft is over finding the right guys and that's hard to do in free agency with the money going everywhere and guys being picked by every team, but the final right guys for our team and bring them in and trust them to learn the system and the coaches putting them to work and putting them in the right position. He was definitely a priority for the Bucks who wanted to get more quarterbacks to develop, you know, and got him out of Kansas after a long career there. Sorry, sorry Casey. And he ran a couple times cuz he's kind of a dual threat quarterback. He ran a couple times including one really nice scramble for a third down, but I think what really impressed the coaches as coach Bowles in particular more was the plays that he made in structure cuz we know he can run. And he talked after the game about how um >> [music] >> coach Whitmer and coach Yates and coach Robinson have all worked with him a lot about these are his his words about ironing out some bad habits from college. Yeah, I felt like his arm strength was shown off as well, which I I will admit I didn't know as much what that was in terms of like he's got a got an arm for sure. Well, uh Tony Castricone caught up with him as well to to chat about that first preseason game. So, let's listen to that interview now. >> What's up, crew? Tony Castricone with star of the show from the first preseason game against the Jets, Jaylen Daniels, our quarterback who led the comeback charge in New York. What was that like for you, your first NFL game? And and just take me through what what the pregame and and getting the mental right was like for you? >> Yeah, I mean, great experience. Um you know, always had the dream of being able to play in the NFL since I was 7 years old. And uh to be able to make that that little Jaylen Daniels proud, um it meant a lot. And I knew that um going into the game that I was going to get opportunity to be able to play NFL football. So, at the end of the day it was about me being able to go out there with all the guys that I've been working with since getting here, play my heart out. And I know those guys were fighting for me, so I was going to go out there and put everything on the line for them. >> All right, you come into the game in the second half. It's 13 to 10 Jets at that point. And you're facing a big third and 13. Take me through that big completion to Green for 35 yards cuz that really was the spark. >> Absolutely. Um so, I mean, we had a play where he was running basically like a very deep curl. Um and as I'm dropping back, if they were in a two high, I was supposed to get off of it. And when I seen that corner come down to the flat and that linebacker in the middle, I knew that they were posted to be in a cover two. But as I'm dropping back, I seen that their safety that was supposed to be over the top didn't get over. So, um I kind of was just sitting there like Greeny I hope you see what I see and he ended up turning around being able to find that open grass. So leads that touchdown drive but then caps off a touchdown drive later in the game to really take the score from a one point game to an eight point game. You found the end zone for the first time in the NFL. What was that moment like for you? >> I mean great. To be able to know that my my parents my whole entire family was in the stands and they came out here to they well they went out to New Jersey for the very first NFL game. So it was kind of just everything in the moment just all hit at once. Coach T.J., Coach Chandler, Coach Z Rob. Just continue to be able to talk ball with them, be able to get a better grasp of of NFL ball knowledge from a defensive perspective and from an offensive perspective. Just being able to make sure that we're going out there preparing as we are right now to be able to go out there and execute the game plan and I got high hopes for our offense because of how much that we've done during this off season. So, I'm very interested and ready to go be see our offense go out there and make plays. I'm excited. >> All right, crew. Get to know him. Number 10. He's a proud Jayhawk. Jaylen Daniels. >> Indeed. Go Bucks. >> I'm noticing now Tony seemed to bring up the Jayhawk thing on purpose. I'm starting to feel piled on here. I need to get more Mizzou people in my media orbit here to have my back, but >> to try to >> Look, here's the deal. Jaylen I I I told him this. I told his family this. I didn't want to like him. Didn't want to like him. I can't help it and I said that's the greatest compliment I can give is as a Mizzou person, I like the Kansas guy. So, that was great. Very cool to hear about him having his whole family there and just what an experience that was. You know, he he diagnosed and was right and he jumped the route and made the play and nice return. So, this is a guy that's showing you that he's doing well in the mental side of the game as well. >> Yeah, that's going to be really interesting to watch him continue on. So even earning a spot like that is a huge success for any player in Jack Pyburn's situation. >> Yep I agree. All right well we wanted to talk a bit about just kind of where we're at at this point. So wanted to fill you guys in a bit on the schedule what the team is doing this last week this upcoming week. So what is the schedule been like for them this week in the way they're sort of prepping for this preseason game? >> So they had four straight practices from Monday through Thursday. They kind of shortened it up today. I'm sure that was a reflection of that because you usually don't have four practices in a row. They will run like what they call a mock game tomorrow which is just basically a walk through and they get most of that day off and then you you know you have the home opener against the Chiefs on Saturday where the starters are expected to play at least some including Baker Mayfield. It wasn't It was with the Jets in doing in New Jersey. Yeah, we have done a great job in years past of building a lot of that practice squad from some of these guys and I think for the practice squad is so big now, you do get to keep a lot of those people. >> 53 plus 17, we're keeping 70 of these guys probably close to it. >> Um it's also the day though that I don't envy Jason Licht's job. Don't want to have to do that. I'd never cut anybody. This would be my problem. Um all right, so now let's look ahead to this next preseason game. You know, we did the players that stood out in the last one. Thought we'd look at some players that we're excited to watch this weekend and it's different from this last game in the sense that you are going to have your starters play and so that's kind of that mixes things up a bit for this game and I think that it's cool always in these games when you get a chance to see starters, other guys fighting for positions. Like this is going to be a fun game for Bucs fans to get to have kind of all of that that you want in a preseason game. So, we each chose one offense and one defensive guy we're excited to watch Saturday. Who are your people that you chose and why? >> Well, I'm going on offense with Kenneth Gainwell. Um we're all excited about what Bucky can do hopefully with better health fortunes this year, but to have that compliment with Kenneth Gainwell. He looks He has looked really good in training camp. Just so smooth in his routes and his his run after the catch and um he looks a lot like he did when he was Pittsburgh Steelers MVP last year and if I thought he was practicing well, you should you should hear Baker Mayfield and what he had to say about him. He used an interesting word to describe it. So, actually let's go ahead and listen to it. >> I mean, he's much more than a gadget guy. I I've just been completely overwhelmed with the amount of talent that he has. know, I I didn't know until a little later in the spring, more towards mini camp, that he was a receiver going into college. He was a slot receiver at Memphis, and that explains why he's so smooth running routes. Uh and just his run game, he he stays true to his tracks. He reads his blocks really, really well. Um I thought he's been, you know, he a huge addition for us, but just another spark to give Bucky a spell. And then obviously you still have Tuck in there, and and Josh Williams has had a great camp as well, but but KG is another guy that's just a a veteran presence, a leader, a guy that leads by example, and uh continues to help set the tone for us on offense. >> Yeah, I thought that was fascinating to hear. As soon as I heard that soundbite, I was like, "Oh, we have to play this in our show." It was >> Overwhelming >> overwhelming talent. And I love the way he described how he didn't know about him being a wide receiver in his past, and then suddenly he was like, "Ah, >> Now I get it. >> Now I understand. This makes a lot of sense. Um >> Very cool. >> Yeah, so it's always cool to hear, you know, your your quarterback gush about one of his offensive weapons that way. And uh so that you you took Gainwell, which frankly >> Yeah, I went first. Just for the record, I went first. >> to choose first, and so I was like, "Well, that's >> In both of these, by the >> I would have also chosen, but that's fine. Um you know, I decided since you kind of went the more starter type, you know, route, I would go with one of the people kind of trying to make the team who's really using preseason for these things. And I decided I'm excited to watch Britain Sharp. >> Well, he'll play a lot. >> He'll play for sure. And I think that it's just cool to watch some of these later round draft guys, and I just think he's such an interesting story of, you know, was the the high school quarterback, only got one offer somewhere to play quarterback, decides, "You know what? This doesn't seem like this is really working out. I'm going to transition to tight end." And I just always find it fascinating when somebody's able to transition positions and have the kind of success that you can make it to the NFL when there's all these people who've played it so much longer than you. And >> Kind of doesn't seem fair. >> I know, right? Like, how are you this good at these many things? >> a quarterback and a tight end, >> It's so true. So I I I was able to talk to him a little bit today as well and he talked about the fact that um he's just working on those little details and because he was a little later to the position but then you know, learning the playbook and I've heard a lot of guys say man, they're really impressed with how quickly he's picked it all up and we know Zach Robinson seems to like using tight ends and that it seems like he really has the right mentality and I saw him make to me a great catch this last game and lower that shoulder between a couple guys and I'm like you know what that doesn't look like a quarterback. >> Yeah. >> That looks like a guy that is fully embraced the tight end role at this point and I just think he's he's going to be a fun one to watch. You know, that Baker's talked about him too of thinking man, the way he's able to his route running, his catch ability, his catch radius like he's just someone that seems like he has a pretty potentially high ceiling and I'm I'm excited to watch him. >> five targets in the game and four catches and the only one that wasn't a completion kind of went up his hands but that was on the very next play they went back to him on the play you're talking about and he picked up a big first down and that set us up for the next play for a touchdown. It was a really good play. So I agree with you on that. He >> really liked that they went right back to him especially again as a young guy as a rookie like [music] knowing he was probably frustrated with that first play. I love that they were like, nope, we're going to go right back to him let him redeem that moment and he did and I thought that was again a good sign for the the mental strength there. >> a lot because we're we're excited about the starters playing but they're probably not going to play a ton. >> Right. title: Benjamin Morrison & Kam Johnson on Perfecting Craft | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: How y'all doing today? Good to know. >> Cam, how's the camp going for you? I know it's a battle, but there's a lot of competition going on. How do you feel you're doing? >> I mean, every NFL organization have competition. I mean, everybody's in the NFL for a reason. So, there's going to be competition every position. But, it's been going real good. I mean, this by far been the hottest week though. Jesus Christ, but it's been really good. It's been good to see everybody make plays out there. Everybody's like taking it serious, taking advantage of opportunities cuz they know what's at stake. So, we trying to, you know, everybody's coming together as one team, one sound. So, it's going to spawn pretty good. >> With some of the vets being out, you've gotten a lot of opportunity. >> I'm excited. I mean, that's all the game of football is though. It's just always next man up, you know. I mean, the game we play, you know, it's a it's the greatest game ever, but it's also physically taxing on us. So, you just got to take advantage of opportunities that's given to you. >> What do you think of Danny Smith and how he operates the special teams? >> Danny is a lunatic. >> [laughter] >> But, Danny is like really good though. I mean, he he has a way with things. You know, he's really dialed in on what, you know, he's really dialed in on like improving this special teams unit from last year cuz you know, we really struggled in that area. So, I'm excited to work with Danny. Excited to see what he does for and for this organization. >> Cam, what's the mentality as a returner? I mean, it's like a a kamikaze for you every single time. What it has to be your mentality in terms of contact and how do you how do you see it? >> Got to have You got to be fearless back there, you know. You got to be able to just soon as you get the ball, see see where you're going immediately. You just got to trust it, you know. You got to trust the guys that's blocking for you. You got to trust that scheme's going to work. You know, you just got to trust your ability at the end of the day. It's God given. So, you just use what God has given you, you >> What's your first key like once you receive, say a punt return, that you're trying to read off the in terms of what you're doing? >> Yeah. Uh usually I always start off with the alignment of the kicker to see if he's offset or if he's right behind the center cuz that usually tell where the ball's going to go. Then, I look at the release of the gunners. You know, those are the first first people down there. So, as long as we hold them up, I got a chance. So, they go anywhere, I know where the ball is going. I just need them to hold it. That's all I say. I say, as long as you hold them two people up, I'm fine. That's all I need is someone just to get it started. So, that's really just the keys I look at. >> And how do you handle keeping your eye on the ball and watching the gunners? Like, how does that work? >> As soon as I hear the ball kicked, I'm looking straight at the ball. I I already got my keys from like if they held them up or not cuz you see it right at the line of scrimmage. So, if they didn't hold them up, you kind of got tell on it, but you know, I got people saying the sideline, you good, you good, but sometimes I don't hear them. So, you just really got to periph, but I'm really focused on the ball at the end of the day. So, cuz that's that's the money maker, you know? >> Hey Cam, is there a particular part of your game that you feel like you want to get better from last season to this season? >> Uh yeah, just turning them long returns into touchdowns. >> You get to work with Jaylen Daniels at Kiwi as well as Kanye Davis. Like, how are those two playing and how are you getting along with the way they're playing the game? >> Both of them are great. They're fun to be around, you know, they really take the game serious. They they take it They both are different. They take different approaches to the game, you know, Jaylen's kind of more goofy, but he's a he's a he brings the energy, you know. Davis is like more like silent killer, you know what I'm saying? But both though both play tremendous ball. Both both really catch the ball. So, it's it's good to work with both of them. It's exciting to work with both of them. >> Coming out of 2025, what did Coach McMillan want you to work on the most this offseason? >> Uh you know, blocking honestly cuz that's what will be my role on the offensive side is to be that blocker. So, that's really what it is. So, that's why I put on a little bit more more muscle. >> How much are you looking forward to Saturday? Just another preseason game against the Falcons. >> Any chance you get a opportunity to play the game, especially at this level, is is a blessing. So, I'm really just out there just to I'm grateful, especially where I come from. I mean, it's a blessing just to be here. Just to be able to practice, be able to stand and play in that stadium is a blessing. So, I'm just really excited for it. >> Cam, you had a really good route today on Hayden Goins. It seemed like a little far away from us, but it seemed like it was 24. >> Yeah. >> What are your thoughts on on Gardner? He's getting more opportunities and you go against him quite a >> He's good. I mean, he's a really good cover corner. You know, you could tell he's really He's a smart corner, too. So, he knows the situation. He knows what to do. He knows what to expect. That's why he made that big play against the Jets cuz usually third and long, that's usually the offense trying to get to the sticks. So, he knew that. So, he's a very good situationally smart corner. So, he's going to be exciting to watch. >> Who's the fastest receiver? >> Fastest? It's got to be between me and Teague, I would >> I know. >> Yeah. Teague Teague can Teague can roll, but Teague can Teague can roll, too, though. So, >> What about Houston? >> Dennis, that's my guy. Houston, he He only has one speed and that's just full throttle like pedal to the metal like Dennis works his tail off every day. Everybody in the building loves Dennis. Like he's amazing. So, Dennis got some wheels, too. So, I mean, we all had to like race. I got money on me. >> Coming to the season, do you have any personal goals? >> Yes. Uh as a team, obviously to get back in the playoffs, make a deep run, hopefully win a Super Bowl. But also, you know, as a person as personal, I'm trying to, you know, be top 10 returner or top five returner. Try to get at least five plus touchdowns in the return game this year. And, you know, do the best I can. Especially and on Gunner, I'm trying to get at least five tackles. It's hard hard as crap to tackle returners in this league. So, that's my personal goals. >> Cameron, you got Kenny Gainwell in here now and he did a lot for the Eagles in the return game. >> Amazing. >> Picked his brain a little bit on on stuff? >> Yeah, you know, every time we do some kick returns, I'm always back there talking about what you see and what you read about there cuz, you know, he was with Danny last year. So, obviously Danny's a I mean, y'all know all about Kenny. He's a tremendous talent. So, he'll be a really good asset in the return game. >> We saw you used a lot of different ways last year in the offense. You had Zach Robinson. Uh I mean, you were doing that, too, with the jet sweeps and different things that you can do out there. >> Yeah. Uh Zay Jones has done an amazing job so far. You know, his offense, I talked to the defense last year, they was like they hate playing against the Atlanta Falcons cuz you know they use so many different formations. You know, so Z Rob knows what he's doing, so I think Z Rob is using my skill set differently that has been that has been used. I'm really looking forward to working with Z Rob. Obviously, the jet sweeps and you know, you know, stretching the defense laterally. I'm very excited to work with Z Rob. >> Anything else? All right, thank you guys. >> Appreciate y'all. Thank you all. >> How you doing? >> How is it How you feeling? How's How's it been frustrating not being able to be out here as much as you want? >> Yeah, I mean this is a game I love. Um, game I grew up playing since I was like 6 years old. Um, uh, when I miss every when I when I miss those snaps and those times out here, you just appreciate even more when you come back, but yeah, I mean it's it's frustrating. Um, it's it's it's just you you want to you want to do what you love. Um, and when it's taken from you, um, on a consistent basis, it sucks, but um, it just builds character. >> What are you dealing with? >> Uh, I mean we're we're just ramping up right now. Um, the the team has a great plan for me. Um, so I mean the the biggest thing is trusting them and that's what Bobby's been relaying in my ears is trust the process. Um, so since day one of camp, they've had a a very like methodical plan laid out for me. Um, some days you you want to you want to do a little more. Um, but I mean you got to trust the process and it got me where I'm at right now. Um, out there feeling great. Um, so just taking taking it all in, appreciate even more. Um, so yeah. >> Benjamin, you were out here today in team drills. How did that feel for you and then you can give me your kind of availability for you to play on Saturday night? >> Yeah, it felt great. Um, that's still TBD. Um, talking with them what's the best plan as we said, I mean we're taking it day by day. Um, I mean this is the best I felt in a in a while. Um, and they they've done a great job with my body. Um, I'm in a great head space, mental space. I'm just excited for what is to come um, and just thanking God through it all. >> Are you concerned at all about falling behind with everyone else getting reps? >> No, I'm not concerned. I mean just the the competitor in you obviously wants to be out there. Um and like like like everyone knows like there's a difference from being out there. Those game reps, those flying bullets, you got to make decisions and you kind of see what you're made of. So, I mean, obviously um I'm not going to be um at my best at day one, but that's the beauty about the process and I think that's just uh what I've been holding in on is just like I may not be there day one, um but uh eventually I'm going to get there um and I I'm going to I'm going to stay when I get there. >> Who have you been leaning on throughout kind of all of this? >> Yeah, my my faith has been huge for me um because I mean, like you guys know, it's frustrating. Um I I don't plan on getting injured, you know, I don't plan on wanting to get hurt. Um but that's just how the way the chips have fallen, but I think the the person I've had to become, the man I've had to become, the husband I've had to become through all this, I mean, it's just changed my perspective. Um and it made me to appreciate this even more, but I think another guy is Vita. Um I've been able to uh lean on him a lot. He he's been someone who I've who's really uh taken the time to ask questions. I can lean on him and ask him things. Um and then my parents. I mean, at the end of the day, uh that's that's that's what matters most your close circle and they helped me a lot. >> When you say day one, do you mean week one or game day? >> What do you mean? >> I you you referenced the day one, you may not be ready day one. >> No, no, I said I was talking about day one of camp. Like I'm not going to be where everyone else is at cuz he asked me um but I forget. He asked me about falling behind. Yeah, yeah, falling behind. I was talking about day one of camp. So, yeah. >> What did you think when you heard the news of Vita signing? >> I was I was stoked. I mean, he's it's well deserved. Um I mean, he's a staple of this team. This This dude has put his blood, sweat, and tears into this organization. Um and I'm just happy that it got done and we got we got a great player back. >> You guys have been side by side the whole time when you mentioned he helped you out. >> So, so in what ways does does he help you out to do that? >> I mean, just just an ear to talk to. Um I think in a lot of in the in the world we live in, it can be like a lot of like in one ear out the other, but to really have someone who really cares about you. I mean, that's why he's a the Um I mean, I I I dream of being a the that he's in. So, I mean, I just respect him so much as a man and as a person. So, just understand that like he always says tough times don't last. And I've just held on to that. I believe it. I mean, this is just a small time in my in my in my long life. And I'm going to take every opportunity that comes my way and run with it. >> You overcame similar injuries last year. >> You didn't have a training camp after that. >> But you did play. >> What did you learn from the the experience you had out there playing? >> I think the importance of mental reps. I think last year I was young, I was naive. And coming out of college, it's more physical. You know, it's more physical. Um, I'm It's mainly like I line up across from a dude and I'm physically better than you. You know what I'm saying? And now it's like everyone in the league is good. So, it's like how can I, even though I'm not on the field, but how can I still gain these reps off the field? And that's where I feel the biggest jump for me was this year coming to camp. Like I said, still getting to where I want to be, but I feel like I've been able to keep up just off of the mental side of the game. And now my mind is there and I'm getting the body back. >> Were you talking about the challenge the challenge of actually trying to get better as a player? >> Say it again. >> And stay healthy at the same time. >> The challenge of trying to get better as a player from last season to this season and trying to get healthy at the same time. >> Yeah, I mean, it's challenging, but I mean, like I said, like you got to embrace it. Like this is my story. I I can I can dwell, I can be I can sulk, I can be frustrated, or I can make the most of it. Like at the end of the day, I still have opportunity. I have a great opportunity in front of me playing for a great organization. So, I can't dwell on what if or what could have happened or being mad about my situation. At the end of the day, like this is what the the hand I was dealt with. So, I have to deal with that. Um, and it's just, like I said, it just grows a greater appreciation and just that that hungriness to get back. Like the the desire in me like late nights just staring at the wall just like like waiting for my time to come. Um and it's it's it's in me. Like it's I know what's in me. I know what's to come. Um but you got to believe in yourself before others see it. Um so that that's my mentality is just leaning on my my my supportive ones. >> If you got If you got beat up back, you got your added bang, you got a lot of guys that can rush the passer and get pressure with four. How does that help you guys in the back end? >> Shoot, more balls for us. I mean, that's that's lovely. That's what we like to see. Um go out there and get back there, tipping over those, you know what I'm saying? I love it. So I mean, we have I'm excited about this year. We got great guys um all around the all around the whole team. So I we got a special group. >> Beyond the health aspect, is the goal for you to play in the preseason or you just focus on getting ready for Cincinnati? >> It's day by day. Um like I said, it's it's a blessing I made it through today, you know what I'm saying? Like that's that's your mentality. Like in everything you do in life, I mean, if we look a year from now, I mean, who knows what could happen? I mean, the world could end. I could die. You know what I'm saying? Something like that. It's just the reality of it. Um so the more and more you look on just causes more stress and anxiety that you just don't need to need to have. Um that's that's what these injuries taught me the most like just control what you can control. I can't control if I play this week, next week, week one. My goal is just to be the best version of myself, get back out there, and play the ball I know I can play. >> Beyond the health aspect, 2025 you had an up and down year for you. The Eagles game was fantastic a little bit later. seemed like you had some some struggles there. What were some of the aspects of your game that you were trying to improve over the off season beyond just trying to get healthy? >> Yeah, I think watching the guys who do does it well. I think we have great guys on our team who I who I was able to watch and then even Jamel Dean. I think uh he's an like an exceptional corner. He's amazing corner. And I was able to pick his brain, ask him questions, see how he plays. He just makes the game so easy. And then I have guys like Jacob and Zion who are stellar corners as well that my dad always says like watch them. Like you know what I'm saying? Like like watch them. Like see what they do well. Like mimic them. You know what I'm saying? Like and then add your flavor to it. Um and that's my mentality. Like, I'm not pressing to uh be great day one. You know what I'm saying? Like, your your your your goal is to get better every single day. Um and my goal is to reach greatness one day. Um but probably you you never will reach that, I feel like. You're always going to keep striving for it. Um so, that's in my mentality. Just like watching the the people who do it right on a consistent basis. Watching the great corners in the NFL do it right. Um watching a just tire tireless amount of film. So, yeah. >> Was there something specific that Jamel gave you that you're trying to implement this year? >> Yeah, I think for me is just put myself in a in a winning position from the start. You know what I'm saying? I think you can eliminate yourself off of a uh a leverage or position. And and last year like I I like we know like bullets were flying. You know what I'm saying? Like, rookie year uh missed some missed some time. So, I just wanted to make every play. You know what I'm saying? I I felt like I could make every play. But, that's not the league. The league is just letting your plays come to you. Being in the right position. And then when your when your time comes, it'll come. >> Couple more. >> Team goals aside, are there any personal goals you're trying to achieve this year? >> Uh I think I'll just keep that within. You know what I'm saying? I I I know what I want to achieve. I know what I'm working for. Um so, I'll leave that for you guys to wonder and for me to to know. >> Benjamin, you're on the other side and haven't been out there to face him, but early thoughts on Ted Hersey. What kind of player is he and >> Yeah, I mean, he's first off he's a great person. Um I think that's what people don't know a lot just cuz you're not in the locker room and stuff, but the the dude's a great guy. Like, funny dude. Um just a stand-up guy. And I mean, his his play speaks for himself. I mean, he's long. He's rangy. Um can run. Can catch. Catch radius is uh insane. Um so, I was kind of excited um during OTAs to start matching up against him. And then in camp, he's been able to take off um and take his game to that next level. He's going to have be a great NFL receiver. Um and I'm excited for the battles um for the years to >> You've got some new coaching this year. So, I could take me through We hear more aggressive. What does that mean in terms of a corner? Does that mean jumping more routes? Are they allowing you to take more chances? What's what's the mental side? >> I think it's just thinking the game within the game. I think that's the biggest thing is just like you know where you have to be on the field but like being able to put yourself like we said in that position to make a dominant play. You know what I'm saying? So like the aggressiveness comes from the the pre-snap and like really understanding what is this offense trying to do to us? How are they trying to attack us? And that that that's been huge for us. >> All right, thank you. >> Thank you.

title: Vita Vea on His New Extension: ‘My Heart is in Tampa’ | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: How is your back? >> Huh? >> How is your back? >> My back? Uh it's It's a little tight, but it's feeling good right now. >> Giannis, how difficult was it to go through this process? I know you you know you didn't want to be traded and then you ultimately ended up staying here. I'm guessing that was your preference is to remain with the Bucks. >> Look, uh I always wanted to be a Buck. And I wanted to be a Buck for life. That's why I'm glad that we were able to we were able to get this done. Um it's something that happens every year. Just so happened to be me this year. Um but there's just stuff that we both had to figure out on both sides and we got it all squared away, so I'm happy we can put that all behind us and move forward from here on out. >> It was reported being that you asked for a trade. Was that report accurate? >> Uh I don't know. It's all behind us now. >> Is this just part of the business? >> Yeah, it's just all part of business. Um I never did I got drafted here. Um this is I made my home. I made Tampa my home. Uh I love it here. The guys on the team are like brothers to me. We look at each other as family, so um I didn't I didn't want to be a I didn't want to leave that and leave that behind and switch teams and get traded, so that was never the the end goal for me. I always wanted to be here. >> Jeff Weltman said a couple weeks ago that you know he didn't have any plans to trade you. Did Were you always confident that this was going to work out? >> Um yeah. That's one of I'm the type of person I am, I'm always like a I'm a big optimistic type of guy, so I always err on the side of optimism. And uh I had a good feeling that we'd get something done. >> You've been out there watching, especially all these new guys with Biyombo and everybody. How excited are you to be part of that. >> I'm really excited. Um I think the we have another a few new pieces in our in our room in the D-line and then obviously in the outside backer room. Um just seeing those guys and just being able to get close with them and pick everybody's brain. It feels good to just feel the camaraderie of everybody. It definitely what I've seen so far is definitely exciting to to be a part of this. I think there's we have something special here especially in our in our room. So you definitely feel that when you're out there in practice watching these guys and >> [snorts] >> hearing or feeling the energy that they bring to every day in the practice. So it definitely feels good on my side to be able to be a part of that and be able to contribute. >> You appear to be in really good shape but then there's football shape. So what's the process going forward? How do you feel physically and just what I guess the goal is Cincinnati, right? >> Uh yeah, that's the end goal but I feel great. You know I've been doing this for 9 years now so you kind of you kind of understand what to do. So I feel like the callus of the of of hitting people is still there. I feel like it never really leaves. It's it's it's in you but I've been in good shape. I have a good team and surrounded around me. So I feel like I'm ready to go good to go. So >> [sighs] >> we'll see how it goes. I don't know the plan yet. We'll still be able to discuss that over next few days and figure out from there. >> Vita, you've been off to the side and you know watching this defensive line room. What have you seen from Calijah Kancey and it seems like you know Bowles has talked about him stepping up as a leader. You lost Lavonte David on that side. Do you see that coming out with Kancey? >> Calijah's always been that guy since day one since he's since he's been here. He's always been Um that's what has always surprised me about him. He's always been as good as he is as a player. He's always been that vocal guy in the room. Which you don't really get from a bunch of young guys, but he's always been he's always been the voice in our room and making sure um to communicate and uh I think he picked up a lot of things >> over the few years that that's helped him out to in today's in his in his game today. So it's it's it's definitely exciting to see what he has in store for him in the future. I think he has a the the the roof is the sky is the ceiling for him. So I'm just excited to see him um ball out this year. >> Khalil gave you a high five when you came out onto the field this morning. A couple coaches were dapping you up. Just talk about what they were saying to you, how happy they are to have you back in the fold. >> Um yeah, I got a bunch of congratulations this morning. Um that's all it was. It feels good to you to um to feel the love from everybody. You know, sometimes you want to feel wanted, so to feel that love just felt good. >> Defensive tackles have gotten new contracts and and the money for that position went up. Obviously, that's why you're standing here today. Um how good is it to see that position recognized that way throughout the league with the stuff that you've been able to do as well? >> Um it's just it it feels really good to um get that recognition. Especially hats off to those guys. You know, they're hell of a players. Or but you know, I just >> they're just in today's game is just you know, you I feel like uh a lot of the work we do we do a lot of dirty work, so it it feels good to get recognized for it. >> Yeah, how important was it for you to be out there during this entire process with the guys? >> Say that again, start over. >> How important was it for you to be out there during this entire process with the guys as they're doing drills, talking up some of the young players. As a leader for this team, what was that like to you for to continue not being on the sideline, not being, you know, sitting out, you were sitting in, you were here. How important was that for you? What Where was that priority for you? >> Um that was really important for me because obviously, one, I know the defense. I've been in this defense for 8 years now. So, um I think it was it was good for me to be able to get some more recall on it, but also be able to help the new guys on the on the on the front and be able to teach them um the nuances and stuff that they don't really know about the defense. So, um there's little details and stuff that that go a long way that I've learned over the years and was able to figure out in this defense that to be able to share that know- knowledge with them and be here. Um [snorts] I feel like it was important to me to to be there for them and to be able to help them out that way and also learn from them from what they're seeing out there and what what they're doing, just watching them. I feel like we're always a student of the game, so you can never be you can never you can never be I feel like you always got to be humble and be able to willing to learn uh no matter how how long you play in this league. >> What was that like for you um because you love playing football and you also love your teammates. You're always pouring yourself into helping them. Um but to not physically participate because of the business side of things. >> Uh during this during this whole process, there's definitely highs and lows. some days are harder than others. Uh but you know, that's what you have your teammates here for. They're here they have my back the whole time. So, it was good to good to be here for them and I had it was good for me to have them uh knowing they have my back. >> And Jimmy Morrison, we talked to him earlier and he said that you really helped him during, you know, his his journey. What advice did you give him and um how have you guys kind of become close? >> Um, you know, uh, Bemo, he's he's he's dealt with a lot in the past year or so, and as as uh as an older guy in this league, um, you look at this game, it's like no one no one's going to leave this game unscathed, so everybody deals with injuries. So, it's just you understand the process of everything, so being able to see and understand what he's going through, it's just I think just being there for someone like that and just trying to help him out through this process, uh, just I feel like speaks volume, so I think I'm just trying to be there for my teammates and be able [snorts] to give him a path to help him be the best they could be. >> From a negotiation standpoint, probably a better idea of what Baker's going through right now than anybody because he's trying to get a new contract, too, and he stood up here and was singing your praises and advocating for you to get a new deal. Uh, what can you say about Baker and what he means to this team and and, you know, him potentially getting a new deal? >> Uh, you know, Baker's the heart and soul of this team. You know, you see the energy he brings uh, on game day, so you know, we feed off of that, too, not only the offense. So, um, you know, I hope things get figured out with him. Uh, I know we would all love to have him. Everybody loves Baker. And that's something that you you wish to have on your side on game day. >> Do you have a thought beta on what went wrong with last season and what'll be the biggest positive difference this year? >> Uh, there's a bunch of stuff. I feel like, uh, kind of want to set the record straight. I feel like there's a lot of a lot of stuff going about on Boles. I feel like none of it is Boles' fault, and I feel like we all love Boles. You can ask every player in the locker room. So, that's one thing I want to set the record straight as we all love Boles. It's not, um, it's not what he's doing. You know, he's telling us what to do. He's giving us all the all the answers to the test. And it's it's [snorts] on us players to be able to go out there and execute what he's telling us to do. So, um he's always putting us in the best position to play. So, that's one of the main things. Just being able to take coaching and and that light. So, if anything is on blame us players for not for not executing. Bowles Bowles puts us in the best position to to win games. I even told Bowles that the day he retires the day I retire. >> Baker had said regarding his own negotiations that the length of contract was really important to him. When it comes to the negotiations that you had with the team, obviously there are a lot of different things that go into that. What was your biggest priority? You only got one extra year on the extension. Was length a little less important to you so much as being recognized in terms of the the APY as one of the five best defensive tackles in the NFL? >> Um you know, you you love to get um that's just one of those things you love to get compensated and and feel that your work is uh appreciated. Um obviously in this league the market goes up um and and that's what happened. So, he just had We just had to work some things out and we ended up getting it resolved. >> Specifically, what have you seen from Reuben Bain and what do you think he can bring to this defense? >> Uh shoot, Reuben's a complete pro. you just see it day in and day out. I think there's videos of him. You see him out there by himself, but he does a lot more behind the scenes when nobody's around. And just seeing how he carries himself, you don't really see that in a bunch of young guys. So, um just seeing the hunger and determination in his eyes, it's just it's good to have on your side and just um he knows so he already knows so much of the game. So, just talking to him about about football, that's at least in my world it's about him, so I feel like he has so much upside and we're glad to have him. Um I feel like everybody who passed up on him on the draft made a mistake. >> What have you noticed from D-line coach Marcus West and what he's brought to the team since being here? >> Uh we all love Marcus, man. Marcus brought brings a lot of energy to us in our room. you know, he's very relatable to us. He played back in the day, so it's always good to have um a coach that, you know, has been through what we've been through, so I'm able to see and able to relate to him. So, I feel like it's as as a good thing for us uh in our D-line room be able to learn from him as well. Uh All right. >> You said you wanted to retire Buccaneer. What is it about this organization that makes it home for you? >> Um it's just one of those things, you know, they took a chance on me in the draft and I've been here ever since and uh it's just I fell in love with Tampa. I fell in love with my teammates. You know, I love the organization. Everybody works here. you know, I walk around every day with my with a smile on my face and I I feel like it just speaks volume to everybody who works here and and and my teammates, so I just they say uh home is where the heart is and I feel like my heart is in Tampa. >> You talked about coach coach Bowles and saying his praises and then you also talked about the people in this organization that every day they they were coming up to you and talking to you and making you feel wanted. I noticed coach Bowles was doing that every day. I understand you guys were talking every single day. Just what did it mean to you the fact that your head coach was continuing to check in on you and make sure you were okay throughout this process and making sure you did feel wanted? >> Um yeah. Me and Bowles Bowles are we we had a level of understanding. Every day we talked. It mainly be about football. Um Um Sometimes sometimes we do not practicing, you see a lot more of of everything that's going on, so it's basically just being able to pick his brain and see what he's thinking on certain plays and able to help me out in the long run with when we get things rolling here in the season. So, it was just it was it was cool to be able to stand next to him in practice and stuff and be able to learn even more from him from a a defensive coordinator standpoint, so um yeah. >> Playing inside in a 3-4 offense can attack you a lot of different ways in terms of their blocking structures. Demonte Capehart being a rookie, how have you What kind of conversations have you had with him in terms of being able to pick those up, recognize how they're trying to attack and being able to react to that? >> Uh you know, you when you when you speak to rookies there's a lot of a lot of stuff that they're they're they're dealing with. Um but Demonte's not one of them. He he he's picking up stuff pretty fast, so I'll be able to to help him see the whole game and see everything is just uh one of the biggest things that you try to teach the younger guys. that's when you when you really break down everything, it's like a football is like a chess like a like a chess game and it's like we're out there we're playing chess. So, it's like you're not just looking at the old lineman you're looking at there's tendencies, there's formations, there's you got to look at your play call, what our coverage is and everything. There's so much stuff that goes on in the one play, so be able to help break that down for him and able to >> explain it to him that's one of the biggest things uh trying to pass it down to them. >> Peter, what's been the biggest adjustment for you not having Lavonte David out there and seems like you know, Alex Anzalone's going to have that green dot. What's What have you seen from Alualu? Leading and taking charge, communicating. Is that a big role? >> Uh it was tough. It was tough, but it was a bittersweet moment. Um obviously, he wanted to end on his own terms. I feel like he had an amazing career. I feel like he could have I feel like he had more in him, but you know, I think the time was right for him to retire. It's always hard. Um I played with him my whole career here, so that was definitely tough um for me, but I'm You're always happy for him. He had an amazing career. I feel like uh I wish he got more praise than he did. I feel like uh a lot of people slept on him, but we knew his worth over here. Uh so, that was hard seeing him go, but picking up a linebacker like uh Alualu as it was big for us as well. Uh um I actually have a good relationship with Alex. Um being that he he's he's a local guy, and you know, he's always here in the off season. I see him. We train together sometimes, so uh we already have that relationship, so it just it picked up pretty well when he got here. >> Okay. Thank you. >> Thank you. Appreciate it. >> Appreciate it.

title: Todd Bowles on Vita Vea’s Command of the Defense | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Morning. >> Good morning. >> You work your magic on B to Bay? >> Uh that's the powers that be more or less, so just glad we got some work done. >> Todd, do you have any idea how soon he would get back in the next physical sample? >> Uh we're going to start working him in next week slowly, preparing him for Cincinnati. There's no way he plays against Jacksonville or anything like that, but we're going to acclimate him and kind of work him in trying to get him ready for opening day. >> Was he getting restless at any point like going to the Jason's office saying, "Hey, we need to get this done at some point?" >> No, that never happened. >> How thrilled were you just at all when when you heard the news last night? >> Just Well, when you got a star player, you're happy to have him back on the field, so you know, it's relieving to know that he'll be out there. >> But also the fact too that, you know, he feels it seems like he's he's in good spirits and he feels good about things. >> He's been in good spirits since camp started. >> You've talked about it saying, you know, you can play without him, but you don't want to. Now you don't have to. So, I mean, just how how much are you looking forward to him just, you know, what he brings to that line and the other guys and now you have as depth behind him? >> You know, we know what he brings to our defense. He's the centerpiece of it. Obviously, he's a big part in the run game and the pass rush as well. So, to get him back in the fold and start getting him working in with the other guys is good. >> Todd, it's pretty well known that the last couple of years he's played an awful lot of snaps. That's a good sign for the Raiders that he comes to take care of himself again. >> He takes good care of himself great, and he's in great ever been in. So, that's a credit to him, and you do that to your body, you can play a long time. >> With the way your defense is designed, like he's constantly eating up double teams, but also like, you know, a lot of people know you for the double A gap blitzes and stuff. I mean, he's he's got to be a big part of that. >> He's a big part of everything. Like I said, he's the centerpiece of the defense, and then guys that work around him, but he can do so many things other than to eat up double teams and that he helps us with to win ball games with that, you know, you can't put a price on it. >> Have you heard anything from from Jack Coiner on what his intentions are? text: Hey. >> Uh the pick six you had talking us through and just take us through what what kind of happened there. >> Are you wearing two gloves? >> Yeah, really great call. title: Sam Darnold: "We're Continuing To Find Our Identity" | Seattle Seahawks
text: Like the We met up with the quarterbacks during special teams and before I could say, "Oh, it's hot out here."
