Mike told us, unfortunately, it sounds like Bo Bo's knee injury is serious. >> Yeah. >> I know he's meant a lot to this team for as long as he's been here and longer than I have, but what was it like for you guys to see that? >> It hurts, man, you know. Uh he's just he's one of those guys that just, you know, he works, uh talks a lot of stuff and, you know, he's just one of the like kind of like Spoon in a way, offensively, like he just he he he brings the juice every single day and, you know, he just does his job. So, it's uh it sucks to lose Bo Bo, um but, you know, I know he's going to attack it and be better whenever he comes back. >> Did you get a chance to say anything to him? I know it's the middle of practice. >> What is If the both teams came over when that happened, what you know the NFL game and what is that a reminder of or the just how precious this might be? >> Yeah, I mean, it's uh just like any sport, right? I mean, injuries happen, but, you know, it's just uh just puts everything in perspective, you know, uh you know, he's like I said, he's going to come back better than ever, but you just never know when stuff like that's going to happen, so um you know, you you just every single play, you just continue to push and and give it give it all you can and, you know, that's I know that's all he does and, you know, that's why it's such a shame that it happened to him, but um you know, like I said, I know he'll be back. >> Sam, you had a touchdown to Hollani and a long pass earlier in practice. What do you see out of the running backs, guys like Jones and Hollani? What do you see out of that group as pass catchers? >> Yeah, they're doing a they're doing a great job out of the backfield. Uh Even when they're not out of the backfield in the slot, you know, being able to catch and and do all the things that we ask them to do, you know, obviously in camp some things happen, receivers go down, tight ends go down, full backs go down, and those running backs have been able to just step up in whatever position we ask them to play. So, they've been they've been very versatile camp and and really really good catching the ball out of the backfield and even in in the slot or out wide. >> Where where do you feel like the offense is right now? It's sort of an adapting to the old Brian Flores and maybe some of the tweaks he's made. >> Yeah, we're we're continuing to find our identity. You know, we just I think for us like we got to continue to to detail things up. It's exactly kind of where we were last year. Not exactly, but, you know, it's just during training camp, especially this point in training camp, uh there can be some guys that think they have it figured out and you know, you kind of myself included like you kind of take your foot off the gas a little bit and you're like, all right, we have all the installs in, we, you know, I I I feel like I've been executing at practice. It's like, no, you got to treat every single day like it's your last day out here and that's really my mindset and I know our offense is continuing to to push push tempo and and all those things that we need to do to um you know, continue to have good practices and and build all the way to the season and then when we get in the season, it's the same thing. We just continue to build. >> What are you learning about Flo? Just like personality wise. >> Yeah, he's, you know, still continuing to figure him out and and all those things. He's very stoic, like I said right when right when I met him. So, just you know, I think for for us it's a matter of like just being able to hang out together, you know, whether it's before practice, after practice, in the building and continuing to talk, get to know each other cuz I think the better play callers and quarterbacks know each other, the stronger the relationship is on the field. >> Last year you told us that Clint and Janocko were telling like listen to your feet was the thing that they hammered in you. What are some things that Brian and Jake Peetz are like really harping on? >> Yeah, I think they do a really good job of just reminding us. It's kind of the similar thing but just saying it a different way like progress, you know, continue to to trust your eyes, trust your feet with your progressions. Like if something's not there, move on and and continue to go through your progressions and find the open guy and if it's not there, play play fast, move around and and if it's a throwaway then that's the right play and you always just got to make the right play and and make fast decisions and um you know, and learn from things. I think is also a huge thing. When when you're not sure, you throw the ball away, you know, move on to the next play and we'll correct it when we get back to our meetings. >> You've seen Saleh's defenses when he was in San Fran. Can you it's so early, can you see Saleh's imprint on that Titans defense yet? >> For sure. For sure. I think you see the aggression, you see kind of uh the pressure that they put on the quarterback. Like their their four man rushes are really really good and when they bring five or six man rushes and even when they bring fire zones like they're really really good. You know, they're really the back end's really good at disguising right now. They're you know, showing a lot of different things defensively without getting too far into the weeds but they're doing a lot of great things and you know, that defense is going to be really good this year. >> You mentioned that Jonnu Smith is back in the catching game. Just having him back these last couple days how does it change the offense I guess or what do you notice from >> Yeah, he's a special player. He's a really special player. He He brings a He brings a different facet to the offense that only only a guy like him can bring, you know, whether it's catching passes out of the backfield, catching screens, you know, running in between the tackles, outside the tackles. Um he can really do it all and I know he's he's just going to continue to get better and learn. >> He showed some toughness there got to over the middle and then he hit him a couple plays later, you like seeing a player kind of respond like that. >> Yeah, I mean, it's you know, I I would like to not put a receiver in a situation like that, but I also would have thought the DB wouldn't have hit him, but yeah, I I tried to give him a shot, and the DB made a really good play on it. So, um but the way that Sheed it's not funny, but it's funny in the moment now that he's good, but I went up to him as he was on the ground. I was I was like, "Sheed." He's like, "Ah." I was like, "You get the wind knocked out of you?" He's like, "Yeah." I was like, "All right, you're good." I thought it, you know, maybe would have been something different, but it looked like he just got the wind knocked out of him. So, when he confirmed that, I was felt a lot better. Um not that I want to continue to do that, but um you know, he uh he showed a lot of toughness by by uh getting up. And also, the way that not only him, but our entire receiver group, man, like we had some obviously Bobo go down, some guys cramp up, like we had a lot of receivers getting a lot of reps today in this heat that we're not used to in Seattle. those guys stepped up in a huge way, and they were playing really, really tired, and showed a lot of grit today. >> I'm sorry, Pittsburgh fans, that their DBs had a tough time last week against the 49ers. And how much had [snorts] you looked at maybe Flaherty and Taylor coming into this, or not at all? >> No, yeah, I've, you know, I I've known that they've been really good players in the league, and um shoot, Taylor made a really good play on me in the 2-minute drill. So, um kudos to them, man. They they have really good defensive players, especially in the back end. Um so, yeah, we just got to continue to, you know, um for us as an offense, like we just got to continue to do what we do, but yeah, defensively, you guys looked really good. >> Sam, bigger picture, how do you feel like you guys have dealt with all the stuff that comes with being Super Bowl champions, and the extra attention, and all the all the just the stuff that comes with it? >> Yeah, I think our guys have been good. We got really good leadership to be able to handle stuff like that. text: Curtis, what was your just your general view of the work you guys got today and kind of you know, just going against another team for the ones for the first time this >> Yeah, no, it was good. They're going to find the softness soft, you know, parts in our coverage. So, it's just work, you know. >> What you saw from Kyle Hamilton that they played in the pick six was he's a guy who's, you know, competing last year to take over starting role and do what he's doing. How have you seen him grow since >> Yeah. Yeah, man. We we love Ty. I think where Ty has grown at is he's just more, you know, more in command at in his voice and, you know, speaking up when things aren't right. And he's just also just taking it to the next level to his game, being ahead of plays. Um being that safety in the back that you you you depend on Ty. You know, Ty's going to be where he needs to be. I think that's just where he where he's at in his career and where he's always been. >> Anything else, guys? >> Appreciate y'all. >> Thank you.

title: We NEED to Talk About Tyrice Knight Knight...
text: Mendoza comes in halfway through the year and they look good enough that Max Crosby wants to stay. I don't know. We'll find out, but um what I will say is Tyree Snider came up there. It was It was remarkable to watch a performance like that and I know it's preseason and the the level of opponent he's playing is not very good. So, >> And does he have a sack celebration? Did I hear a rumor? Does he have a >> He does He does >> Is there anything that Seahawks fans can be looking for? >> Yes, it is it is a repeated like it is his kind of go-to sack celebration. Like this is the wrong person to ask this question to, but uh Dante loved it. The next day got a sack, did it, and it's been with him ever since. He also said he really loves getting the crowd into it and you know, the combination of that, a speed rusher, Lumen Field, you know, there were times where it just felt unfair when Cliff Avril and Michael Bennett were rushing the passer in Lumen Field because they were both so quick off the ball. Quick twitch is not his attribute. Uh that is something that Dante Fowler does bring as a former number three overall pick. So, uh you know, I wouldn't say Dante Fowler's been dominating, but I do think that there's evidence of what he can bring and and he's done it enough that I'm not really worried about that. And even his last year, I think I've said this before, his pass rush win rate was higher than any edge player the Seahawks had last year. So, you know, we'll see. We'll see how that translates. But as far as Tyreek's goes, Tyreek's is not a guy with a lot of words, man. He he kind of comes in, he does his job, he loves football. And I think one of the things that really You got to always be careful how much you put into people's Instagram personas, as we should all know, right? And football players, some of them put up all these videos of workouts, and some of them put up videos of them going to clubs, and whatever else, right? Right? But it is, no matter what time of year, no matter what time of day, you will almost always find clips of Tyree's working on football. I think that that's been demonstrated in this training camp where he is just absolutely required the coaches to find a way to get him on the field. And Mike McDonald will find time. Kobe Bryant, Ty Okada, Josh Job, he will find time for guys who in practice demand playing time. And And that's exactly what Tyree's Knight's doing. >> I love that and I love that perspective. And I didn't really know what to expect. I have to be honest. I watched the game having just an incredibly long 30 hours going to London and back for my day job. And And when I got to actually watch the game, I'd I'd pretty much just was watching it and then remembered in the first drive, oh yeah, Brian Flores, first drive. Um so it didn't strike me that it was anything that different. And then obviously they scored and I thought, great, that's a decent start. They've got a good drive going there. And then it just it was a I felt I found it a very painful watch for the rest of the way. I I hope that he can just show some improvements. I don't really know what to I want to see because I remember a year ago the Seahawks had that amazing game against the Chiefs in preseason where it looked like they could get 8 yards on a run every time they called a run. And then we spent the first half of the actual NFL season saying, where did the Seahawks going to sort their running game out? Like and then eventually they got there, but it it it often if you see good things, it doesn't necessarily mean it's going to happen when the the real football begins. But, we didn't see a lot there, and um I must admit a lot of my thoughts did go to the quarterbacks. I I understand why Drew Lock is the backup, and he and Sam Darnold, you know, they knew each other in high school. They went through the Rivals camps together. And Drew seems like a great guy, and I'm sure he's great in that quarterback room. But, um I I don't think if the Touch Wood it won't happen. If Sam Darnold gets hurt, I'm not sure that you could roll out Drew Lock for, say, four games, five games, and keep the season going. I'm not sure you could. And um it's funny really, cuz I I was kind of like watching a few of the other preseason games, and Carson Wentz came out who, you know, no one really wants to see play football again, but I did sort of think I I think if you needed someone to win you a game, he might be a better option than than Drew Lock. And you think, great, let's let's see something here. I'm not sure the two series each thing helped either of them that much, but um I thought he was really hesitant. I think he's he's not a fit for this system. I I'd never thought he was a fit for the Shanahan offense, and and I'd like to see him just accept maybe a little bit more that whatever his strengths, creativity, running first and foremost, and playing off that instead of the other way around, instead of I'm going to hold it onto it, hold onto it, and then take off when it's too late. I think we're not seeing any of that real burst as a runner, because it's always a late afterthought in the play rather than instinctively, here's my chance, I'm going to go for this, which is I suppose what we're doing a bit more in Alabama cuz there's a lot of more called runs or or option plays. Um, and and the other thing I think is I don't know really what the plan's going to be moving forward cuz this is the second Shanahan disciple you've got as a defensive coordinator now. So, if Mike Macdonald is really connected to the Shanahan offense for his his offense. Is it time for the Seahawks to start looking for the quarterbacks that you would say quote unquote fit the Shanahan offense? Cuz that's not really the kind of quarterback that John Schneider's been attracted to. John Schneider likes size, physical tools, improv, like the the crazy creativity, the Josh Allen, the Mahomes, the Russell Wilson, and and Shanahan quarterbacks are Kirk Cousins and Jimmy G and Brock Purdy, that type. And um, that's a very different quarterback. And there's there's been like, you know, I'm not saying they should have drafted him. I'm definitely not saying that. But that's what like Garrett Nussmeier, for an example, is somebody you'd say he might be a Shanahan quarterback and he's available in like round seven or something. And you think, okay, that would be a system fit. But the Seahawks seem to have a backup and a third quarterback, neither of which are an amazing fit for this system. And I wonder if that's ever going to pivot, whether they're going to just stick to what the GM prefers or what the offense calls for. Is there Is there always going to be this hope that there's something that will mesh with Sam Darnold does cuz he's great physical talent, but he fits the offense. I don't know. title: Something Is Wrong with the Seahawks' Offense...
text: Uh, Seahawks will work to get that back in the second preseason game, but Rob, I would love just your overall first thoughts. You've had it now a few days to sit on this game. What was your takeaway from that first preseason game? >> Uh, I was disappointed, and I understand that anytime that you criticize this team now, uh, that that people don't like it. Cuz I did a stream the other day, and a lot of the comments were quite angry that we talked about negatives, but no one thinks the preseason's going to be indicative of anything this season. It was all backups, and everybody accepts that, but it's still okay to review a game of football that the Seahawks played in, and the players that played in it. And I thought it was quite poor. They had one drive in the game, which was heavily influenced by the officials. They didn't do anything after that. I I found it very hard to understand what they're actually trying to do on offense. I know that um, they're not going to come out with an exotic scheme in the first week of preseason. It is going to be quite a vanilla setup, but still, I would have hoped to see a bit more. Clint Kubiak had over 200 passing yards in his first preseason game a year ago, and they struggled to get about 70-odd in this game, which was disappointing. Uh, I really struggle to watch Drew Lock play quarterback. Uh, I'm sorry. I like He seems like a really cool guy. Not a great watch. And then Jaylen Milroe came in, and I I don't think he's an NFL quarterback, uh, personally. Uh, you look at the defense. Again, I was writing about this in the week. No one's banking on these young players to be an answer for the Seahawks either this season or in the future, but it would have just been really cool to see one of the edge guys look really good. Just because next year, you've got a It's not unrealistic. Demarcus Lawrence is going to is going to retire, he says, at the end of this season. Dante Fowler's into his 30s, and Chenna's in the last year of his deal. It's not beyond the realms of realms of possibility that those three aren't on the team next year, which leaves you with Darrell Hall. And we've we've been in with the Seahawks in the past where they've suddenly had quite a void off the edge. And sometimes they get it right. Uh Chenna Ewuosu, DeMarcus Lawrence, good free agent signings. And sometimes it's Benson Mayowa or Bruce Irvin in trading up for Darrell Taylor. And I I don't really want to risk that. The The reassuring thing is that Mike McDonald has shown whoever you give him, he'll kind of turn water into wine. And he did that with Jadeveon Clowney and Kyle Van Noy Baltimore. And I think if it was Darrell Cole and a couple of veterans that they signed on the cheap next year, he probably would be able to make it work, especially with the interior options that Seattle has got. But I really wanted to see one of these young guys just go, "I'm your man. You know, I can be in this rotation, and then I can maybe take a bigger role in the future. Maybe be the the Drake Thomas or the the Tyre Carder of the pass rush, maybe." I don't think any of them really showed that. >> Well, Rob, uh Mike McDonald loves the word, so he would be happy with that analogy that you gave him. But Brian, curious your thoughts just on the pass rush. I know you talked to Dante Fowler, I believe today at practice. Was it today? >> Yeah, before practice. Yeah, I I'd agree with Rob on a lot of his takeaways. I I think that you know, I'll I'll go through a little bit there. But Rob, and NAB 2, who who do you think is the best pass rusher that John Schneider's ever drafted? Who comes to mind? Cuz it's not a long list. Obviously Darrell Cole and Boye Mafe most recently. Neither one of those guys have proven that they are an A-list pass rusher. There's one guy that comes to mind for me. Frank Clark. >> Yes, Frank Clark's got to be. >> Yeah. >> Probably their best pass rusher they've drafted. And Frank Clark was a good Pro Bowl pass rusher, but even Frank Clark, I don't really think was an A-list pass rusher. So, you're talking about a Hall of Fame general manager who's done a lot of things right and has added some very good edge rushers, but they've been generally added through free agency or some other mechanism. And you are entering a situation where there's going to be turnover one way or another. And so Connor O'Toole, Jared Ivey, Jamie Sheriff, like you were looking for somebody to step up and flash. Jamie Sheriff's been hurt, but hopefully he'll get more of an opportunity more of a rep now. He played in practice today and actually had a good practice. But I don't think Connor O'Toole did jump up. I don't think Jaylen Gaines did jump up. I think Jaylen Gaines has a chance to be a guy that's an interesting player. But there's not a single guy that I see that I'm like, "Okay, this is the next A-list edge rusher that other teams are going to have to game plan for." So, what do you do? I think that you're going to start to see Mike Macdonald attack the edge in different ways. One, Dante Fowler, DeMarcus Lawrence, Uchenna Nwosu, Derek Hall are fine for this year. So, let's not like overreact to that. But I also think Tyree Knight is a guy that I think you're going to see him on the line of scrimmage and I think that he showed last year that he can get after the quarterback when given the opportunity. I think you're going to see Devin Witherspoon and Nick Eubanks will be sent after the quarterback and we've seen what those guys can do and one of the things that was going on in OTAs and mini camps was Nick Eubanks getting more reps with the edge rushers during positional drills and even now when I see him working on things and he's not fully back, they're edge rush kinds of things. I think that's the area that of anything that he's probably trying to add the most to and ironically, first time I saw Nick Eubanks standing in a locker room or even on the field, I was like, "God, that guy looks like an edge rusher." Like he is the size of DeMarcus Lawrence. Uh he isn't literally, but he looks like that. So, >> Like that, wow. >> I mean, he he's he's just size-wise, he he's in that kind of conversation. So, I think you're going to see other guys um, in position to attack the edge, and I think you might see some interesting lineups where they're playing five down linemen, and you've got Uchenna Nwosu and Demarcus Lawrence and um, Darrell Taylor on the field. I think you're going to see some situations where you might not believe it. Nose tackle Byron Murphy. You might see him on the edge. Leonard Williams today. He's done it before, but he was on the edge and absolutely a terror on the edge because what do you do when you have Leonard Williams, Jarran Reed, Byron Murphy, Riley Mills, like this massive store of a really good defensive tackles? You get them on the field any way you can, and that might be playing some of these guys outside. So, I think Mike McDonald will work his way through it. I still think it would be ideal for them to get a dynamic edge player. Maybe, I mean, we talked about it before, maybe they go in for Maxx Crosby? Maybe? >> You would just lit Rob up. You just His whole persona just changed, Brian. >> It They got 12 picks next year in the draft. You saying for sure there's no chance that mid-season they're going to say, "You know what? Let's add a little bit more." That would be probably the first name in my mind. Uh, doesn't mean it's going to come close to happening, but it might. So, yeah, I agree with Rob on that front. >> So, Rob, do you have enough confidence though in the D-line that Brian talked about that it might make other players' jobs easier? Or would is it is it that Maxx Crosby name that just lights you up and and bring a smile to your face that you would you would take that exhale? >> I think when I've watched Maxx Crosby, I've just thought every single time I would love for him to play for the Seahawks. Like he's just everything about him, the fact that he is so dynamic off the edge and a constant threat, but plays every down like it's the last one of his life. And uh I've just always liked that. I think it's a great fit for what the personality of this team is. So, I'd be always down for that. And whether that's at the if they get him at the deadline to say, "Okay, we've got the Rams twice at the end of the year. Let's go and get this guy. This will This will put us in pole position to maybe win the NFC West or get the number one seed or whatever it is." then I'd be totally down for that. But also then you look ahead and you think he's under contract. Yes, you might need to pump up some of the money uh when once you've traded for him, but you're getting somebody that all of a sudden you're going into next season, yes, still with a decent chunk of picks and some some uh ability to add, but you've got Maxx Crosby and Darrell Cole with your great interior uh defensive line. And all of a sudden it looks like a really good line for this this window that the Seahawks are in. So,

title: John Harbaugh Recaps Joint Practice & Previews Dolphins Matchup | New York Giants

title: Saquon Barkley & More on Joint Training Camp with the Patriots
text: Don't laugh at that. >> Huh? >> Yeah. >> How would you evaluate the offensive performance last year? >> Um, yeah. I mean, you know, it's it's good work, great competition. Probably take that out. Um, great competition. Um, going against a great team, well coached team. So, I kind of joint practices. I don't try to look too much into it. Uh, I don't look too much into the good, don't look too much into the bad. There's a lot we could still work on and um just get better from it and move on. >> Was there a sense of excitement about the potential of the run game with the new scheme and the way that you're performing here in camp? >> Um again I don't look too much into the performance of it. I'm super excited because you know I know how great this team will be and how great we can be and you know you know I know what it looks like when we're all on the same page and we're playing a high level. Um, but right now this this whole portion of camp and this part of the season is really about just grinding. Um, you know, putting the little things together, staying focused on the little details and getting better one day at a time. They talked this morning about uh pre- snap operation, how they truly all with like bringing the play play clock down to really try and put pressure on you guys. What's your takeaway from those things and how do you feel like that's going in practice? >> I didn't hear the first part, but um uh yeah, I didn't really hear the first part. I heard I know the second part, but >> on you guys. >> Who said that though? >> Nick. >> Okay. Okay. Um, yeah. I mean, I think Nick does a really good job of creating, you know, chaos in practice, um, and drills. Um, it's never, you know, when you go out there, it's hardly ever, it's rare that it's going to be perfect. Um, but just make us focus on the little things, make sure we're our procedures where it needs to be, getting out of the huddle. Um, you know, that's something that every team right now in this phase is kind of working on. Um, I think, like I said, I think Nick and Sean and all those guys do a really good job of creating that for us. And, you know, are we where we want to be? No. Would I want to be perfect right now? Not even two. So, just get better at it every single day and just move on. >> What's the other value? What's the value of like testing the running game in a setting like this against another opponent, not just, you know, your own guys? >> Um, I'm the wrong guy to ask cuz I I I hate joint practice to be honest. Um, I think one day is good, but uh, you know, you know, we we play in a, you know, a ego ego sport, uh, with a lot of men and it can I'm all about just putting the work in and it's good to go against someone new. Uh, I think we're definitely were at that part of camp where we needed to go against a new face. Um, but I do think if you do it the right way, um, there's a lot of good out of it. um going against different looks, going against different people. Um it's hard when you got to run the same play over and over against JC and and JD. Uh they're pretty good players and you know they get a a hint of what you're doing, it's even harder to block. But yeah, when you do it the right way, it's good, but honestly, I'm not really a fan of joint practice. >> Just you know, it's just more times than not, nothing good comes out of it. Like you get the the when you have the work it's good but then you get to push in the shove in and you're someone say this about you and I'm like oh no but I'm not that you're this and just like it's it's immature when we get to that level. I got to do a better job too cuz I'm a little you know a little troublemaker sometimes but I was a good I was good this week. >> Was there a little more of that today though? Maybe a little after the whistle and stuff. >> Yeah, that's that's bound to happen after day two. You go back you watch film. you know, you don't I don't believe in like someone won the day versus they lost today, but you watch film and it's going to be a little more, you know, I don't want to say competitive because it's it's not even that. It's just, you know, obviously football is just a physical game within itself. And it's just a little extra pushing and shoving, but we got to do a better job of also not allowing that to, you know, have a factor in our practice because I think coach said it best at the end of practice, that stuff only lasts forever. That only lasts maybe five minutes. You know, that's why big games aren't real things. you go out, you you feel the atmosphere and the energy and all that that lasts for such a little time. It really goes back to the little things. Um who's the who's have the better fundamentals, who's detailed, who's locked in, who's doing the right things that's going to win football games. So, um we got to do a better job of that and as leaders, you know, it's our job to to lead in that that area. Also, >> it's been three weeks since we spoke to you. In that period, there have been three different backs who who signed big deals. Given kind of the position that you took a few years ago, um how gratifying was that to see? >> I love it. Um, I love it. That's how it's supposed to be. Uh, Christian did it before me. I did after Christian and now we got three in a row. Um, I look forward to the next guys to do it. Um, you know, for a little short period of time. You know, it went like that for every other position besides running back. And you kind of can see that coming back to life. And those guys are well deserving of it. They're hella players. They're they make a lot of impacts in games for their teams. Um, their their team is different when they're out on the field. So, um, you know, hopefully in the next 5 to 10 years, it keeps going higher and, you know, that's how it's supposed to go in my opinion. >> Have you seen the view of the position shift in these past two years since you had the year you had? >> Um, no. I think it depends who you're talking to. Like, everybody, every team and every GM is going to have a different opinion, you know, just, you know, when I rush for 2,000 yards, there still some GMs probably don't think that I would make that difference on the team. And you have a guy like Howie who believed in me. And really that's all it takes is you need one or two two people to believe in you and I appreciate how we for the opportunity and you know what we were able to do in 24 and hopefully we're able to do that again this year and you can see that in the GMs and the teams over there with Bon with JT with uh Gibbs the type of players that they are. Um and you know so it's it's based on the team I feel like you know there's probably still people who are stuck in their ways not just for running backs but other positions. You know some people don't want to pay wide receivers this amount of money. Some people don't want to. Everybody's going to pay the quarterback like they're going to get paid. But um depending on the position you're talking about, >> well as far as your preparation, >> I feel good. I think uh Jamal has a really good game plan for me right now. Um you know, of how the week's going. I can feel my workload going higher and higher each week as we ramp up. Um you know, I just trust in him and Nando and our strength staff. uh put me in a position to go out there when it's time to go um to have the the condition to be conditioned enough to go out there and and perform at a high level um for four quarters. Um you know, I don't believe in, you know, like you know, you let the first four games get you get you set in, you know, [snorts] from one to hopefully week 21 or 22, whatever it is. Um I want to be able to go at a high level. So trusting them the way that they, you know, getting me ready each week and the plan that they have for me and I'm just going to keep attacking it. >> Any general impressions of the defense you faced the last two days and just of the team that Mike? >> Yeah, I think they're a great team. I think they're a well coached team. I'm not going to really get into speaking about individuals. Um I I think they're a great team. There's there's a reason why they made it as far as they did last year, but it's a new year. It's a new start, and we're all trying to see where we're at. And that's the good thing about joint practicing when you you're able to do that. But um like I guess I already told you how I felt about joint practicing but um yeah I I got nothing but respect for for all those guys over there and um you know I feel like they have a good chance of going very far. >> Jaylen yesterday mentioned details and aligned and getting on the same page. Where do you think the offense is as far as that? >> Yeah at this point >> we got a lot of work to do and that's what you want. You know what I mean? Uh, Jamal did a great example yesterday in our in our meeting and, you know, he kind of created levels and like circle this, we're great. And I know Jaylen holds us to that standard, holds himself to that standard. So, we got to be detailed. Obviously you guys see a little bit of stuff that we're doing. Um, I'm a big believer in not trying to give all the information you can here, especially when you got a new OC and you're going against a a team that hasn't played you yet or played against him. I mean, I'll have to watch that back. I didn't see um you know what happened on that side of the field, but um you don't see that too often, you know, that that far away from the end zone. Usually happens, you know, a lot closer um to the goal line, but yeah, I didn't see that one. So, they'll watch it back. >> When you go back to watch [snorts] the first day practice, how much is that different than going kind of scouting a team like normally? >> Yeah, it definitely helps. Um, obviously you're not preparing, you know, preparing for the for the offense you're going against when you're coming to joint practice. You know, you're kind of going in there blind a little bit. Obviously, you have a little understanding of who they are as an offense. Um, you know, but when uh when you get that [snorts] first day, you're able to go back and, you know, look at the looks that they gave us, where they hurt us, um, and things that we did well, too. So, um, you know, I think we did a good job of that. You know, learning from our mistakes yesterday and, you know, cleaning those things up today. goal to go. A lot of base in those go to goals playing safety. What's your take away from that experience against? >> Yeah, it's it's been it's been up and down kind of. Um I've been I've been learning. Um obviously we got coaches in our room who are great at uh you know, coaching me. Um you know, but I'm I'm starting to get comfortable back there. Uh more and more comfortable as as camp's gone on. Um I felt good out there today. Um yesterday we got some, you know, challenging looks, you know, for me back there, which I I need to clean up and and be better at. But, um, yeah, I'm starting to get more and more comfortable back there and, um, communication's getting better, you know, everybody getting on the same page and like I said, that's always key. >> Michael Carr is going through the same process that you are. What have you seen [snorts] from him as he's making that same adjustment? >> Yeah, he's been great. Um, you know, I think he's been making plays, you know, almost every day of of camp. Um, he's been fun to watch. um and and learn, you know, learn off of each other, you know, which has been great. You know, anytime you got two guys, you know, making the same move and playing the same two positions, you can always ask questions and and learn from each other. So, um you know, it's been fun to go through that process with them. >> Thanks, Appreciate it. >> All right. Nice guy. >> How did would you evaluate the last few days kind of what you take out practice? >> Um should be fun. It was a chance to go against a great defense and see, you know, what this new offense and the potential that it can get to. Uh it's been very educative uh from a, you know, offensive standpoint, uh say the least. Uh but yeah, I think it's been, you know, been pretty fun. It's been pretty fun uh last two days. >> Jordan, what is that potential? Um, you know, I think Humble Me wants to just say, "Yeah, you know, it's it was good, but we have a chance to to do something special." Um, but in order to do that, we can't have days like the last two days of, you know, up front. It always starts up front and we've had multiple false starts, you know, that starts with with me and and Lane and, you know, it's got to trickle down to the receivers and everyone that's on that field, you know, and so we have the potential to do uh do a lot, but that's all it is. It's potential, you know, it's we we see the limit that, you know, the sky's the limit. Everybody always says that, but we see where we can get to. And you know, we had a a a good day yesterday and today, you know, we got to clean up some of that uh less boxing and and more football. >> You say less boxing. Was there some stuff after the whistle coming from them? Uh more intensity. >> Just boys being boys and it's football, you know. I think uh I think people running in, myself included, made it worse. You know, it's just you you you can't help but you know, want to be there for your teammates. And so it's just again situation is is each situation is different and guys guys were running from all over the place today to to get a piece of you know the opposition and days like that it it kind of again it starts with me and I got to be better on that. Um, but you know, we got to remember when we start things like start fights and start things like that, we take away reps from the younger guys and you know, it's it's [snorts] unfortunate. So, we got to be better up front um again with the communication and and and how the laying the ground works for the practice and uh you know, sliding fights isn't isn't a way to go about it. >> This might stand across all of training camp, but Nick Siani was talking this morning [snorts] about in terms of the play clock. Sometimes there'll be plays where they intentionally break it down to put pressure on the pre- snap operations. >> What has been kind of your experience with that and how do you think that's going to go? >> Um, I think it could be a lot smoother. Uh, each position taking their own part of the accountability, you know. I think for us, we're just worrying about the [snorts] offensive line and are we getting to the line? Are we breaking the, you know, from the huddle to the line of scrimmage? Are we making our point and getting ready for the play to start? We only look at that. I can't look at, you know, again, my job is already hard enough as it is. And whatever Jaylen's doing back there, we just got to go on whatever whenever he says. And, you know, sometimes we're we're not breaking the the huddle fast enough. And now it's on us now. We're we've got 10 seconds to send a motion and send this motion that way. And, you know, speaking of emotions, how fun was that? It's nice. As a first time football player back in 18, how many pre-season games or even preseason years did it take before you felt like you that you could do what you were doing? >> Uh probably 2022 up until 2022 where I felt really comfortable in who I was as a player. I felt like every year I was proving myself. I mean, even now I'm still trying to prove myself, but I'd say 2022 up until 2022, I felt very comfortable in who I was and who I am. Um and the player that I that I am and the player that I can be. still got a long way to go, you know, very lucky to play with Lane and so for me, I'm chasing greatness and that's every day. >> Thomas Dean look like he's ready to take the next step. >> Absolutely. It's contra contract year, man. >> Contract year. You know, usually you you go either north or south and he's on his contract year and he's playing lights out right now. You know, he's going to have a good year, but he needs to stay here. He needs to stay mission focused, tunnel vision, uh to get that. And you know, if he can continue to excel and continue to to get better every day like he is, you know, I think he's going to have a great season. But >> is there anything particular about his game that's taking a leap from last year? >> Kind it's kind of like the what the question that Zach just asked me about coming into yourself and when did I feel confident in who I was. I think that's happening for seen at a much earlier rate. This is year four for him and he's he's starting to feel that right guard position. We've drafted him as a left tackle, moved him to left guard, moved him to right guard and back to left guard, you know, and now that he's, you know, essentially had one year under right guard and going into the second year as a right guard as the starter, you know, I think he's he's found a home there and that's why he's we're seeing to we're starting to see him excel. >> How do you see from the running game as far as Son's concerned [clears throat] and also Tank when he gets a chance? >> Um, again, I see a lot of potential out there. Uh, the running backs are doing a great job. Sean's doing a great job of, you know, getting to his reads on the run. Uh, the beautiful thing about our scheme is he can hit anywhere and um, you know, again, it's not just all on Saquon. It's got to be on us up front. We got to get to our landmarks and and win our block up front, you know, and some of that today wasn't there. Um, but again, it's something that we can always improve on and focus on getting better. >> Are you seeing it like you >> I am seeing us getting better. Absolutely. We just We're buying into it. We're seeing, especially after these two days, we're seeing what he can do up front, especially yesterday. Yesterday was a a a better day for us. Um, you know, running the ball. Today, not so good, but yesterday we were able to see, you know, with the misdirection and and the way the the concept is designed where the ball can hit anywhere. You know, ship had a great day yesterday and ship and sake had a great day, but more ship ship was able to to effectively, you know, again, execute the scheme that we're now in. What do you think? >> What do you think has clicked for you guys up front in run game compared to where you were at when you started camp? >> Um just the continuity of the same five guys up front. Um and then reps. You know, this is essentially a new world for all of us up front. Um you know, and we're all on our own journey of uh learning this scheme and and and trying to become more aggressive player and and executing it up front. And so I think this just as time goes on, we're going to keep getting better and prove as cliche as it is the 1% better. I really do think in this case, in our case, this is going to apply to us. >> The run run game was better yesterday. What do you What do you think the difference was today? >> Um the run game had a better flow yesterday. There were less fights. The fights the fighting we got to cut that out because it killed momentum. Um and then it's you know both sides are now amped up and now we're we're not thinking about our assignment. We're thinking about, you know, roughing the next guy you which is great, but again, not effective in our in our scheme and concept of things and that's why I think, you know, there were no fights yesterday. Um, it was a pretty clean practice and we were able to build on that momentum. You know, if it was two yards, three yards, it just kept each yard kept leading to more yards and we weren't affected today because we decided to put the boxing gloves on today. But it wasn't like full-on fledged fights, you know. It was just like, oh, you know, push pushing shoving and and grabbing and stuff. But nevertheless, it killed the momentum. >> Thanks, Jordan.

title: Nick Sirianni on How He Analyzes Joint Training Camp
text: Hey, good morning everybody. How we doing? >> As uh as Kai Lemon works his way back, are there things you guys can do as coaches to help him catch up? >> Oh yeah. I mean shoot the uh extra meeting time, you know, being able to go through some of that stuff like even just when that meeting time too, you can just, you know, walk walk through some things and in the meeting room. And so yeah, always always mentally you're you're doing everything you can do to to help that. And then obviously too, you know, you want to be in good great shape. So there's things that you know that you can do there too as well um as far as you know what he's doing in the training room to make sure that he's in as good a shape as he possibly can be when he steps back out on the field. So all those things are thought about and uh and and we're working through all those things right now. >> Uh good work back and forth. Um, you know, just like, excuse [clears throat] me, just like, you know, there's back and forth in, you know, our practices when it's us versus us. You know, there's good back and forth yesterday. Um, you know, this is why, and I just felt like these guys, a really well coached team with good players, a really successful team. Um, you know, it's that's why you pick teams like this to to go against. And so, we really got uh good work and that's what we were we were looking for. And you can't say enough about uh the Patriots and coach Vrabel and and how uh how good that practice was. We're looking for another day that to be able to go through that today. >> On that note, Nick, um a lot has been made about whether you won or lost practice. Do you guys evaluate that? How do you evaluate these two days? >> Yeah, just uh just like we evaluate normal practices. Um you know, you go through it and you're making the corrections. You're praising the good things. you're making corrections to the to the things that need to be fixed and you're looking for improvement on on a daily basis throughout training camp. Um yeah, I we don't get too much into the win and loss of a joint practice. There's a lot of different situations we're working, different scenarios we're working, uh different flows of the of the game. It's not truly a a drive. So again, we're just looking for good work and be able to correct and and praise the things that went well. In some years you've had uh two teams you've gone against this year only one. What was the reason for that? >> Yeah. Um just the way it worked out this year. Um you know and thought we could get good two days work against again a team that that is a good football team um that's well coached and you know uh just have a good working relationship with coach Vable and uh you know appreciate him. >> Jaylen Herz was mentioning yesterday about maybe working on some details with the offense and more alignment and stuff like that. Where do you think it is overall with alignment and everything, you know, at this point in the preseason? >> Yeah, again, you're just looking to to stack days upon days and um and looking for progress, right? And the things that, you know, that are we're really focused on, you know, making sure that we're all on the same page as far as our assignments, uh you know, our effort, our fundamentals, um our pre-nap uh penalties. So, you know, again, we've been making improvements there. Uh cuz the I mean, you have no choice but to make improvements when you when you practice the way our guys do. They they they put everything into practice. We have good intensity at practice. Um and so, you know, I think it's been it's been a good uh progression and we're we're continuing to look to get better. >> Your offense struggled against simulated pressures last year. What does the new offense do to address that? >> Yeah, I'm not going to get too much into scheme. Uh but you know, you always you always are looking for you want to try to put the guys in as many position uncomfortable positions as you possibly can. Um you get that in practice, you get that in walkthrough, you get that against going against different teams, um like we are right now. Um and again, you're you know, you might think that you're going to come out and see a certain defense, but we know that, you know, the they game plan, too. And so you're trying to put yourself into as many unknowns as possible but and play your rules of with those unknowns and then make adjustments off of that. And so yeah, again, I think it's just so important at this time of year where you're testing your rules versus every different look you can get. And this is a great opportunity for us to just, you know, you can do that in walkthroughs. You know, you can do that in some periods where it's like a offensive emphasis or a defensive emphasis, which we do in in uh in during training camp amongst each other. Uh but this is a great opportunity for us to get some more unknowns uh when we go against another team. >> You you and AJ had a lot of success together. Was it weird practicing against them? Did you get a chance to catch up with them? What was yesterday like for you? >> Yeah, just good to see all the all those guys. Good to see AJ, good to see Milton. Good to see Christian Ellis. uh you know, and some of the guys there, you know, been on a team with Hunter Henry. Good to see him. Uh you know, you build relationships with guys and those those relationships, you know, when they're strong, you know, are life lifelong relationships. So, it's always good to see those guys. Um yeah, obviously we had we've had a ton of success together. Um and you know, um so it was good to see those guys yesterday. >> Sounds like Bernard is empty for week one. Did he suffer a setback? >> Uh I I think he's doing a nice job progressing. Um we'll see where that is. Uh you know, we'll see where that is as we as we get closer to it, but he's doing really he's working really hard to get himself back and and doing the things that he needs to do and the things that he can control. And so, yeah, I'm not ready to say that where where we are on any of that yet. Um except for the guys that aren't out there practicing are are working hard to get themselves back. And we got a great training staff and doctor doctors and uh strength and conditioning staff that are working hard to make sure he's ready when when he can be. >> How much more value can you get from like, you know, working your new offense against an opponent as opposed to, you know, going against yourself in training camp or even in the preseason game? >> Yeah. Again, I think it's kind of what we talked about earlier in the sense of you're you're trying to test your rules versus every different thing. Um, and again in walkthroughs or in, you know, offensive emphasis or defensive emphasis periods, um, you can simulate, you can, hey, let's get a nickel pressure on this or a safety pressure here or a line stunt here. Um, and so it's just, you know, in in a practice like this, you're getting some some more some more of that that you haven't seen on a daily basis or even some stuff that you haven't scripted into a daily basis. So that's always that's always good because again we want to make sure our job description to the players is extremely clear and it's not like and when you when you do job descriptions it's like hey here's your assignment but here's what you have to do versus all these different looks and there's as we know there's so many different looks a defense can throw at offense and vice versa offense can throw at defense. So, you're trying to prepare them for every scenario. And sometimes the answer is, hey, we got to do this combination or make this call right here. And sometimes it's, hey, we got to check out of the play, but you want to put them in as many unknowns as possible. So, they're so it's so they're handling those things second nature when it when it comes to the game. Um, and so this is always beneficial. >> Sorry, I'm I'm from Boston. >> Hey, how you doing? >> Good. How are you, man? >> Yeah, good. Um, you guys have a new offensive coordinator this year, some other new coaches, which is not unusual for you. What's that like as a head coach just kind of every year like getting building a new staff and building offense? Yeah, it's the uh it's the the way of uh the NFL and and you know, I know this I know Coach McVey goes through this a lot and I know uh you know, Coach Shanahan goes through this a lot and uh you know, we've had to go through this a lot. And so, one one thing that's awesome is you get to uh meet and work with different people that that's what's a great thing about football is it brings people together you probably wouldn't have ever met otherwise. And so, you get to form these new relationships and everything like that. But there's a lot of work obviously that goes into that as well of you know uh all the things that have to be taught and thought through and hey if you're in this scenario you know situational football especially of hey when we're in this scenario this is the kind of plan of attack of how we do things. Um and so it's getting everybody on the same page in that manner of the game management portion of it. Um so it's fun. It's a it's a it's a long process. Uh but you know it is you know it is a it is a big part of the process that we got to go through and it's always it's always fun going through it with new guys and you know not only are you learning are they learning about you know kind of the way we attack in different certain ways offensively defensively but you're also getting to to learn how they've done it in the past and and and and that's great collaboration cuz sometimes you're like I haven't thought about it that way and and you and you find the best path for the 2026 Eagles, not hey what the 25 Packers did or what the 24 five Eagles did, but what's the best path for this team and so you know with that comes growth and um you know and I and I always appreciate that and that's this time of year and and with new guys. >> Sean said that he was going to uh experiment up >> you're from Boston. >> Yeah. Okay. Very well. Uh Sean Manny had said he was going to experiment up on the booth uh the next game. Just what are your perspective on the pros and cons that perspective? [snorts] >> Yeah, everybody's a little different and and so I want to make sure that he has an opportunity to feel both things out. Um you know, again, some guys like to be up in the booth, some guys like to be on the field. Without getting too much into it, you know, I always think it's important to be able to have a direct line of communication to guys. Um, he's got coaches and we got coaches that we trust to be on the field to be able to handle that. But, you know, I know that's always something that when guys call it on the field, they they like to be down there to feel the flow of the game and of the flow of the players. And on the other end, you know, being up in the in the box, right, you can have all you can like you can have all a ton of papers l kind of thought processes that you might not be able to have on the field. Different uh view of the game of seeing different things. Um, you know, obviously the NFL has made it very easy for the guy to that's in the box calling the play to be able to directly talk to the quarterback, which you, you know, so that used to not be the case. I remember in 2010 I was talking to the quarterback, but Charlie Weiss uh was uh calling the plays from upstairs. They didn't have that communication yet. Um, so that's not a thing anymore. But, you know, benefits, there's there's positives and negatives to both both sides and it's just weighing out what works best. There's, you know, there's so many different ways to do this. Like, there's so many different ways to to lead a football team. There's so many different ways to run an offense or a defense. There's so many different ways to work situational football. And it's about finding out what's best and work what works for you. I think like I think young in my career, it's like, no, this is the only way to do it. That's just not the way it is. is like there's so many different ways to do it and it's being open and finding out the best way of how your team should go about it. >> I know obviously from the same hometown as Ryan Hudson from this area. I know he went to a joint practice practice earlier this year. What can you say about him as a person and how much you look forward as you go? >> Yeah, he was a he was a little younger than me so didn't know each other quite as much until we got into this coaching profession and it's been fun following his career. obviously he's a star of um you know of how fast he's risen up the um you know the coaching ranks. So I'm excited to you know now that yeah I've been be able to follow him the last couple years. Always fun to watch another team when it comes to March Madness and to into college basketball because I'm sure a big fan of that. Um but I've enjoyed getting to know him and obviously see the talent that he has as a coach has been fun. uh and being able to bounce, you know, as another guy I'm able to bounce ideas off of. Uh, you know, he was able to sit in on some of our meetings and, you know, just be able to bounce some ideas. I'm always interested to see how basketball teams operate as opposed to football teams because there's differences, but there's things that we can learn from each other and uh yeah, rooting for rooting for them and uh and for his success because uh you know, obviously I think think highly of them. >> Have you thought about the the new rule with the challenge flag? Are you going to >> But I still like I still like Villanova basketball. I'm still I still got to >> the new rule with the challenge flag. Are you going to keep it yourself? >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I Yeah, that we we had a quick discussion about it. But yeah, I don't know. Yeah, I'm definitely I'm definitely going to keep that. uh because my direct communication upstairs again don't want to I don't want to have a misstep or anything like that where you know there there's times on the challenge flag from my perspective that I think back to 2022 Smitty catches a ball over his shoulder in Washington um at Washington and we run a play fast and coach Rivera throws the flag, but our the ball is being snapped as he throws the flag and we beat the we actually beat the challenge. And so in my eyes, the way we need to do the way the Philadelphia Eagles are going to do is I just want that direct communication. So if I have to get the the flag out quick, I'm not saying my releases really quick. I'm not saying anything like that, but like at least I can get that out quick. That's just my feeling on it of what we're going to do. And uh you know because I know sometimes it comes down to just little ten of seconds to be able to get that flag out per the 2022 Washington game. >> Two more. >> In in past years we noted the benefit of being away for days. Are you guys doing anything during the stage to freak out? >> Yeah, you know, again, these these first two days obviously is all focused on on practice and then we'll be focusing on getting ready for the game. Um, but naturally, yeah, guys will go out to eat together, guys will spend time together, coaches will spend time together, coaches and players will spend time together. And there's a lot of, you know, there's a lot of time, excuse me, Zach, too, where they're they're just together being together. I think one thing we talk an awful lot about when we talk about connection there's you know you can form connection through adversity of tough practices of of adversity that you face as a football team together you can you can grow connection through you know building trust on a daily basis but there is no substitute for you you have to spend time you can't just form a connection without spending time with each other and so this and and there is no shortcut on that it's like how do you gel a team to get quickly to come together? Time is one of the most important things that we have here on this to be able to build a connection as a football team. And so this is just more probably a more carved out time than they they get because they're not going back to the hotel or anything like that. And they you know they they almost you spend more time together in that. So, um, I always been I always appreciate that about this portion of of practice of a way joint practice >> as many earlier. How much of the offense are you able to get to? >> Uh, we're still getting to a lot of it. Um, you know, you're still installing your base offense and still going through it. Um, and you and you're you know, this isn't if a guy misses time in a season, you may pivot and shift, but you're still going to the the things that are your your you know, bread and butter, your your base offense, you're still going to work through. So, um, you know, we're working through that right now. >> Last one, guys, from now until the start of the season, what do you need to see from Kyle to trust him? again, you just want to make sure that he's just like all our guys. I talk a ton about, you know, um making sure that we're all on the same page, everyone knows their their job description. Um so it's, you know, building trust within that and it's, you know, the fundamentals and all those different things. And um I wouldn't say I have a you know, anything that's a check mark or anything like that. You know, when you know, and there's a there's a feel to it and I know he's working like crazy to get back. >> All right, next one. Go ahead. >> I was just thinking about calling >> unless I don't like the question and I'm going to >> we have seconds. >> Um, so when you when you got a play call a situation, >> see, I'm always he's always pushing people out and I'm like, "Yeah, you know, another question. I'm I'm Yeah, >> that sounds >> I'm just kidding. >> Uh, just throw Bob under the bus um for for play calling. Uh, >> those are nice sunglasses, Bob. >> Thank you." >> When you stumble into >> You look like Robert Dairo. >> Oh, okay. that you've been planning for where you know the play that you want to get to. There's a the quarterback presumably knows the play you want to get to. What's that feeling like to get into it to call it in those 25 seconds? Is it a little bit different when it's like exactly what you wanted? >> Um, you know, if I'm if I'm assessing your question right, you know that we we try to do some different things in training camper. We take the play clock down to put as much stress on us as we possibly can to push our operation as fast as we we possibly can. And so it is just this perfect like everyone's got to work together from coaches to players to get that communication in and to get you know if you have a check on the play or anything like that. There's just every it's about being all on the same page. Um and so it's a it's actually a pretty cool process of what how many pieces and parts it takes to do their job so everybody can do their job right. one person doesn't do their job right in that particular case and that's 65 times plus a game then it's going to struggle. >> Thank you.

title: Football at Four: Updating Several Eagles Situations Before Preseason Game 2
text: Football 4ward powered by the Inside the Birds podcast, insidethebirds.com, and is always brought to you by Ocean Casino Resort, the FanDuel Sportsbook, and the Gallery Bar Book & Games is Ocean's go-to game day destination with huge screens, great drinks, and all the Sportsbook action you want. It's the perfect place to catch every play and celebrate every win. And today, we are celebrating the wrapping up of the week Eagles joint practices. We talked with Adam Caplan last couple of days live from Foxboro, and today we have Andrew DiCecco, who was also at the joint practices. So, we got a lot to recap ahead of tomorrow's preseason game number two, and Andrew is back with us here on the Sports Bash on 97.3 ESPN. Andrew, welcome back in. How you doing today? >> I'm doing well, Josh. How are you? >> I'm doing good, and I feel like we have so much to get to, so I want to start with this. You know, for you going looking at those two joint practices, I got to get your reaction to what Jordan Mailata said yesterday cuz he talked about and we played the audio how he said that, you know, day one was a pretty good day for them, but day two they did a little too much boxing and not enough football. So, for you, what were the big contrasts for you between day one and day two? >> Yeah, so on day one, I thought they got a lot of really quality work in. Not to say that they didn't on day two as well, but day two was noticeably more chippy, and you could tell from the beginning of practice, Josh, that the energy and intensity was ramped up, and I think the Eagles really brought the juice that day. Particularly, I noticed it on the defensive side. Rhamondre Stevenson, the Patriots running back, gets downhill, gives a little extra blows his shoulder on Cooper DeJean. I think Elijah Vera-Tucker, the guard, throws a little extra shot in there, and Noah Smith took exception to it. Andre Sam put a nice stick on Andre Stevenson. Zach Von popped Treyvon Henderson along the sideline. I was really focused on the defense yesterday, but on the offensive side, there was a scuffle, a couple of them as well. So, yeah, I could see where Jordan's coming from and sometimes when you're facing a team for the second day, it was much hotter the second day, at least it felt more humid. It just felt like it was bound to happen, but I thought the Eagles made a statement from early in practice that they were there to bring it and I thought that they did a nice job. >> Speaking of the defense, I want to get your perspective on Vic Fangio made the comment earlier in the week about Jihad Campbell and about how you and I talked about Campbell a little bit last week about this is a guy who because Nakobe Dean came back last year, that he, you know, I'm paraphrasing a little bit, was behind a little bit behind the eight ball in terms of his development and understanding the defense. I just think that I know that Vic Fangio does not traditionally rotate linebackers, but when you have someone like Trotter Jr. who has had a good camp. He had a good camp last summer, and there's different things that he brings from an intangible standpoint that I think that they could incorporate into the defense and and maybe add another layer to it. He brings you a certain unique athletic traits there that that maybe you're not really going to find around the NFL. I think he's very much so the modern-day NFL linebacker in terms of his movement ability, but there's more to it than that, and that's why I think the Eagles kind of have the best of all worlds with those three linebackers. >> Talk with Andrew DiCecco for today's Football at Four powered by The Inside The Birds podcast. You can get all of his coverage of the Birds over at insidethebirds.com. Andrew, you mentioned Andrew Makuba a moment ago. Talk to us about safety. What have you observed from the joint practices at safety cuz Fangio, he did talk about guys like Michael Carter and others during his pressure this week. >> What were my impressions? >> On safety. >> Yeah, I mean, look, Marcus Epps has been the frontrunner and that's been something that's been a common theme throughout training camp. And for everything that Marcus Epps brings, he's a steady, consistent player, very instinctive, high football IQ, but he's not one that's going to typically make the big play. But, he gives you a certain level of stability there, whereas Michael Carter's new to the position, but Michael Carter, I would argue, elevates the ceiling of the defense because he's around the football a lot. He gives you certain traits that maybe otherwise wouldn't have from that position, meaning short area quickness, eye discipline, ability to break on the football. Some of his traits that carried over from him being a high-end nickelback where he was with the Jets, where he was once the highest-paid nickelback in the NFL. I just think that he brings a little something different and the way that the NFL's trending, the modern era, you need to have safeties that allow you to be multiple and they can cover some ground and allow you to do some different things defensively. I think Michael Carter has probably had a slightly better summer, I think it's fair to say. That's not to say that Marcus Epps has had a bad summer because just because you haven't seen him make a lot of plays, that that's not always the biggest indicator. He's always seems to be in the right place. He's not giving up big plays and I think there's a lot of trust there when it comes to Vic Fangio and Marcus Epps, but I think Michael Carter is an interesting player because he does have uh the range. Now, sometimes his versatility may work against him because he wears three different hats. And so, he he's someone that you can deploy in a number of different ways and I think that they're going to find a way to get him on the field. >> Andrew, one more on the defensive side of the ball. So, without him, a lot of focus and curiosity is about who is the guy that's going to be outside of Josh Sweat. We know Sweat has popped. He has developed well. It's been quiet, but he's been effective. He's a violent edge setter. He's added weight and strength to his frame. And I I think that he's provided some good pressure in practice. He brings a lot of intensity. I think he's kind of growing into more of a leadership role. And he's healthy. More important Most importantly, he's healthy at this stage of the game, which is incredibly important for him because injuries have kept him from, I think, reaching his full potential. He's done some good things in terms of just setting the edge. I think he's shown some juice as a pass rusher in different circumstances. And he's played a lot of football. He has some juice there. Then, you have someone like AJ Epenesa who's played a lot of football. He's being asked to do things that he hasn't had to do before, but he's working through some things. If you listen closely and pay attention to what Vic Fangio says, you'll hear that he seems intrigued with the player and his body type, Josh, is different from the other players in that room. He's more of a a bigger-bodied run defender type, and he does bring a little bit of an edge to him. I like the way that he plays the game. I remember talking to Josh Sweat, the Eagles rookie free agent in his first ever NFL game. Talked to him afterwards, and he said that in the first or second play of the game when he watched Epenesa set the edge, he said to himself, "Oh, okay. It's on now. The game's on." So, that tells you the kind of player that he is and the way that he plays the position. I think he adds a different dimension to that edge rusher group. >> You just mentioned about how Fangio has talked about Epenesa. Can we hit on that real quick cuz you talked about it earlier about how hey, Jeremiah Trotter might be a guy who gets play action in certain match-up certain situations. Is Epenesa potentially could maybe be that kind of guy, too, where if you're facing certain teams with certain formations or certain situations in a game, that he could be a valuable piece for Fangio to deploy defensively? >> Yeah, I think so. Elijah Moore missed the second practice with a neck injury, but prior to that, he's been someone that Jalen seems to have some trust in as an as a chain mover, not as not typically I say typically because he caught a deep pass in that practice, but not typically as a as a big play guy, but more of someone who can effectively move the chains and keep the offense on schedule. And and Darius Cooper's cooled off a little bit after a really hot start to training camp, didn't have a good preseason game. So all that group, I mean there there is a little bit to be desired. I mean the Eagles just waived Johnny Wilson um >> Yeah. >> right as we got on this call. And that's a shame because Johnny Wilson's a player who uh I was curious to see how he would fit in this offense. I think the Eagles really liked him, but he's been sidelined with a knee injury. So I I think their wide receiver depth, we're going to learn a lot about that over the next couple weeks. And Britain Covey and Makai Lemon, needless to say, still needs to get he needs to catch up. He showed good juice and burst. Really, he's no different than the player that he was since he's been here, but yes, both Saquon Barkley and Will Shipley caught the ball very effectively. Uh Tank Bigsby, that's not necessarily his forte. Jalen Hurts has to be able to to embrace it if that's something that Sean McVay wants to do because for whatever reason every offense, every iteration of it year after year has not incorporated it, but I think in this particular circumstance it it makes a lot of sense. >> For more Eagles coverage, go to insidethebirds.com for all of Andrew DiCecco's coverage for you and insidethebirds podcast. Like, subscribe, and download wherever you get your podcast. And Andrew joined us here on a Friday edition of the Sports Bash on 97.3 ESPN. Andrew, happy hour Friday to you. Keep up the great work, my friend. >> Thanks, man. Take care.
