Oh, it's the Chargers. All right, guys. Thanks for watching. I'll be back tomorrow. If you want to stay up a little later and watch Grant after after dark on Tik Tok, you're welcome to. Um, yeah. Thanks so much everyone and I hope you enjoyed this game. I'm really glad I wasn't there for it. Was that is that terrible to say? I'm really glad that I'm in my house about to uh, you know, stream again from my from my office. Anyway,

title: The 49ers just DROPPED THE HAMMER…
text: I'm on my way out of Sofi Stadium where they're literally shampooing the Chargers logo and endzone text off the field. 49ers truly making this their second home. But I was just in that locker room where I collected the first really, really cool story of this season. We didn't know this. Jacob Cowing tore his hamstring not once, not twice, not three times, he tore his hamstring four times last season. So, he's been to hell and back. And that means that the 83yd punt return for a touchdown on this field meant a whole heck of a lot to not just Jacob, but to his teammates. And the 49ers were very, very excited after that play. >> Been through a lot with a hamstring last year. very frustrating to, you know, as you're running that ball down the sideline, just what what you've been through kind of flashed through your head. >> Uh, I definitely I felt like I was in a dream for a second, honestly, just hearing the crowd go crazy and then just seeing my teammates run side by side with me. Uh, seeing how happy they were and then I'm like, ain't no way this is happening right now. But at the same time, it was a special moment for me. Um, you know, everything that I battled last year, being able to come back healthy, feeling healthy, and became healthy, and most importantly, um, you know, just battling with the guys was fun. But I think it's just really important to remember that these guys are humans and that they're playing a brutal sport and guys who can run a 4-3, you're putting a lot of strain in your muscles as well. For Jacob Cowing, he obviously had to fight through an enormous amount of pain and frustration last year that fans did not know about. They thought that a simple hamstring strain or tear was keeping him out for the whole season. There's actually four of those. What a cool story that we picked up in that 49ers locker room. Here's Jacob talking about his punt return. >> Soon as I seen the ball off the punter foot, um I'm like, "Oh yeah, I definitely have some time." Um before as soon as the ball was hit, I looked outside to see the gunners um to see if they had a clean release. They didn't. So they were getting held up pretty well, so I'm like, "All right, I definitely have some time." As soon as I got the ball in my hands, I'm like, "All right, make a beline to the left sideline, use as much gas as I got, trust my guys with the blocks, and then try and get an end zone." And that's exactly how it played out. >> We'll hear more from Jacob Gowing in a bit. For now, I just want to say that even if he doesn't contribute a whole heck of a lot offensively, the fact that he did that on punt return and he has that 4-3 speed means that he's likely going to make this 49ers 53man roster because they need a punt returner. And guess what? Last year, Sky Moore, he didn't really contribute offensively for the 49ers, but he made the team as their punt returner. Somebody else who's on his way to making this 53man roster is Kalon Black. Very, very excited to actually be able to break some tackles today, >> especially for a back like you. You're so you have such good numbers after contact, breaking tackles. You can't really do that in practice. How excited are you to get into live tackling, >> man? Yeah, I just feel great. Um, finally getting into real contact, playing against another team, you know, um, and taking advantage of it, you know, putting my shoulder down, grinding for those extra yards, doing what I can to help the team win. >> People were so upset when the 49ers drafted Black in the third round. I don't understand why you'd be mad when the 49ers picked up a ball of muscle, who runs a 44 who does everything right, pass protection, run after contact, receives the football. I don't know why he'd be upset when the 49ers drafted such a player, but thankfully they did because he might be the best number two that the 49ers have had to Christian McAffrey over the course of the past half decade. Now, speaking of help for McAffrey and for Brock Perie and for the whole offense, Dejon Stribbling continues to impress. He did drop a pass today, but he showed off his very strong hands before that. And guess what? Brock Perie says that he actively thinks about Dejon dribbling strong hands when he's deciding where to go with the ball in crucial situations like third down. >> It's pretty evident like all the guys around here talk about how strong of hands he's got and whatnot. So, um, for me on third down when we got to stay on the field, like that's definitely something that I think about when it comes to matchups and making sure we're going to the right guy and and all that. So, um, he showed that tonight. >> So, dribbling really really talented player. I think that, you know, Kyle Shanahan is going to discuss some of the the missed run blocks that he's had. There have been a couple that I've seen with the naked eye. I'm going to watch all the tape tomorrow and I'm sure that we'll hear more from Kyle Shanahan on that front. But boy, uh, this guy is adapting quickly to the NFL level as a receiver and the mistakes will be fewer and farther between just knowing his work ethic and watching him operate out there and his physical prowess down to his technical acumen. I mean, the the fact that he's catching these footballs in traffic, the fact that he's displayed hand strength that has impressed even the 49ers starting quarterback, I think that the future is really really bright for Dejan Stribbling. Back to Kalon Black. When he was out with the torn adductor, I noticed that he was doing something special, not not everybody does on the sideline. >> While while you were out at I noticed you were out at practice, you had a sheet in your hand. Is that a play sheet? and and what do you do while you're out to kind of make sure that you're still mentally plugged in? >> Yeah, so it is a play sheet and um just making sure you play by play, you know, visioning the plays and also watching and you know, seeing what you know the guys can get better as well. Um and then after that, you know, you just stay locked into practice and taking those mental rest that you always going to need. >> Do you feel that that helped you when when you did come back to where you didn't skip a beat? >> Definitely, man. And um honestly, I have great coaches, man. They help me out a lot. Um, just always staying on me, making sure I'm in my playbook and, you know, spending all that extra time in the playbook. It definitely helps. >> So, Kalon Black indeed did not skip a beat and he's going to be a vital vital piece of this 49ers team. The stat that I love, I'll say it again. 3.2 yards after contact per carry at Indiana. Quick injury report for the 49ers. They're going to be testing Ronaldo Green, so I'll have an update on his hamstring whenever that is available. Jack Jones will take his spot if Ronaldo misses any time. Nick Martin, the linebacker who had the forced fumble on this field, also a hamstring injury, so he's going to get tested when they are back in Santa Clara. Robert Jones, 49ers, maybe the leader in the clubhouse to be the starting left guard, hurt and likely out of the final preseason game. Carver Willis, the 49ers rookie, started this game at the left guard position. played a lot at left guard for the 49ers today. Maybe he's now on the inside track now that he's had a chance to play the position for a handful of snaps at the NFL level. We shall see. I do know that Connor Colby was at right guard for the 49ers. And I do know there's one more preseason game. Mike thinks the 49ers might be trying to hide Wesley Grimes so that way they can cut him and bring him back to the practice squad. That's the one player we didn't really hear from today. We saw some Will Pauling. We saw a lot of Cadarl Hodgej, the veteran receiver, playing well for the 49ers on offense and on special teams. Didn't hear much from the 6'2 target Wesley Grimes. That is going to be interesting moving forward. That last game that's, you know, teams are really starting to pay attention now to who might be cut, who they might claim on waiverss. Grimes has made a lot of plays for the 49ers over the course of training camp. Bigbodied wide receiver. We'll see what the 49ers do in Las Vegas this coming week. All right, back to Jacob Cowan who, you know, we talk about the punt return. I I do have to mention, you know, I just I like to look at this in really unbiased terms. the 4. It did seem that the 49ers were running an audition between him and Jordan Watkins by playing both of those guys well into the second half today at wide receiver and making Jacob Cowing play on the outside. Like I mean he was he's 5'9. He's probably never going to be a good outside receiver because you need a little bit more height on the outside. You have to be able to grab some of those higher throws. It's harder to be accurate as a quarterback when you're throwing across the entire field. Did you guys know that a field like this is 53 and 1/3 yds wide? I know it's an optical illusion. Might not seem that wide, but it's really wide. So, if a quarterback is throwing cross hash to the boundary, and there were two boundary attempts that went incomplete to Jacob Cowing today, it's not always going to be on the money accuracy, which is why you want a bigger catch radius, a taller wide receiver. So, the 49ers are running this audition between Cowing and Jordan Watkins. And I think Watkins is a little bit better suited for it at outside receiver, but cowing is so suited for that punt return job. He's got a lot of experience. The, you know, short stature, the 5'9 stature probably makes it easier to be shifty at that punt returner position. So, I mean, that's going to be his job with this football team. And then maybe he can make some hay on the inside. But for these preseason games, at least for for this one where the 49ers were running him on some of those boundary routes, I just don't know if that's going to be the type of player that Jacob Cowing is for the 49ers, at least in a successful role for this football team. Watkins, I I mentioned it in the instant reaction, he's going to have to do a better job if he wants to take that Z position and play a big big portion of the snaps in place of Ricky Pearl. He's going to have to make some of those contested catches with more regularity over the middle. But he did score another touchdown today. That was from Adrien Martinez. I was sitting in the locker room joking around. Adrien Martinez uh was was saying, you know, I'm not happy with all my plays, but I can make them exciting. We know how much he ran the football during college [snorts] at Nebraska and then at Kansas State. And M. Jones said, well, you know, I'm I'm the opposite. He makes the boring plays. M. Jones admitted, "Hey, I might not be that exciting, but he just was was laughing around. It was me, M. Jones, and Adrien Martinez." And it is true. Mac is not very fast, but some of those boring plays. Yeah, they they definitely uh check mark in that column for M. Jones. And then, of course, there was Brock Birdie who had that good debut for the 49ers today. Four of six on his one drive, played the 12 snaps. Kyle Shanahan likes the 10 to 12 snaps. I'm sure he'll play more, maybe a quarter next week in Allegiance Stadium. That is going to be the game against the Las Vegas Raiders. For me, it is now a trip back up to the Bay Area and I'm going to watch all this tape as well. So, we're going to have a lot more for you after I get done watching the tape. For now, enjoy the full interviews with Jacob Cowing. Also heard from Kalon Black and of course a little bit from Brock Birdie. >> Well, how did your vision open up there on that punt return? Just take us back through it. >> Yeah. Uh, as soon as I seen the ball off the punter's foot, um, I'm like, "Oh, yeah. I definitely have some time." Um, before as soon as the ball was hit, I looked outside to see the gunners um see if they had a clean release. They didn't. So, they were getting held up pretty well. So, I'm like, "All right, I definitely have some time." Soon as I sideline. use as much gas as I got, try and get an end zone. And that's exactly how I play. >> Been through a lot. The hamstring last year very frustrating to, you know, as sideline, just what you've been through kind of flashed through your head. dream for a second, honestly. Just healthy, feeling healthy, end of the game healthy, and most importantly, um, you know, just battling with the guys was fun. >> What does it mean to you to have all those guys go out there, meet you? I mean, there was a penalty, but it had to have felt good. >> Oh, amazing. Amazing. It was definitely a a long time coming. Um, something I've dreamt about for over a year now, ever since last year. So, being able to to make it come true is definitely a special. >> You had a lot of recognition when you went back to the bench area. Lots of congratulations. I mean that is it a little overwhelming? >> Uh a little bit at first for sure, but I mean just seeing everyone how happy they were for me and everything that they knew that I went through last year. Um you know I just felt it felt great that you know all these guys have my back. They were happy for me to see see me go out there and uh you know make a touchdown come come to life. >> You have this job in 2024 as a returner. So do you feel like that this is your job again? Like how do you do with your mindset on I mean a heated competition. I got it. This is mine and he's taking it from me. I mean, at the end of the day, we're still in training camp and, you know, there's still guys that are battling um at the end of the day. But me personally, I'm I'm gonna come in and battle um each and every day and and try and make that job solidified by by me, but at the same time, we also have other guys that are very good at at pump training as well. So, um you know, just very excited to see what the rest of training camp has. >> Did you have to give some tips for his first attempts at training? Um, I said, bro, just try and catch him. Trying to make something happen, bro. I mean, it's definitely tough, especially in that stadium, like when how how high the punter kicks it. You can kind of lose it sometimes, but um, you know, just try and make something happen, dude. Um, just most importantly, catch the ball. >> Shanahan said you lost the first one. >> I did. I I saw it and then absolutely it just went dark. I'm like, "Oh crap." Like, I don't know where it was at. Yeah, absolutely. Absolutely. >> How supportive has D.Va been through this journey of this first year back for you? >> Very supportive. Um, you know, he's been giving me tips. um you know very very he's a he's he's like a big brother for me for sure. Um he brings energy um each and every day in the receiving room and you know make makes guys make sure that you know we're up and ready um for the challenge at stake at the day and um you know I look forward to working with Debo. He's a he's a good player. He's a good dude. So um I enjoy his company. >> Does he give you any advice on returns too >> or would you give him advice? >> Uh we haven't really talked about that for sure but he gives me advice about receivers and stuff like that. So that's what we mainly talk about. Last year you tore your hamstring the first day it came from and then after that how it it progressed or it didn't progress what did you tear it again? >> Yeah, I tore it four times last year. Yeah. How much? >> Four. Four. >> Four times. Yeah. Yeah. So that was a that was a big huge mental workout going through. So able to battle through it and and come out strong. >> At what point in your recovery going into this year did you know I'm good? >> Um >> maybe on this run or what? [laughter] >> I would say definitely as soon as the season ended. I mean, I stayed back in in the Bay Area and um I just got my routine together. Um I trusted the the training staff, the and the um the strength coaches and we put together a plan for me that is obviously working. It's keeping me healthy. So, I appreciate them putting the time and effort into me and and helping me execute um me being healthy. >> Was there a point where you just had to shut it down for a while after the fourth tear? It seems like it kept on on on coming back. >> It was definitely after the fourth one. um you know, me and the training staff, we we kind of went back and started talking things over and um we just thought it would be best to kind of take it slow and to make sure that my hamstring is strong enough to where this doesn't happen again. So that's what we mainly talk about. >> And then just within the context of all that, there was a practice the other day where you were banged up a little bit on the the sideline, then you came back and made an amazing catch. I mean, [clears throat] correct me if I'm wrong, but it seemed to me that that that might have been big just considering the history of the past year. >> 100%. Um, you know, at the end of the day, like I got I got some heart in me. So, even though I'm a little banged up, I'm still going to try and go out there and perform at my best and um, you know, give my all to this organization. And I mean, they they trusted me. They drafted me here. So, the the least I can do is, you know, give my 100% effort to I'm on that field. >> Who did you lean on emotionally while you were going through all these the injury issues? >> Uh, definitely my family. My mom was a big one. She definitely helped me get through a lot. Um, you know, shout out to my mom. I love your mom. She she was she was my rock and I love and appreciate everything she she was doing for me during that time. >> Thanks. >> Especially for a back like you, you're really do that in practice. How how excited are you to get into live tackling? >> Man, it feel I just feel great. Um um and taking advantage of it, you know, putting my shoulder down, grinding for those extra yards, doing what I can to help the team win. >> How did you feel getting into a playing the game again. >> It felt great. Um, you know, it's been a while since we played, you know, back in January for the national championship, but, you know, getting out here playing, you know, spell football, it's just a blessing to be out there and doing it. >> And then you had that one where you kind of the second effort got you through the line a little bit more. How did that feel? >> You know, it's just one of those things where, you know, you're out there, you just, you know, doing what you can and, you know, scratch out some extra yards. Just always playing hard and just, you know, staying focused. >> Do you keep the ball on something like that? You said, >> "Do you keep the ball?" >> I do. >> Okay. All right. >> While while you were out, I noticed you were out at practice. You had a sheet in your hand. Is that a play sheet? And and what do you do while you're out to kind of make sure that you're still mentally plugged in? >> Yeah. So, it is a play sheet. And um just making sure you play by play, you know, visioning the plays and also watching it and you know, seeing what you want the guys to do better as well. Um and then after that, you know, you just to the next stay locked into practice and taking those mental rests that you always going to need. when you did come back to where you you great coaches, man. They helped me out a lot. Um just always staying on me, making sure I'm in my playbook, and you >> Man, it's it's been great working with Coach T, man. He's a really good coach and you know he's co a lot of great backs as well and you know I'm just looking forward to you know the future success with him. >> 11 is the first. >> Uh I would say yes and no. Um I feel like in college we also have to know a lot of people's you know expectations and what they have to do as well but here is more of an emphasis on it. Um and it's going to help you play faster regardless. Oh yeah. All the small details.

title: REACTION: 49ers destroy Chargers…
text: Number two is in the books, and the 49ers actually tied a record. 41 points. Brock Purdy looked sharp, knocked off the rust, didn't get hurt. 12 plays for Brock Purdy. I told you guys that Kyle Shanahan likes 12 plays from his quarterback in preseason game number two, and he got it exactly 12 snaps over that first drive. Apologize about some of the noise here in the press box, but we're going to give our very very quick reaction before I head down to the 49ers locker room. By the way, this might be the first of three times this season that the 49ers are here in SoFi Stadium. First time being this game, second time when they play the Chargers in December, and yes, the Super Bowl this year is at SoFi. All right, that first drive for Brock Purdy is everything that you want to see from your starting quarterback, and I'm going to hold this right here cuz I know that the PA announcer is super super loud. Brock Purdy had good rapport with De'Shawn Shivers, caught three passes from Purdy. Shivers, I said this on X, the strongest hands of any rookie wide receiver that I've covered, and this is my 10th season covering the 49ers. He did drop a pass from Mac Jones a little bit later, but I don't think that we're worried about De'Shawn Shivers dropping passes. Only had one drop last season at Ole Miss, and that would have been a touchdown today. It's probably just going to help some fantasy owners because they're going to buy a little bit lower on De'Shawn Shivers in their drafts. Also was very impressed today by Sincere McCormick. We talked earlier about the fact that Patrick Taylor Jr. is done for the season, on season-ending injured reserve for the 49ers. Well, that opens up potentially the fifth running back spot for the 49ers, and McCormick, he's only 25 years old, has already been with five teams over the course of his NFL career. Ran hard today. I mean, that was a pinball-like touchdown that he had following the 37-yarder. And you might have noticed on the 37-yarder down the sideline, two really good blocks, one from Brayden Willis, who's filling in at fullback, a tight end playing a different position, that might punch him a 53-man roster spot. He had a great kickout block on that run. And also, a really, really good block from Jordan Watkins, who later caught a touchdown from Adrian Martinez in the second half. Of course, the most electric play of this game, probably the 83-yard punt return for a touchdown from Jacob Cowing, which had to feel good for a player who missed all of last season with a hamstring injury. Now, Jacob has been underwhelming as a receiver. And I think at 5'9", it's just really tough to put him on the outside. Today, there were a couple balls that he couldn't bring in, and I think that his height was a big disadvantage. But if he can show the electricity that the 49ers know he can show, and he did show today as a punt returner, he's probably going to make this roster. I mean, that was a sweet, sweet return where we saw the 4.3 speed on display from Jacob Cowing. And you know, last year, they had Skyy Moore at punt returner, and he only very, very marginally performed for the offense. So, I mean, the 49ers would love if their punt returner could also be a big weapon on offense. I think that might be why Deebo Samuel fielded the first punt in this game, but that position is so important, and the 49ers have not returned a punt for a touchdown in a regular season game since 2011 when Jim Harbaugh was the coach, and Jim Harbaugh was on the other side today. So, I mean, if you can have that type of speed and electricity at punt returner, you don't care if that guy is an offensive contributor. You I mean, you would love if if he were, but but if he's not, and he could field the punts cleanly, arrows up for somebody like Jacob Cowing today. Osa Odighizuwa was one of the bigger names that started for the 49ers today on defense. Stock up. He's good. Where can I buy Osa Odighizuwa stock? When we watch the tape of this game, it's going to be fun. Then the limited action that we saw from Osa, it's going to be fun to watch him wrecking shop. He had like five or six would-be sacks against the Chargers the other day in the joint practice. Now, speaking of Jim Harbaugh, back to SoFi Stadium right here. The 49ers when they put up 41 points, a preseason record in 2013, Jim Harbaugh was their coach. Now Jim Harbaugh is the Chargers coach. Obviously, a lot has changed since 2013 and we saw a lot of Trey Lance today for the Chargers against the 49ers. So everything really came full circle. But I want to talk about the one drive that the Chargers first team offense and Justin Herbert had against the 49ers defensive starters. I don't want to say first team defense because there was no Fred Warner or Nick Bosa. But everything that was a huge issue for the 49ers at the practice on Tuesday, over the three plays that they had, the three-and-out that they registered against the Chargers, they fixed. The first play was O'Marien Hampton, who, you know, ran over Ja'ir Brown and the Chargers had a lot of plays to the edge. They successfully ran to the perimeter in the practice on Tuesday. Pitch right to Marien Hampton. Sam Okwanu set the edge, tripped him up. Jaiden Digger, the rookie with the long, long wingspan, was in there to to clean the play up. They set the edge on first down. On second down, the Chargers found Charlie Kolar, who's one of Brock Purdy's best friends, his tight end at Ohio at Iowa State. I was about to say Ohio State. It's late at night here. Found Charlie Kolar in the flat. Renardo Green made an excellent open field tackle. Set up a third down. Deommodore Lenoir, great coverage on Ladd McConkey. Incompletion from Herbert. That was Justin Herbert's night. And we knew he was only going to play one series. And the 49ers did well to completely stonewall that offense. So, if anything, I mean, it was just a short three plays, but a confidence builder for a 49ers defense that did not play Fred Warner or Nick Bosa today. I could clip this back in here. So, I have a little bit better access of of my screen so I could go through some of the stats and some of the notes about what happened today. Carver Willis made the start at left guard for the 49ers. Played late into the game at left guard. One sneaky option, at least entering this game in that left guard battle, would have been Austin Pleasant who started instead of Trent Williams at left tackle. They shifted Pleasant into left guard, but then it looked like Pleasant got hurt in the second half. So, we're going to have to see how severe his injury is. If he did get severely hurt, or if he's going to be out for a few weeks, you can rule him out as a left guard option. But, the fact that Carver Willis got first team looks today, and Connor Colby was on the right side today. Started on the right side because Dominic Pooney got a rest today. That is That is an arrow up for Carver Willis in that wide-open left guard battle. Also, Renardo Green hurt his hamstring. We don't know how serious that is. But, if Renardo is out for any period of time, it's Jack Jones who's the next man up. And Jack Jones had a nice nice pass breakup today against Keiondre Lambert-Smith in the end zone. Remember Trey Lance threw that ball jump ball. Jack Jones has been good all training camp and preseason for the 49ers. That's the reason why you get that veteran insurance at cornerback. I am going to have to rewatch this game before I pass judgment on Alfred Collins. I know that was one of the the big things that I wanted to track in this game. Did he hold up a little bit better against the run? Well, we shall see. I know that first down play was good for the 49ers defense. They only saw three plays from the Chargers starters. Adrian Martinez, good for him. I know he did throw a pick-six, but he also did run for a touchdown and throw a touchdown pass. Remember, he was born in Hanford. Shout out to the 559, and Adrian Martinez played football at Clovis West High School in the Fresno area. So, he scored a touchdown and he threw for a touchdown in a San Francisco 49ers uniform, which is, I think, a a cool story. Somebody who's probably going to end up on the 49ers practice squad. Jordan Watkins today, he caught that touchdown on the little post from Adrian Martinez. He made six catches last week. I think Watkins is a lock for this roster, but one area where I'd love to see him improve, some of those contested catches over the middle. I mean, he's a he's a really good route runner. He's got a lot of speed, but again, he had one over the middle uh from Mac Jones, where it probably should have been a flag, but Rodney Shelby was able to break it up. Watkins just wasn't able to hold on to the football. Those are the types of plays that he's got to start making if the 49ers want him to firmly grab that Z wide receiver position, and by extension, allow Deebo Samuel to be this all-around gadget weapon, which is what I think would allow the 49ers to most effectively replace Ricky Pearsall. But the good news is that they got De'Shawn Shivers. He was lining up everywhere. Inside receiver, outside receiver. Purdy had confidence going to him on some of those quick slants. Mac Jones had confidence going to him on the on the deeper little seam post crossing the field. That was the big gainer to Shivers. He had confidence going to him on the move that got him behind the defense. Unfortunately, he dropped that one pass, but De'Shawn, I think, looks the part, looks fantastic. He might have missed one run block. Kyle Shanahan will probably tell us if if he shares my opinion. But, you know what? Uh I think he's getting used to blocking at this level, and he's definitely has gotten used to to running routes and catching the ball at this level. One more little look at at SoFi Stadium for you guys emptying out. Maybe the first of three trips for the 49ers here this season. I thought that Nick Martin today, the 49ers linebacker, he was playing late in the game, which sometimes isn't a good sign in these preseason games for players roster chances, and I know I've talked about the fact that Nick Martin isn't quite, you know, doesn't have like the wingspan that Jayden Duggar has, and we saw Duggar in coverage on a tight end. I mean, you could make up for a lot of missteps and mistakes with a 7-ft wingspan. Martin doesn't have that, but he still flies around like a missile, and even if Raheem Morris, who you know, it's very unpredictable what he's going to want as a defensive coordinator, if he's not interested in Nick Martin, and he might be, well, we'll see at cutdown day. Brent Boyer, the special teams coordinator, has got to be really, really interested in this guy because he flies around, he forced a fumble that Marquis Siegel picked up today. I mean, he runs a sub-4.5 and is a ball of muscle, kind of like Kaylon Black, who was awesome for the 49ers over a short period of time. I know I already talked a lot about Kaylon over the course of the past couple days coming off the practice. Today we got to see Kaylon, the running back, for the first time with live tackling. Because you can't bring guys to the ground in practice, and you know, the reason I was so excited to see Kaylon is because he is he's Zeus. Zeus, you know, we could we could flex here for for for Kaylon Black. Zeus was loose today. title: Darius Slay describes what it was like playing with Jalen Hurts, shares 'welcome to NFL' moment
text: It's our pleasure now to be joined by one of our newest team members here at CBS Sports. Darius Slay, great to be with you, pal. >> Great, thanks. >> Uh big play Slay, we're going to ask you about some of those plays in a moment, but first it's been quite some time since you approached something as a rookie. Is there anything you're drawing upon in your in your career, in your experience in football as you approach this new opportunity? >> Uh I'm I'm just looking forward to something new. Uh it's it's fun, it's exciting. Uh I'm new on this journey, crossing over to the other side, so I hear nothing but great things about it, so I'm just looking uh forward to uh know, experiencing this new end journey of mine. >> What about it excites you the most? When you look at maybe taking all of your knowledge that you acquired over these years and and giving it to the masses in an entertaining way. What are you What are you looking to to bring to NFL Today block? >> I'm looking forward to like basically I know, sharing my stor- stories. You know, I got a lot of stories from football. Very outgoing, very laughing. Some stories I can't share uh share in a NFL way because you know, you want to be perf- professional, but it's still professional on this side in a good way. So, I'm looking forward to like sharing my story, giving my thoughts uh on how the game was and through my lens and uh and have fun with doing it cuz everybody kind of see my football might be up tight. I was a guy that I played the game and had a lot of fun, was laughing every play. Uh I took football serious, but I actually truly had fun playing the game. A lot of guys take it that serious as in like they treat it as a job, which it is a job, but I think a guy like me, I had to love my job to do it at a excellent level, so and uh I just want to get that perspective of a different view than some guys that be like like uh who I can say? A Brian Dawkins, say he want to take souls. Not me. I'm just trying to have fun and get compete. You know what I'm saying? So, stuff like that. So, uh it's a it's another different perspective of the game. >> Along the line of successful defensive back play that you know, you said you got a lot of stories and just a moment ago our guy Nate Burleson whispers in my ear, "Ask him about the story, practice number one in Detroit. You called out Megatron?" >> Yeah, yeah. >> Take me through this. >> So, uh I got drafted to Detroit as well, as you know, um um I was just chilling and then um I just felt a little little up, you know, so I went against Nate first, you know, so me and Nate was going at it. Then uh me and he I made a couple of plays on him, he made a couple of plays on me. And then I said, "Man, come on, come on, Calvin. Come on, come on out here." And uh I learned quickly not to call him out, you know what I'm saying? I learned quickly [laughter] not to do that. Uh that whole rookie year, I lost every battle. So, um I waited till my first time actually making a play on Calvin was my second year in the league. And and like a real competitive play like I actually made it. Uh but um other than that, man, y'all learn my lesson quick, but without Calvin, man, I wouldn't be who I am today. Man, he helped me become a great player, man, understanding how to play this game, and he helped me in every way. >> So, that's when people ask, "What's your welcome to the NFL moment?" It's like every practice that Calvin was looking at you. >> Every practice it was a welcome to a moment. Calvin was mossing me every day. >> Uh trial by fire and learning through experience there. It has led to some of the biggest plays and the biggest moments that we've seen in recent memory. You don't get the name big play Slay >> Right. >> uh with no plays behind us. Take us through your top three plays when I ask you, your favorite plays you made in your career, where does your head go? >> My favorite play is basically um my favorite favorite is the Eagles the Eagles. >> Okay. >> Uh Thanksgiving Day, I played against the Eagles. It was Carson Wentz's first pick he threw against to me as a rookie, I think. And um I had made back-to-back plays. I had made a forced fumble on Matthews. Uh we got the ball back, kicked the field goal. >> Mhm. >> And the next play of that next possession after we kicked the field goal, I caught a pick to end the game. I won a defensive player of the the defensive player of the week that week, and um it was fun. That's one of my most experienced and fun games I ever played in, one of my biggest moments. Uh I enjoyed that one, man. I ain't going to lie, even though it was against my former Eagles. Uh I had a good That's one of my best games, though. And my second one would be my first pick-six. That was against Arizona, man, to get in the end zone to get in the end zone for the first time as a as a defensive player. >> Would you >> that one off? >> Uh the rook, the rook. Who they drafted with number the 10th overall? Rosen? >> Yeah. >> Yeah, Rosen. Yeah, Rosen. So, yeah, I got my first pick-six. I loved it. And then after that, I started getting interceptions a lot more than after that. So, >> [laughter] >> He got a taste for >> He got a taste for it. It felt pretty good. So, I I I loved that part about that game. And my third one was my first career playoff pick. And I got that 2 years ago after we just won a Super Bowl against Green Bay. Thank you, Jordan Love. And um so, those are my best plays I had all through my career. >> I I want to go right there. That last run with the Philadelphia Eagles ending with that Super Bowl title. You you realize this childhood dream and and you get to experience it. I remember seeing you we had our cameras out running around after that and just the joy that was coming out of you in that moment. Can you can you take me into Philadelphia right now cuz you still know a lot of guys in that room. But there are some moving parts. We're hearing that it might be Lane's last go. Jeff Stoutland no longer there. It starts inside and it goes outside. One thing I know about Vic, he's going to have that defense ready to go. I think he's one of the best things that happened to that building besides, you know, a lot of great players that come through there. Vic is a great dude. We're saying he's not capable of doing it, but since he's been in the league, it's always been gun, you know, handing the ball off, whatever. Uh he's a guy you know he he lets his emotions show. Uh he's a great leader, a great guy that just lead by example, but uh behind closed doors man he got a lot of profanity. >> He got a lot of profanity, but well it's worth it though cuz you know as a leader he we need some of us need that energy and he and he goes hard and uh he got to respect his game, got to respect how he approach the game. He put the team first. >> So uh it's a great thing for him. I think they got a great leader always been. I told him that as a rookie I said this is going to be your team sooner or later because how he carried himself. So it just good to see that he's progressing and becoming a better player each and every year and I'm you know I'm happy to always been a part of it cuz you know we we had made a lot of great history together. So I'm looking forward to them to continue to keep leading the way, you know, hopefully bring another Super Bowl to the team. >> that his best football comes out in the biggest moments in those Super Bowls on the right side and the wrong side. He's been a fantastic uh leader and quarterback in those moments and it feels like everybody just keeps putting that chip right back on his shoulder. I think the uh I think the Giants got a a good chance to try to like to knock on the Eagles door for sure because of the the adjustments they're making. I think the quarterback Darnold is pretty good and I think the defense on that side cuz my defense my defensive coach is over there right now. So he's the D-coordinator. So I think they're going to do a great job over there on the defensive side. So I think they they got a good chance of coming from from last to first. >> Worst to first, the New York Football Giants. Keep an eye on it. That's Big Play Slay here with us here on CBS Sports. Thank you, Darius. 18

title: Antonio Pierce talks Raiders' QB situation, debates David Tyree & Santonio Holmes Super Bowl catches

You know they're going to put up points. But the problem last year was what? The defense. >> Yes. >> Can they Can they stop these guys? Can they stop the other teams in that division, right? Can they finally dethrone the Philadelphia Eagles? Is Jayden Daniels and the Commanders that brick offense that they present to the Dallas Cowboys? So I'm really interested to see what happens down in Dallas, right? How does Dak Prescott, some off the, you know, some off the field stuff that they talked about personally. But let's talk to the field. Can he Can he go back to that guy that we saw that was playing at a very high level before the injury? With two elite receivers. The running game might be the only question mark I have, but I think other than that, this is a team that can score, but the pressure is on the Cowboys to win. >> Yeah, and you're talking about the Cowboys who currently play in the NFC East. title: Matt Campbell Is Ready To Lead Penn State Into A New Era | Full Interview
text: Huge move happened up in State College, Pennsylvania last season. Obviously, they move on from James Franklin after like week five. Game Day had been there 3 weeks beforehand, and then there's a massive turnover. Who's going to be their head coach? Who are they going to land? Do they have no plan? What the hell? Then they land maybe the coaching hire of the entire off-season. Ladies and gentlemen, formerly of Iowa State, now the head coach of the Penn State Nittany Lions, we can't thank him enough for joining us. All the fam, coach, ladies and gentlemen, Matt Campbell. >> Yeah, coach. >> How you doing? >> Thanks for having me, you guys. I appreciate it. >> Dude, thank you for joining us. I I think you caught the tail end there of Pete Thamel talking about the chaos right now happening and all the injunctions. How much do you got to pay attention to that type of stuff? I assume it does affect everybody, especially at the highest level. Is this something you pay attention to every day? Do you have somebody looking into this? How do you kind of view all the off-the-field chaos that's currently happening? >> Yeah, you know, Pat, I still think we we live in a world where if you start to worry about all the craziness that's going on under around us, then I think you can really quickly lose sight of what's going on in your own building and you know, I I it's a unique time, it's a crazy time, but I think when you lose focus of the 18 to 22, 23-year-olds that you're in charge of, then I think you can really lose focus of your team fast. So, we've really tried to concentrate on everything here in house, um worry about ourselves. I still think it's about creating team, and the best team still wins on Saturdays, and I think that's got to be the focus in house, and that's really what we've tried to put our focus on. >> Yeah, and I think your answer right there is why a lot of NFL teams wanted your services. >> And obviously, you had been with Iowa State for a very long time. We just had Brock Purdy on. He obviously thanked you for your service at Iowa State. You going to Penn State, the natural reaction from a lot of people is, man, what he was able to do at Iowa State, now he's going to have the backing of Penn State, which has one of the best, I think, sports support systems in all of sport. I think we've learned that through not only going up there, but also watching what they've done. Number one hockey player, basketball, volleyball, you you it, they're going all in. Football will do a $700 million upgrade to Beaver Stadium over the weekend. It's like they are all in on sports. So, the thought of you having everything that Penn State has to offer, the brand Penn State as a whole, what does that do for you? Are we blowing that out of proportion that, you know, going to Penn State is a massive, massive opportunity for you to take advantage of what some other schools have been able to do? And how do you view that as a whole? >> Well, I I I think in a couple ways, Pat. I I And I think you, me, AJ can at least understand growing up in this man, 4 to 6-hour radius of this area what this the history of Penn State football has meant to the world of college football. And I think before anything else in terms of revenue and all the stuff that happens you're in a place where the high school football, 6 to 8 hours around our campus it's as good as anywhere in the country. And the opportunity to be around a program and be a part of a program that can give a young man 18 to 22 years old the opportunity to chase every goal and dream, not only on the on the field of football, but off the field because of the leadership, because of the commitment, and really because of those that came before us ever that stepped on the field and made a really important to play the game of football at Penn State. It's a really special opportunity and it would have taken that it had to take be the right opportunity for me to leave what we were able what we were able to accomplish and what we did at Iowa State and we really felt like the value system in this community in the the state of Pennsylvania, in the 6-hour radius around us, man, that that fit who I was, our family, and really our coaching staff. And we're really grateful to be here. >> I love to hear that, and I think everybody's very excited for you. And it feels like it wasn't a messy exit, either, which is normally how it normally goes. And I think that's because of how you've handled it all, and obviously how Iowa State has handled it all. And also, you have an athletic director over there who's worn a cowboy collar in big 10 football. So, I I don't know how many other places have that. AJ has a question for you, Matt. >> Yeah, coach, obviously I know you've been you know, on the grind in camp working day-to-day for that, but have you given any thought to what it's going to feel like running out of that tunnel for the first time leading your Penn State squad out on that gigantic stadium? Obviously, you have players, it'll be some of their first time as well, but you as a coach, I guess how do you control your emotions in that situation? >> Yeah, and you know, I I think it just goes back to what I said earlier, AJ. You know, number one is I think you're so caught up in the present right now. You know, the the unique challenge that we're under of creating a team and creating a team that's ready to respond to real adversity by the time, man, two two less than two weeks come at us. But, I do I would be remiss not to say, man, 10:30, 11:00 every night and you look at this expansion and the lights on in this stadium and there's not even a couple nights where you're kind of like, man, I you kind of sneak into the stadium and you walk around and you say, look look at this place and look how special it is to play in one of the one of the great, you know, the great places to play college football and we're really fortunate to do it. I'm excited for the opportunity, but I'm more excited to give our fan base in this university a team that can represent the history of this place the right way. >> Obviously, you sound like a guy that doesn't need an alarm clock, what what is the morning routine for you and is the alarm clock a whoa? Is that the uh >> It need It It does need to be that bad. I don't need an alarm clock, but I will take that and and we'll we'll make sure that's on repeat here for a long time. >> See that? Here we go. Now, we're getting ready. You talk about being one of the best place to play all of college sport. So, it's pretty bittersweet finding out you were going to Penn State and I was probably going to be seeing you every year anyway. But, congratulations nonetheless. How important was it for you, you know, bringing Taylor Mauk with you and some of your support staff and obviously Rocco, not only for, you know, the the continuity that you're going to have, but kind of being able to immediately build your culture right away, right when you got there? >> Yeah. I >> [laughter] >> I'm a huge Kirk Ferentz fan. I love I have great respect for him. So, we have that in common, but I I hopefully we can get you on our side a little bit moving forward. But, you know, I I would say the continuity piece You win with people. You know, it's it's why you guys have had so much success. It's why we haven't been able to have so much success in our past. It's because we have had great people in every corner from academics, nutrition, strength and conditioning, life after football to our our great coaches that have been great developers of our players to our players. And I think the uniqueness of college football today, in a lot of ways we were able to pick up our program and some of the nuts and bolts of what made our program special and just move it over to where we are right here at Penn State and so I think to have Taylor Moyer, to have so many of those pieces to come in and that were great pieces of the development of our players at Iowa State which is we had to be better than anybody in that just to even compete. To have so many of those staff members come with us, that was really big and and then, you know, to to not say, man, to have Rocco here. I mean, what he means, we've been developing an offense for the last four years around him. And to be able to watch his growth process and even what he had to fight through last year, some really tough injuries and how that guy played at the finish of the season through the injuries he had, I think shows everything about what makes that guy really special. I think those were huge advantages for us and I think it'll give us a great opportunity to build the right foundation um as we get ready for the for the season. >> Rocco Becton of West Virginia legend Anthony Bect, obviously. Like to have a little West Virginia tie to any school if they want to have success. You know that, Coach Campbell. Um last question for me and for us is we appreciate your time here today on this college football showcase. You wear a whistle all the time? We got a whistle around the neck all the time everywhere we go? >> Not not all the time, but we do have a walk-through here in about in about a half hour. So I'm ready to rock and roll. >> I like that. What are you soft whistle, double whistle? What is your normal >> Oh, no, I'm I'm old school whistle. Not not one of these new ones that all these these young guys got. I'm old school. >> Can't get a lot of spit in those ones though. Those ones get a little excited. They do get caught you know, you don't need that. I know you're not doing that. That's why they brought you in. We don't need any in the middle of practice. People think you're going to lose every game. That is not what you do. You're a winner, man. That's why Penn State got very lucky that they hired you and I'm sure they're appreciative just like you are and we appreciate you, man. Have a good one. Good luck out there. >> All right, guys. Thanks so much for having me. Really appreciate it. >> Ladies and gentlemen, the head coach of Penn State, Matt Campbell. >> [snorts] >> The worst. >> Need a Fox the Fox 40 whistle. That's the best. >> That's why not that it's got the little hood on it. >> It's a good one at the I don't know if it's got a hood on it. It's the one that the most NFL refs use, yeah. >> [music]

title: Will Howard, Drew Allar STRUGGLE, OL woes, Elandon Roberts wows, KJ's chance | Steelers Rewind
text: What is going on everybody? Welcome back to Steelers Rewind here on pennlive.com. The Pittsburgh Steelers shut out 17 to nothing here in their second preseason game against the New York Jets. A game where the two young quarterbacks, Will Howard and Drew Allar, were the big talking points and they remain the big talking points. Not necessarily cuz of things you wanted. Will Howard throwing two interceptions. Drew Allar not being able to lead a touchdown drive. To not throw away a pick. And I think these are two separate things. So, let's talk about it. Will Howard had a few drives where he was actually able to get this offense rolling a little bit. They were able to move down the field. They were able to actually get a rhythm at some points. But two turnovers in Jets territory and a costly sack dropped them out. Um I I think Will Howard with pocket movement was very inconsistent today. There were a few ones There was one play he slid up and hit straight up and I was like, yes, there's that. And then, you know, on the Broderick Jones sack, Broderick gets beat by David Bailey very badly. But I also would have liked to have seen Will Howard step up into the pocket. You know, it's not a good habit, right? We talk about process versus results. Now, I would say the result was a sack, but it's bad process to try and go back and out that side. Um you know, if you are not a special athlete, you probably don't want to be doing that. Will Howard certainly is a solid athlete, but not a special athlete for the football uh for the quarterback position. So, you know, that's one thing I would like to see corrected. I think the inconsistencies there. I think It's not the picks. I mean, he doesn't see Roman Wilson on the uh he doesn't see Andre Cisco on the first one to Roman Wilson. Both of these to Roman Wilson. The second one, not a great throw. I also don't think Roman Wilson ran these routes as crisp as he could have. These crossers drifting upfield um a little bit. And so, I think there's two things here. Will Howard certainly not identifying the coverage and kind of throwing these balls either behind Roman Wilson or not great spots, and then Roman Wilson not having the detail and the the clean route concepts that he needed to, you know, not separating at the top of routes. So, I thought Roman Wilson also is part of that discussion. I thought this offensive line didn't look very good. Broderick Jones had a really rough night. I didn't think Brock Hoffman played very well. I actually think Troy, Mason McCormick, and Zach Frazier looked fine. Dylan Cook, I think was much better than Broderick Jones, but I don't think it was like some just stamp of where oh, Dylan Cook was so good. This offensive line did not get much movement in the run game. They allowed too many free runners. They got beat on one-on-ones, and I understand it's a very big schematic change. When we talked about Arthur Smith's scheme, you know, there was a lot of vertical sets, a lot of help. And now it's like a lot of actual deep drops. It's a lot of one-on-ones through pass sets. And so, it's a it's a change, and and the techniques change. So, you're seeing some of these guys have to kind of adjust themselves, but still, what a rough day for the offensive line. And I thought that was a story for Drew Allar was the offensive line had him under duress. I think, you know, some points, you know, he had self-admitted maybe he could have gotten rid of the ball. I thought there were a few dump balls he missed. I didn't think it was like super clean for Drew Allar from a processing standpoint today. I thought that did stand out as one thing I would like to see from Drew Allar more. I thought he you know, last week he played quick, played snappy, he played on time. I think he was thrown off at some points. I did like the off the off-platform stuff. I like the out-of-structure. I thought the great throw down the sideline to Liam Clifford was a great throw. And I thought Clifford made a really nice catch. He also had a lot of drops from his receiving core in this game. I thought that was something else that really just stuck out, right? You think about the two seam balls dropped on that that last two-minute drill. I I thought there were more than just that drop as well where it was like, "Dude, what is going on here?" So, I don't think the receivers did him any help. I don't think he had much of a run game. I don't think the O-line played very well. I will need to watch more, you know, all-22 to kind of truly evaluate uh both these guys' performances, but this is just kind of my snap-off-the-bone uh takeaways. I thought, you know, on positives, I thought defensively, I thought Elandon Roberts looked phenomenal. I mean, the the three plays of that four on that one drive where he destroys a puller, comes in on third down destroys the A-gap allowing Cole Holcomb to shoot through for the TFL, and then makes a great play in space on the wheel route to tackle that running back short and getting the turnover and down. So, that's E-Rob through and through. No rust to knock off. He's here and he's ready. Uh he is a much added bonus to the Pittsburgh Steelers' inside linebacker room. And then I think Rashaan Jenkins, you know, made a few really nice plays. I thought Robert Spillane Jennings also did. He had a really nice stick on about a 5-yard curl. He had me he uh forced a block in the back. He's a gunner on punt. I thought that was really good. I don't think Kaden Weisman looked very good today as a punt returner. Um had a fumble that luckily for him the the the recovery did not get his second foot in bounds. So, it wasn't all that great, but I didn't think the special teams were all that good today either. Missed a kick. Um Nick Folk did. So, a lot of things uh Caleb Johnson played more this week. I I I he he ran hard and he ran hard between the tackles. title: Will Howard, Drew Allar’s BIG CHANCE, safety room depth, Roman Wilson’s next test | Steelers Preview
text: What's going on everybody? Welcome back to a Steelers preview here on pennlive.com. Nick Farabaugh here with you all. It's very sunny out today. Pittsburgh Steelers will take on the New York Jets in about 5 hours here. As I'm recording this, the Steelers certainly appear to be ready to kind of have a youth movement tonight. You look at Will Howard playing Drew Allar. That's obviously going to be the focus of tonight. Seeing these two young quarterbacks and what you want to see out of them. I mean, I think we want to see continued growth from both these guys. For Will Howard, it's dealing with stuff under pressure. The process of going through an entire football game, an entire half where you have four or five drives is a little different than you know he had three. It was kind of stunted. Stunted, he came in in the middle of it. Now, he had a full week to kind of prepare to start mentally. He prepared himself for that. He's going to probably face most of the Jets starters. He's probably going to be out there with a lot of the starting O-line. It's going to be a good barometer to see where Will Howard is. But, I want to see the easy stuff look easy. I want to see him deal with pressure. Well, I want to see that pocket movement we saw on the seam ball to Robert Tonyan. I want to see him continue to flash that accuracy up the numbers and in between the numbers. I think those things are really important for him. And, I want to see a general command of the offense. I think that's a big thing for him. For Drew Allar, it's really I want to see the easy continue to look easy. I want to see him continue to play really fast. I thought mentally you watched how he played against the Green Bay Packers. And, it was really quick. Every decision was dialed in. He looked like he trusted his himself. Trusted his eyes. And, he threw with the anticipation, which I thought was really important. Want to continue to see that. Will we see a wild throw down the field? We could. I think those are all on his tape, on his resume. But, I want to continue to see the easy look easy. So, that'll be something to keep an eye on. I think we're going to see a lot of those injured players out. We may not see a guy like Jennings Dunker, a guy like Baylen Everett, which I think is a little bit of a bummer because you are going to see the Jets starters. Um so, you know, I think this is a big game for a guy like Asante Samuel Jr. to continue to continue to build on his strong summer. Um it's it's nice to see the safety room step up, right? I want to continue to see Robert Spears Jennings make plays because that safety room I think is going to have a crunch, especially as we continue to talk about, you know, these positions around the team including quarterback where if they keep four, something's got to be a roster crunch. With Jaylen Ramsey's versatility, is it only three true safeties plus Ramsey's the four? You know, Jennings and guys like Raheem Shaver and Sebastian Castro and all these other guys are competing for that spot. And so, I continue to look at it um and say could the Pittsburgh Steelers actually end up keeping the young guy or are they going to keep the veteran or can they keep both? How hard is that safety room construction going to be because you have two obvious starters in Brisker and Elliott. You have Ramsey who can do both but is going to be your starting slot. Who's going to be the other guy? Is there going to be one or two of them? I think it's a real question. So, that safety room is one I'm watching today. We're going to see Lane Roberts again. I think it'll be fun to see him flutter around against the New York Jets. But really tonight, it's all about the young players. It's all about seeing guys like Jeremy Bernard, seeing guys like Roman Wilson. I think Roman Wilson needs a nice game today. Probably going to get more time in the slot than he did last time. So, I think you're going to see a splash year game from 14. Um but I think these young guys are going to be big, you know, big game for Caleb Johnson. Can he get more than just five stats? Mike McDonald seemed to hint that he would. Um and if he can do that, then certainly we are going to have a lot of evaluating of 20 to do, especially because there's so many moving parts. There seems like Travis Homer is a roster lock at this point. Um so, lots of things to watch in this game, but it's all about those young QBs and evaluating Will Howard and Jaquan Brisker. I want to continue to see them play fast. I want to see the accuracy flash. Little bit of different things for both of those guys overall. But you want to continue to see the progression of Will Howard and Drew Aller. All right everybody, make sure to like, comment, subscribe, turn on the notification bell for more and thanks for watching.
